objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_conn_t h2o_conn_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for the base HTTP connection type. The complete definition appears later as struct st_h2o_conn_t. Pointers to this are passed throughout the API to represent a client connection.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_context_t h2o_context_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for the server context; fully defined later as struct st_h2o_context_t. Encapsulates event loop, global config, caches, stats, and per-thread resources.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_req_t h2o_req_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for an HTTP request; fully defined later as struct st_h2o_req_t. Represents one HTTP request / response lifecycle including headers, body, filters, timers, and state.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_ostream_t h2o_ostream_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for an output stream filter node; fully defined later. Filters form a chain to transform response output.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_configurator_command_t h2o_configurator_command_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a configurator command structure. Not defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_configurator_t h2o_configurator_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a configurator object. Not defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_pathconf_t h2o_pathconf_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration for per-path configuration; fully defined later. Holds handlers, filters, loggers, mimemap, and env settings.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_hostconf_t h2o_hostconf_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration for per-host configuration; fully defined later. Holds authority settings, path list, fallback, mimemap, and HTTP/2 options.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_globalconf_t h2o_globalconf_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration for global configuration; fully defined later. Aggregates hosts, defaults, timeouts, proxy settings, mimemap, status hooks, etc.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_mimemap_t h2o_mimemap_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration of MIME mapping registry. Not defined here; operations are provided via functions in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_logconf_t h2o_logconf_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration of compiled log configuration. Not defined in this header; managed via compile/dispose functions.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_headers_command_t h2o_headers_command_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration for header rewrite commands; later defined as struct st_h2o_headers_command_t entries forming a list of commands.
Base type for request handlers that can generate responses. Instances are attached to path configurations; they may stream request bodies, handle Expect, and have per-context init/dispose hooks.
Base type for response filters that can insert ostream nodes and observe informational responses. Registered per path and initialized per context.
Base type for access loggers. Registered per path with per-context lifecycle and a log_access callback.
Cached stringified timestamp forms used in responses and logs. Managed by context timestamp cache.
Timestamp object with timeval and shared cached string representations. Obtained via h2o_get_timestamp.
Configuration for HTTP/2 server push casper (cache digest) settings: capacity and whether to track all asset types.
Environment variable configuration applied to requests. Supports inheritance via parent and lists of names to set / unset.
Per-path configuration: path string, handlers, filters, loggers, mimemap, environment overrides, and error logging behavior.
Per-host configuration: authority fields, strict matching, path list, fallback path, mimemap, and HTTP/2 server-push settings.
Descriptor for an extra status endpoint: name, final renderer, optional init and per-thread setup. Instances are registered into global config.

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(h2o_status_handler_t *) h2o_status_callbacks_t;
objects.description: Vector of pointers to status handlers kept in the global configuration.
Policy for emitting HTTP 1xx responses to clients.
Control of zero-copy proxying behavior, including forcing pipe-backed vectors even if protocol handler lacks support.
How proxy handles Expect: 100-continue headers and interim responses.
Global server configuration: hosts, naming, limits, per-protocol timeouts and limits, proxy defaults, informational mode, mimemap, filecache, and status callbacks.
Per-mime-type attributes like compressibility and relative priority for scheduling.
Entry in a mimemap. Either a static mimetype with attributes, or a dynamic type that embeds a pathconf for extension-based handlers.
Slot in per-context storage with an optional disposer for stored pointer.

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(h2o_context_storage_item_t) h2o_context_storage_t;
objects.description: Vector of storage items kept in h2o_context_t for module-private per-thread data.
State of a connection used for accounting and shutdown handling.

Execution context (often per thread): contains loop pointer, queues, caches, per-protocol counters, proxy client/conn pool, SSL and QUIC stats, storage, timestamp cache, and connection tracking lists.
Generator interface used by handlers to produce response bodies asynchronously and to stop on abort.
Node in the response output stream chain. Filters implement do_send to transform data and forward to the next link, and stop to abort.
Response metadata and header/trailer sets, with optional MIME attributes and a snapshot of original headers prior to filter rewriting.
Structure returned by debug callbacks to expose HTTP/2 connection state for diagnostics.
Virtual function table for connection-specific operations, push, tracing, RTT, zero-copy capability, request iteration, and structured logging fields.
Base connection object shared by protocol implementations. Holds context, host set, connection time, ID, callbacks, UUID cache, state, and linkage for context connection lists.
Per-request prefilter chain to intercept and set up ostream filters prior to normal filter chain.
Per-request overrides for proxying behavior: client context, pool, upstream URL, location header rewrite, Expect handling, proxy protocol, host preservation, and header rewrites.
Extra fields for extension-based dynamic content: script name, path info, and local filesystem path.

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_write_req_cb)(void *ctx, int is_end_stream);
objects.description: Callback prototype for protocol handler to submit request body chunks to a streaming handler.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_proceed_req_cb)(h2o_req_t *req, const char *errstr);
objects.description: Callback prototype invoked by handler to signal readiness for next body chunk or an error.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_forward_datagram_cb)(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_iovec_t *datagrams, size_t num_datagrams);
objects.description: Callback prototype for forwarding HTTP/3 datagrams at RFC 9297 layer.

The central per-request object containing input request line/headers, routing (host/path), active filters/loggers, normalized paths, env, overrides, state flags, proxy stats, response structure, streaming callbacks, datagram hooks, and a per-request memory pool.
Accept-time context holding target h2o_context, host list, TLS context, optional HTTP/2 origin frame, proxy-protocol expectation, and memcached ticket receiver.
Compression/decompression stream context with transform callback and optional push buffer. Implementations provided for gzip, gunzip, and brotli.
Parameters for compression filter: minimum size and codec qualities (negative to disable).
Mapping from status codes to error document URLs used by errordoc filter.
Arguments to Expires/Cache-Control filter: absolute expiry string or max-age seconds, and mode selector.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_fastcgi_handler_t h2o_fastcgi_handler_t;
objects.description: Opaque fastcgi handler instance. Created by register functions; definition is in the FastCGI module source.
Configuration for FastCGI handler including timeouts, document root, delegation behavior, and a custom dispose callback payload.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_file_handler_t h2o_file_handler_t;
objects.description: Opaque handler serving static files or directories. Created by h2o_file_register; definition resides in file module.
Specifies when a header rewrite command applies: while sending final headers, informational/early, or both.
Single argument to a header command: header name (possibly a token) and value.
A header rewrite command: operation code, argument array, count, and when to apply. Chains of these are registered per-path.
Configuration for reverse proxy and CONNECT handlers including timeouts, Happy Eyeballs delays, Expect handling, host/proxy protocol flags, header rewrites, buffering, and HTTP/2 options.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_redirect_handler_t h2o_redirect_handler_t;
objects.description: Opaque redirect handler created by h2o_redirect_register; definition is module-internal.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_reproxy_handler_t h2o_reproxy_handler_t;
objects.description: Opaque reproxy filter handler. Registered via h2o_reproxy_register.
Access-control entry for CONNECT/CONNECT-UDP targets, covering allow/deny, address family and mask, and optional port restriction.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_access_log_filehandle_t h2o_access_log_filehandle_t;
objects.description: Opaque file handle / writer for access logs, created by h2o_access_log_open_handle.

Absolute priority descriptor holding an urgency level (0..7) and an incremental flag. Used to represent HTTP absolute priority signals (e.g., as defined by Extensible Prioritization). The bitfields pack into a byte: 3-bit urgency and 1-bit incremental. Other bits are unspecified/unused.

Opaque-ish balancer handle that holds a pointer to a callbacks vtable controlling selection and destruction behavior. Instances are created by factory functions (e.g., round-robin or least-connections). Details beyond the callbacks field are not exposed in this header.
Vtable-like struct of function pointers used by a balancer: a selector deciding which target to use and a destroy function to clean up a balancer instance.

objects.definition: typedef size_t (*h2o_balancer_selector)(h2o_balancer_t *balancer, h2o_socketpool_target_vector_t *targets, char *tried);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a selection callback. Given a balancer, a vector of socketpool targets, and a bitmap/array indicating which have been tried, returns the index (size_t) of the chosen target. Exact semantics of tried come from the broader socketpool API and are not documented here.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_balancer_destroyer)(h2o_balancer_t *balancer);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a destructor callback invoked to destroy a balancer instance.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_cache_t h2o_cache_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a cache instance. The structure is forward-declared only in this header; its layout is private to the implementation. It represents an in-memory cache with capacity- and time-based eviction, optional multithreading protection, and optional early-update behavior.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t /* eq. khint_t */ h2o_cache_hashcode_t;
objects.description: Hash code type used by the cache for keys. It is a 32-bit unsigned integer, compatible with khash's khint_t. Used for passing precomputed key hashes to avoid recomputation.
Concrete key object combining the key bytes (vec) and its precomputed hash. Useful for callers that manage keys and hashes together. h2o_iovec_t is an external type representing a byte span.

Reference object representing a cached entry returned by h2o_cache_fetch. It includes key, hash, timestamp, value, and internal fields for LRU and age lists and reference counting. Callers should treat fields as read-only and must release using h2o_cache_release when done. Internal fields (prefixed with underscore) are implementation details.
Enumeration of cache status values used as the return type of lookup functions. Represents unknown, not cached, fresh, and stale states of a resource in cache digests.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_cache_digests_frame_t h2o_cache_digests_frame_t;
objects.description: Opaque/incomplete struct representing a single cache-digest frame. The actual structure is defined elsewhere; only pointers are usable here.

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(h2o_cache_digests_frame_t) h2o_cache_digests_frame_vector_t;
objects.description: Vector type of h2o_cache_digests_frame_t elements, expanded from the H2O_VECTOR macro defined in h2o/memory.h. Exact layout depends on the macro; here it is treated as an opaque container for frames.

Top-level cache digests object that maintains fresh digests in two vectors: one keyed by URL only and another by URL+ETag. The 'complete' flag indicates whether the fresh digest set is complete. Lifecycle is managed with h2o_cache_digests_load_header (constructor/loader) and h2o_cache_digests_destroy (destructor).

Configuration context object passed through configurator callbacks, holding pointers to the active global, host, and path configurations, plus mimemap and environment. Also indicates dry-run mode and links to a parent context for hierarchical configuration processing.
Represents a single configuration directive handled by a configurator: its owning configurator, name, flags, and handler callback.
Base configurator object that owns and manages a set of configuration commands and lifecycle callbacks (dispose, enter, exit).

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_configurator_dispose_cb)(h2o_configurator_t *configurator);
objects.description: Function pointer type for an optional callback invoked when the global configuration is being disposed for a configurator.

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_configurator_enter_cb)(h2o_configurator_t *configurator, h2o_configurator_context_t *ctx, yoml_t *node);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback executed before configuration commands are handled, given the configurator, context, and current YOML node.

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_configurator_exit_cb)(h2o_configurator_t *configurator, h2o_configurator_context_t *ctx, yoml_t *node);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback executed after configuration commands are handled for a given context and node.

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_configurator_command_cb)(h2o_configurator_command_t *cmd, h2o_configurator_context_t *ctx, yoml_t *node);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the handler of a specific configuration command (directive).

objects.definition: typedef h2o_headers_command_t **(*h2o_configurator_get_headers_commands_cb)(h2o_configurator_t *conf);
objects.description: Function pointer type returning a pointer to an array (or vector) of header commands associated with a configurator. Exact ownership and lifetime are not specified here.

Opaque or externally-defined vector-of-bytes/string slice type used by the h2o APIs. It is referenced as the return type of h2o_file_read but is not defined in this header. Since it is not defined here, details such as fields, lifetime, and ownership semantics are unknown from this file. Likely defined in h2o/memory.h.

Reference object representing an entry in the file cache, holding an open file descriptor or an open error, file metadata (stat), cached Last-Modified time (tm and RFC1123 string), cached ETag buffer and length, an LRU link node, a reference count, and a flexible array path buffer. Intended to be managed via h2o_filecache_open_file/close_file; users can query Last-Modified and ETag. Unknown details: lifetime and thread-safety beyond provided API are not documented here.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_filecache_t h2o_filecache_t;
objects.description: Opaque file cache object managing capacity-limited cached file entries (h2o_filecache_ref_t). Created and destroyed via the provided API. Internal structure is intentionally hidden in this header.
Bitfield flags carried by a single HTTP header. Currently only contains the dont_compress flag indicating the header value should not be compressed. Additional flags may be added in the future.
Represents a single HTTP header: a possibly-tokenized name (points to h2o_iovec_t, often an h2o_token_t), the original case-preserved name string, the value as an iovec, and per-header flags.

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(h2o_header_t) h2o_headers_t;
objects.description: A dynamic vector of h2o_header_t elements. The exact layout depends on the H2O_VECTOR macro expansion (typically a struct with base pointer and size/capacity). Used to hold a list of HTTP headers.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_req_t h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_req_t;
objects.description: Opaque request handle for an asynchronous hostname lookup initiated by h2o_hostinfo_getaddr. The underlying struct st_h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_req_t is forward-declared only in this header and defined elsewhere. Use this handle to cancel a pending lookup via h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_cancel. Ownership and lifetime are managed by the hostinfo subsystem; callers should not dereference or allocate this type directly.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*h2o_hpack_decode_header_cb)(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, void *ctx, h2o_iovec_t **name, h2o_iovec_t *value,
                                          const uint8_t **const src, const uint8_t *src_end, const char **err_desc);
objects.description: Function-pointer typedef for a callback that decodes a single HPACK header field. It consumes bytes from [*src, src_end), allocates strings (using pool) for the header name and value, and reports hard/soft errors via err_desc and return code. The ctx parameter is a caller-provided decode context.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_http1_upgrade_cb)(void *user_data, h2o_socket_t *sock, size_t reqsize);
objects.description: Function-pointer type for an HTTP/1 upgrade completion callback. Invoked after upgrading a connection; receives user_data, the accepted socket, and the number of bytes already read and staged for the upgraded protocol. Detailed semantics (call timing, ownership of sock, and lifetime) are not documented in this header and must be inferred from the h2o HTTP/1 upgrade flow.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only contains macros and function declarations. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_http2_casper_t h2o_http2_casper_t;
objects.description: Opaque HTTP/2 "casper" cache-bloom-like structure used to track which resource paths are (or were) cached by a client, enabling conditional server push or cookie-based hints. The actual struct layout is not defined in this header (incomplete type); manipulation occurs only through the provided API.
Container for HTTP/2 peer SETTINGS values (subset handled here). Holds negotiated values for dynamic header table size, push enablement, concurrency, initial flow-control window, and max frame size.
Represents HTTP/2 stream priority parameters: exclusive flag, dependency stream ID, and weight.
Dynamic HPACK header table implemented as a ring buffer. Tracks entries and HPACK size/capacity constraints.
One entry in the HPACK dynamic table, holding name and value iovecs and a soft error counter. Entries are managed by h2o_hpack_header_table_t.
Parsed HTTP/2 frame header and pointer to payload bytes. Used as the common container for decoded frames.
Decoded DATA frame payload view: pointer to data and its length.
Decoded HEADERS frame payload fields including optional priority, and a pointer/length pair to the HPACK block.
Decoded RST_STREAM payload containing the 32-bit error code.
PONG/PING payload container with fixed 8-byte opaque data.
Decoded GOAWAY payload including last processed stream ID, error code, and optional debug data as an iovec.
Decoded WINDOW_UPDATE payload with the window size increment.
Key/value pair used when encoding a SETTINGS frame. Key is one of H2O_HTTP2_SETTINGS_* identifiers; value is the 32-bit setting value.
Simple flow-control window tracker storing available credit in bytes. Inline helpers provide init/update/consume/get operations.

HTTP/2 connection object holding peer settings, stream registry, scheduler, windows, timers, and various bookkeeping for flow control, prioritization, and DoS mitigation. Constructed and managed by the HTTP/2 server core; provides context for streams and write buffering.

HTTP/2 stream object representing a single request/response exchange over a connection. Tracks state machine, flow-control windows, priority, pending data, and push/pull-specific flags, along with the associated h2o_req_t.
Enum of per-stream lifecycle states used by the internal HTTP/2 stream state machine.
Counters tracking numbers of streams in various phases (open, half-closed, actively sending body) for a category (priority/pull/push).
Enum of connection-level lifecycle states: open, half-closed to new streams, or closing.

objects.definition: KHASH_MAP_INIT_INT64(h2o_http2_stream_t, h2o_http2_stream_t *)
objects.description: Instantiates a khash map type keyed by 64-bit integers to values of h2o_http2_stream_t*. This macro defines khash_t(h2o_http2_stream_t) and related API. Treated here as a custom container type alias usable via khash macros.

Queue entry used by the HTTP/2 scheduler to track a schedulable item within a priority queue, maintaining a link and a deficit counter for weighted fair scheduling. Documentation in this header is minimal; behavior inferred from field names.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_http2_scheduler_queue_t h2o_http2_scheduler_queue_t;
objects.description: Opaque/incomplete queue type representing the internal priority list used by the scheduler. Only forward-declared here; definition is not present in this header.

A node in the HTTP/2 dependency tree (either the root for a connection or a per-stream node). Tracks parent relationship, a list of child references, and an optional priority queue. Used as the root handle for scheduler APIs.

Represents an open HTTP/2 stream reference that participates in the scheduler. Embeds a scheduler node, weight, link into parent’s list, activation counters/flags, an internal queue node, and a relocation flag. Lifecycle is managed through open/close/activate/deactivate APIs.

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_http2_scheduler_run_cb)(h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t *ref, int *still_is_active, void *cb_arg);
objects.description: Callback function type invoked by h2o_http2_scheduler_run for each active reference. Should signal whether the reference remains active and whether traversal should stop.
Enumeration of HTTP/3 priority element kinds (request stream, push stream, placeholder, or root). Used when encoding/decoding PRIORITY_UPDATE or managing dependencies.
Represents an HTTP/3 PRIORITY_UPDATE frame: indicates whether the target is a push, the element id, and the priority field value as an iovec.
Represents an HTTP/3 GOAWAY frame payload containing the last stream or push ID to accept.
Aggregated QUIC statistics maintained by the context, including received/processed packet counts, largest sentmap size, and embedded quicly counters.
Top-level QUIC runtime context tying together event loop, UDP socket, quicly context, forwarding/accept callbacks, and stats. Initialized and disposed via provided API.
Callback vtable for generic QUIC connections; currently includes a destroy_connection hook invoked on connection teardown.
State of an HTTP/3 connection: open, half-closed (no new streams), or closing (no sending).
Base connection object tying an application connection to a quicly connection and context, with callbacks and transport timer.
Configuration for QPACK on an HTTP/3 connection, currently the preferred encoder dynamic table capacity.
HTTP/3-specific callbacks extending the generic QUIC callbacks, adding a handler for control-stream frames.
HTTP/3 connection object embedding the generic QUIC connection, connection state, QPACK encoder/decoder, peer settings, control streams, and header frame size limit.
Parsed frame view returned by h2o_http3_read_frame: contains frame type, parsed header size, payload pointer, and payload length.

HTTP/3 egress unidirectional stream state holder. Contains a back-pointer to the underlying QUIC stream (quic) and a buffer for outbound data (sendbuf). Exact lifecycle and ownership semantics are not documented here; inferred usage suggests it is embedded in higher-level HTTP/3 connection/stream management code.

objects.definition: /* generated by KHASH_MAP_INIT_INT */
objects.description: Hash map type generated by KHASH_MAP_INIT_INT, mapping int keys to h2o_quic_conn_t* values. The concrete struct definition is generated by the khash macros and not explicitly present in this header.

objects.definition: /* generated by KHASH_MAP_INIT_INT64 */
objects.description: Hash map type generated by KHASH_MAP_INIT_INT64, mapping 64-bit integer keys to h2o_quic_conn_t* values. The concrete struct definition is generated by the khash macros and not explicitly present in this header.

HTTP/3 server context wrapper around h2o_quic_ctx_t. Holds QUIC context (super), the H2O accept context, a flag indicating whether to send QUIC Retry, and the HTTP/3 QPACK dynamic table/context. Intended to be used when accepting and serving HTTP/3 connections on the server side. Details of member lifetimes and ownership are not documented in this header; they follow H2O/QUIC context lifetimes.

Primary HTTP client object representing a single in-flight request/stream. Holds callbacks, buffers, context, and byte counters, and exposes operations to cancel, query connection properties, update flow-control window, and write request body.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_httpclient_forward_datagram_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client, h2o_iovec_t *datagrams, size_t num_datagrams);
objects.description: Function pointer type invoked to forward QUIC DATAGRAM frames to or from the application.

Mutable per-request properties initialized by the client stack and optionally adjusted by the application (e.g., PROXY protocol line, chunked encoding, Connection header override, pipe-reader preference, Expect: 100-continue behavior).

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_httpclient_pipe_reader_t h2o_httpclient_pipe_reader_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for a structure describing pipe-based body consumption. Full definition appears later in the header.
Arguments delivered with response headers: HTTP version, status, reason, headers, and optional DATAGRAM forwarders and pipe-reader facility.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_httpclient_proceed_req_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client, const char *errstr);
objects.description: Callback to notify that previously provided request body bytes have been flushed and the sender may proceed or that an error occurred.

objects.definition: typedef int (*h2o_httpclient_body_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client, const char *errstr, h2o_header_t *trailers, size_t num_trailers);
objects.description: Callback invoked to deliver response body chunks and final trailers; returns non-zero to continue or stop depending on implementation contract.

objects.definition:
typedef h2o_httpclient_body_cb (*h2o_httpclient_head_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client, const char *errstr,
                                                         h2o_httpclient_on_head_t *args);
objects.description: Callback invoked when response headers are received; returns a body callback to receive the body.

objects.definition:
typedef h2o_httpclient_head_cb (*h2o_httpclient_connect_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client, const char *errstr, h2o_iovec_t *method,
                                                            h2o_url_t *url, const h2o_header_t **headers, size_t *num_headers,
                                                            h2o_iovec_t *body, h2o_httpclient_proceed_req_cb *proceed_req_cb,
                                                            h2o_httpclient_properties_t *props, h2o_url_t *origin);
objects.description: Callback invoked when the stack is ready to issue a request; the application fills method, URL, headers, body, properties, and returns the header callback.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*h2o_httpclient_informational_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client, int version, int status, h2o_iovec_t msg,
                                               h2o_header_t *headers, size_t num_headers);
objects.description: Optional callback to receive interim 1xx responses (except 101 when final).

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_httpclient_finish_cb)(h2o_httpclient_t *client);
objects.description: Callback type for completion notification (declared but not referenced further in this header).
Concrete definition of pipe-reader: provides a file descriptor to read the body from and a callback to notify consumption of piped data.
Per-thread client connection pool referencing a shared socketpool for HTTP/1 and per-thread connection lists for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.
Configuration for probabilistic selection between HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 usage across requests.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_http3client_ctx_t h2o_http3client_ctx_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for HTTP/3-specific client context; full definition follows later in this header.
Global client context holding loop, timeouts, buffer limits, protocol selection heuristics, HTTP/2 settings, and optional HTTP/3 context.
HTTP/3 client-wide context including TLS, QUIC, H3 parameters and an optional session-resumption loader callback.
Timestamps capturing client-side timing milestones of the request/response lifecycle.
Describes properties of the underlying connection for a request: TLS info and the socket pointer, if any.
Public members of an HTTP/2 client connection used by the httpclient: context, origin, socket, stream count, and ordering link.
HTTP/3 client connection object used internally: wraps an h2o_http3_conn_t plus client context, origin identification, handshake properties, timers, address-resolution request, and linklists.

Intrusive doubly linked list node/anchor type. The same structure represents both list nodes and the list head (anchor). Nodes should be zero-filled upon initialization; anchors must be initialized with h2o_linklist_init_anchor before use. A node is considered linked if its next field is non-NULL. Unlinking resets next and prev to NULL.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_memcached_context_t h2o_memcached_context_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a memcached client context used by this API. Actual structure is not defined in this header, indicating it is private/hidden. Used to perform get/set/delete operations and to manage worker threads and connections.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_memcached_req_t h2o_memcached_req_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing an in-flight memcached GET request. Returned by h2o_memcached_get and can be canceled via h2o_memcached_cancel_get. Definition is not provided in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_memcached_get_cb)(h2o_iovec_t value, void *cb_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for GET completion callback. Called with the retrieved value (possibly empty on miss or error, semantics not documented here) and the user-supplied cb_data pointer.

Opaque/forward-declared handle to a buffer prototype, with concrete definition present later in the file. It stores an initial buffer instance and optional mmap settings used to initialize and manage h2o_buffer_t instances.
A simple iovec-compatible buffer view consisting of a base pointer and length. Commonly used to pass contiguous byte ranges.

objects.definition:
#define H2O_VECTOR(type)                                                                                                           \
    struct {                                                                                                                       \
        type *entries;                                                                                                             \
        size_t size;                                                                                                               \
        size_t capacity;                                                                                                           \
    }

typedef H2O_VECTOR(void) h2o_vector_t;
objects.description: Generic vector layout macro and its void-specialized typedef h2o_vector_t. Represents a dynamically sized array with entries, size, and capacity.

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(uint8_t) h2o_byte_vector_t;
objects.description: Vector of bytes using the H2O_VECTOR layout. Holds a growable array of uint8_t.

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(h2o_iovec_t) h2o_iovec_vector_t;
objects.description: Vector of h2o_iovec_t using the H2O_VECTOR layout. Useful for batching buffers.
Configuration for the memory recycling allocator: object size and alignment (as log2 via align_bits).
A simple recycling allocator that caches freed fixed-size chunks for reuse, governed by a configuration and a low-watermark threshold.
Header placed before ref-counted shared allocations made by the memory pool. Tracks reference count, an optional disposer, and the start of payload bytes.
Arena-style memory pool that allocates from linked chunks and tracks shared references and direct allocations for cleanup.
Resizable byte buffer for incoming/outgoing data. May be initialized from a prototype, optionally backed by mmap via file descriptor _fd. Contains inline storage for small data.
Settings controlling when and how buffers use mmap: threshold size and template for temporary file names.
A helper that toggles between a receiving buffer and an inflight buffer to coordinate producing and sending data.
Receiver registered to an inter-thread message queue. Holds a back-pointer to its queue, an internal link and message list, and the callback to handle received messages.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_multithread_queue_t h2o_multithread_queue_t;
objects.description: Opaque queue object used for inter-thread communication and integration with an event loop. Definition is not present in this header.
Message node sent through a multithread queue. Embeds a link for inclusion in linked lists.
Counting semaphore implemented using pthread mutex/cond. _cur tracks current count; _capacity is the maximum. Use h2o_sem_init/destroy/wait/post/set_capacity.
Thread barrier primitive. Tracks participating threads and those that have exited wait. Initialize with h2o_barrier_init; use wait/done/add/dispose to manage lifecycle.

Rate-limited error reporter. Public fields (without leading underscore) may be accessed by the reporting callback. Private fields manage synchronization, a delayed timer, success counters, and the callback to invoke when delay expires. Initialize with H2O_ERROR_REPORTER_INITIALIZER, record successes via inline h2o_error_reporter_record_success and errors via h2o_error_reporter_record_error.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_multithread_receiver_cb)(h2o_multithread_receiver_t *receiver, h2o_linklist_t *messages);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type invoked when messages are delivered to a receiver. Receives the receiver pointer and the list of messages.

BIO_METHOD is an OpenSSL struct type referenced here but not defined in this header. This header provides a backport constructor helper BIO_meth_new that allocates and initializes a BIO_METHOD for OpenSSL versions prior to 1.1.0. The actual structure layout is defined by OpenSSL, not in this file.

Pipe-backed sender state used by the H2O framework to transmit data via a pipe file descriptor pair. Tracks the pipe fds (initialized to -1 until started), whether data is currently inflight to the protocol handler, and cumulative bytes sent. Used with helper functions to init, start, send, and dispose. Detailed lifecycle and IO semantics beyond these fields are not documented in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_qpack_decoder_t h2o_qpack_decoder_t;
objects.description: Opaque QPACK decoder handle used by the H2O HTTP/3 QPACK implementation. The actual struct layout is intentionally hidden (forward-declared) and managed via the create/destroy APIs in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_qpack_encoder_t h2o_qpack_encoder_t;
objects.description: Opaque QPACK encoder handle used by the H2O HTTP/3 QPACK implementation. The actual struct layout is intentionally hidden (forward-declared) and managed via the create/destroy APIs in this header.
Enumeration of the client connection state for the Redis async client. Values indicate closed, in-progress connection, or established connection.

Opaque-ish client state for managing an asynchronous Redis connection integrated with an h2o event loop. Holds loop handle, connection state, connect/close callbacks, timeouts, and the underlying hiredis async context and timeout timer.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_redis_command_cb)(struct redisReply *reply, void *cb_data, const char *errstr);
objects.description: Callback function type invoked upon completion of a Redis command. Receives the hiredis redisReply pointer (may be NULL on error), user cb_data, and an error string if any.
Enumeration of command categories supported by the client: normal request/response and subscription-related modes, monitor, and an internal error marker.
Represents an issued Redis command bound to a client. Stores the completion callback, user data, command type, and a per-command timeout timer.

Enum type representing the state of a send operation in the H2O context. Values indicate whether sending is ongoing (IN_PROGRESS), has completed normally (FINAL), or has failed (ERROR). Intended for flow-control/state-tracking in send logic. Destruction is trivial; it is a value type.

Sliding window counter/timer helper tracking an average over eight slots plus a current running period. Used to start, stop, and compute average durations or counts over time. Start timestamp is stored in cur.start_at; prev holds ring-buffer aggregation.

Abstraction of a socket that may be plain TCP or TLS (OpenSSL/picotls). Holds callbacks, I/O buffers, statistics, address info, latency optimization hints, and zero-copy state. Managed via API functions in this header (connect/import/export/read/write/etc.).

objects.definition: struct st_h2o_io_uring_cmd_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration for an internal io_uring command object used by probes. Definition is not present in this header.
Socket address wrapper embedding sockaddr along with its length. Used for local/peer address storage within h2o_socket_t.

Send vector abstraction providing deferred materialization of bytes via callbacks. Holds current remaining length and either a raw pointer or callback arguments for producers. Used with h2o_socket_sendvec.
Callback vtable for h2o_sendvec_t. read_ is mandatory to provide sequential access; send_ optionally performs zero-copy or direct OS sends.
Opaque export package containing fd, TLS state pointer, and input buffer for detaching a socket from a loop and importing to another.
Tunable thresholds guiding latency-optimized write behavior: minimum RTT, maximum additional delay percentage, and max cwnd in bytes.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_socket_cb)(h2o_socket_t *sock, const char *err);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type for socket read/write/notify events. Receives socket and error string (NULL on success).

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_socket_ssl_resumption_get_async_cb)(h2o_socket_t *sock, h2o_iovec_t session_id);
objects.description: Callback type invoked to fetch session data asynchronously for TLS resumption, given the session_id.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_socket_ssl_resumption_new_cb)(h2o_socket_t *sock, h2o_iovec_t session_id, h2o_iovec_t session_data);
objects.description: Callback type to notify creation of new TLS session data to be stored for resumption.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_socket_ssl_resumption_remove_cb)(h2o_iovec_t session_id);
objects.description: Callback type to remove TLS session data associated with a session_id.

Type referenced from picotls for logging TLS connection state. Not defined in this header; included here only because h2o_socket_t embeds it. Skipping per instruction would normally be appropriate, but it appears as a field; definition is external and unavailable.
Forward-declared elsewhere (picotls). Not defined here; referenced by functions only. Per instruction, this should be ignored, but it appears as a parameter type only.

Main event loop object for H2O. Holds pending socket queues, current time (ms and ns), last gettimeofday snapshot, timer wheel handle, execution-time sliding counter, and run counter. Owns timer scheduling via _timeouts and tracks sockets awaiting processing.

objects.definition: typedef h2o_evloop_t h2o_loop_t;
objects.description: Alias typedef for h2o_evloop_t used where a generic 'loop' name is preferred. Same layout and semantics as h2o_evloop_t.

objects.definition: typedef h2o_timerwheel_entry_t h2o_timer_t;
objects.description: Alias typedef for a timer entry managed by the timer wheel. Used with h2o_timer_* helpers/macros to schedule callbacks on the event loop. Actual structure is defined elsewhere (h2o_timerwheel.h).

objects.definition: typedef h2o_timerwheel_cb h2o_timer_cb;
objects.description: Alias typedef for the callback function type used by timer wheel timers. Actual function signature is defined in h2o_timerwheel.h.
Enumeration of socketpool target kinds: a named target (hostname/servname to resolve) or a sockaddr target (pre-resolved address).
Per-target load balancer configuration. Stores weight minus one (valid 0..255 corresponding to weights 1..256).

Represents a single backend target for the socket pool, including its URL, type, optional pre-resolved sockaddr or named service, per-target load-balancer configuration, and per-target shared state (pooled sockets and leased count).

objects.definition: typedef H2O_VECTOR(h2o_socketpool_target_t *) h2o_socketpool_target_vector_t;
objects.description: Vector container of h2o_socketpool_target_t pointers. Exact layout depends on H2O_VECTOR macro expansion (not shown here).

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_balancer_t h2o_balancer_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for a load balancer strategy used by the socket pool. No definition in this header.

Connection pool managing outbound sockets to a set of targets. Holds configuration (capacity, timeout, SSL context, address family), event-loop linkage, shared synchronized state for pooled/connecting sockets, and an optional balancer. Thread-safe regions are under _shared guarded by a mutex.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_socketpool_connect_request_t h2o_socketpool_connect_request_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing an in-flight connect operation issued to the socket pool. Used to cancel or track a connection attempt.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_socketpool_connect_cb)(h2o_socket_t *sock, const char *errstr, void *data, h2o_url_t *url);
objects.description: Callback function type invoked upon completion of a pool connect attempt. Receives the connected socket or error string, user data, and the resolved URL.

Referenced vector-of-bytes/string slice type used throughout the API (likely has .base and .len). Not defined in this header; definition is expected in included headers (e.g., h2o/memory.h). No definition present here, so details are unknown in this context.

Referenced memory pool handle used by allocation functions in this header. Not defined in this header; definition is expected in included headers (e.g., h2o/memory.h). No definition present here, so details are unknown in this context.

Referenced vector type representing a collection of h2o_iovec_t. Not defined in this header; definition is expected elsewhere (e.g., h2o/memory.h). No definition present here, so details are unknown in this context.

objects.definition: typedef struct st_h2o_timerwheel_t h2o_timerwheel_t;
objects.description: Opaque timer wheel context/handle. The underlying struct st_h2o_timerwheel_t is not defined in this header, making this an opaque type managed through the provided API functions.

Timer entry/node to be scheduled on a timer wheel. Contains an intrusive link, an absolute expiration timestamp, and a callback invoked when the timer expires. The struct is fully defined here and can be stack- or heap-allocated. Initialize with h2o_timerwheel_init_entry before linking; unlink as needed. The _link field is for internal linkage via h2o_linklist and should not be manipulated directly by users.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_timerwheel_cb)(struct st_h2o_timerwheel_entry_t *entry);
objects.description: Function pointer type for timer callbacks. Called with the corresponding h2o_timerwheel_entry_t when the timer fires.

Bitfield flags describing token metadata, including HPACK/QPACK-related attributes, proxy drop rules, compression behavior, and repeat-likelihood. Also carries an index for the HTTP/2 static table header name if applicable.
Predefined, read-only, fast variant of h2o_iovec_t representing a header name token with associated flags. Instances are provided as global, preinitialized entries and should be treated as immutable.
Represents an entry in the HTTP/2 HPACK static table, pairing a header name token with a constant value buffer. Likely used for indexing/encoding operations.
Represents an entry in the HTTP/3 QPACK static table, pairing a header name token with a constant value buffer. Used for indexing/encoding operations similar to HPACK.

objects.definition: typedef int32_t (*h2o_qpack_lookup_static_cb)(h2o_iovec_t value, int *is_exact);
objects.description: Function pointer type for QPACK static-table lookup callbacks. Implementations take an h2o_iovec_t value and an out-parameter is_exact, and return the index (int32_t) in the static table or a negative value if not found. The header provides an extern array h2o_qpack_lookup_static of these callbacks. Note: h2o_iovec_t is referenced but not defined in this header.
Represents a URL scheme (e.g., http, https). Holds the lowercase scheme name, the default TCP port for that scheme, and whether it uses TLS (is_ssl).

Concrete URL object containing scheme, authority, host, path, and the parsed port. The _port field is 65535 when unspecified; use h2o_url_get_port to obtain an effective port (falls back to scheme->default_port).

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. The file contains only preprocessor macros for version information (e.g., H2O_VERSION, H2O_LIBRARY_VERSION). Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

Opaque-ish websocket connection object for h2o that wraps a socket and a wslay event context. Holds user data, a message callback, and small write buffering. Used to manage an upgraded HTTP connection as a WebSocket. Lifecycle is controlled by upgrade and close APIs in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void (*h2o_websocket_msg_callback)(h2o_websocket_conn_t *conn, const struct wslay_event_on_msg_recv_arg *arg);
objects.description: Function pointer type invoked on incoming WebSocket messages for a given connection. If arg is NULL, the user should close the connection by calling h2o_websocket_close(). The second parameter type is declared by wslay and is only referenced here.

functions.name: h2o_accept
functions.description: Accepts an inbound socket and starts HTTP handling using the provided accept context (hosts, TLS, etc.). Typically called by a listener when a new connection arrives.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized h2o_accept_ctx_t (ctx->ctx set, hosts configured; ssl_ctx if TLS is desired).
sock must be a valid, connected h2o_socket_t owned by the caller; ownership is transferred on success.
May read PROXY protocol if ctx->expect_proxy_line is set.

functions.name: h2o_create_connection
functions.signature: h2o_conn_t *h2o_create_connection(size_t sz, h2o_context_t *ctx, h2o_hostconf_t **hosts, struct timeval connected_at, const h2o_conn_callbacks_t *callbacks);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a connection object with the given size and callbacks for a protocol implementation (HTTP/1, H2, H3).
requirements: sz must be >= sizeof(h2o_conn_t) and match the concrete connection struct size.
ctx must be initialized via h2o_context_init.
hosts must be a NULL-terminated array of h2o_hostconf_t* or NULL.
callbacks must be a valid struct; required members for the protocol must be provided (e.g., get_req_id).

functions.name: h2o_destroy_connection
functions.description: Destroys and releases resources associated with a connection.
requirements: conn must be a connection created by h2o_create_connection or by the protocol layer.
Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: h2o_conn_get_uuid
functions.description: Returns the connection UUID (v4) as a NUL-terminated string, generating it on first call.
requirements: conn must not be NULL.
Returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of conn.

functions.name: h2o_conn_is_early_data
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the connection is in TLS early-data (0-RTT) state (risk of replay).
requirements: conn must not be NULL.
Requires conn->callbacks->get_ptls to be non-NULL and TLS to be in-progress; otherwise returns 0.

functions.name: h2o_accept_setup_memcached_ssl_resumption
functions.description: Configures TLS session resumption backed by memcached, with the given expiration seconds.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized memcached context usable by H2O.
expiration is the session lifetime in seconds (implementation-dependent bounds).

functions.name: h2o_accept_setup_redis_ssl_resumption
functions.signature: void h2o_accept_setup_redis_ssl_resumption(const char *host, uint16_t port, unsigned expiration, const char *prefix);
functions.description: Configures TLS session resumption backed by Redis at host:port, with key prefix and expiration.
requirements: host must be a valid hostname or address string.
port is the Redis TCP port.
expiration is session lifetime in seconds.
prefix may be NULL or a string prefix for session keys.

functions.name: h2o_stringify_protocol_version
functions.description: Writes a textual HTTP version (e.g., "HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/2") to dst from a 0xMMmm version int. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: dst must have sufficient space (at least length of protocol string including no trailing NUL is implied; typical usage writes into a large enough buffer).
version must be a valid 0xMMmm encoded HTTP version.

functions.name: h2o_stringify_proxy_header
functions.description: Builds a HAProxy PROXY protocol v1 header line for conn into buf. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: buf must have capacity of at least H2O_PROXY_HEADER_MAX_LENGTH bytes.
conn must be valid and provide local/peer addresses via conn->callbacks.

functions.name: h2o_extract_push_path_from_link_header
functions.signature: void h2o_extract_push_path_from_link_header(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *value, size_t value_len, h2o_iovec_t base_path, const h2o_url_scheme_t *input_scheme, h2o_iovec_t input_authority, const h2o_url_scheme_t *base_scheme, h2o_iovec_t *base_authority, void (*cb)(void *ctx, const char *path, size_t path_len, int is_critical), void *cb_ctx, h2o_iovec_t *filtered_value, int allow_cross_origin_push);
functions.description: Parses a Link header value, extracts rel=preload targets for HTTP/2 push, and optionally filters value. Invokes cb for each push path discovered.
requirements: pool must be a valid per-request pool.
value/value_len must point to the header content.
cb may be NULL if only filtering is desired; if non-NULL, it must be callable during parsing.
filtered_value may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives a possibly filtered version.
base_path, schemes, and authorities should correspond to the request context. allowing cross-origin pushes depends on allow_cross_origin_push and configuration.

functions.name: h2o_get_compressible_types
functions.description: Parses Accept-Encoding in headers and returns a bitmap of supported compressions (H2O_COMPRESSIBLE_* flags).
requirements: headers must be initialized and contain request headers.
Caller interprets returned bitmask using H2O_COMPRESSIBLE_GZIP/BROTLI/ZSTD.

functions.name: h2o_build_destination
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_build_destination(h2o_req_t *req, const char *prefix, size_t prefix_len, int use_path_normalized);
functions.description: Builds a destination URL or path by concatenating prefix and the request’s path or normalized path.
requirements: req must be initialized.
prefix may be NULL or non-NULL; prefix_len must match.
If use_path_normalized is non-zero, req->path_normalized must be available.

functions.name: h2o_add_server_timing_header
functions.description: Marks the request to include Server-Timing information as a header or trailer.
requirements: req must be initialized.
uses_trailer non-zero indicates timing will be emitted via trailer; otherwise header.

functions.name: h2o_build_server_timing_trailer
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_build_server_timing_trailer(h2o_req_t *req, const char *prefix, size_t prefix_len, const char *suffix, size_t suffix_len);
functions.description: Builds the Server-Timing trailer value, optionally adding prefix/suffix.
requirements: req must be initialized and have timing data (set via h2o_add_server_timing_header or defaults).
prefix/suffix may be NULL; lengths must match arguments when non-NULL.

functions.name: h2o_cleanup_thread
functions.description: Garbage-collects per-thread reusable resources, optionally those associated with ctx_optional. Returns milliseconds until next cleanup is advisable.
requirements: now is a clock timestamp in milliseconds; pass 0 for full GC.
ctx_optional may be NULL or a valid context whose resources can be collected.

functions.name: h2o_init_request
functions.description: Initializes a request object for processing on conn. If src is non-NULL, creates a shallow copy.
requirements: req must point to caller-allocated storage.
conn must be a valid connection.
If src is provided, it must point to an initialized request whose fields are safe to shallow-copy.

functions.name: h2o_dispose_request
functions.description: Releases resources attached to a request after processing is complete.
requirements: req must have been initialized by h2o_init_request or used by protocol handler.
Do not use req after disposal.

functions.name: h2o_req_validate_pseudo_headers
functions.description: Validates that HTTP/2/3 pseudo-headers are present and in correct form before handing to h2o_process_request. Returns non-zero on success.
requirements: req must contain parsed headers and pseudo-header fields.
Should be called by protocol implementation before h2o_process_request.

functions.name: h2o_process_request
functions.description: Starts processing a request that is ready (routing, handlers, filters).
requirements: req must be initialized, validated, and bound to host/path configurations (via h2o_req_setup/bind).

functions.name: h2o_get_first_handler
functions.description: Returns the first request handler from the bound path configuration for this request (or NULL).
requirements: req must be bound to a pathconf (h2o_req_bind_conf or h2o_req_setup).

functions.name: h2o_delegate_request
functions.description: Delegates processing to the next handler in the chain for this request.
requirements: req must be in processing state, typically within a handler.
May change req->handler to the next available handler.

functions.name: h2o_delegate_request_deferred
functions.description: Schedules a delegation to the next handler using a zero-timeout (deferred).
requirements: Same as h2o_delegate_request, but safe to call when immediate delegation is not possible (e.g., inside certain callbacks).

functions.name: h2o_reprocess_request
functions.signature: void h2o_reprocess_request(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_iovec_t method, const h2o_url_scheme_t *scheme, h2o_iovec_t authority, h2o_iovec_t path, h2o_req_overrides_t *overrides, int is_delegated);
functions.description: Reprocesses a request (internal redirect), optionally changing method/scheme/authority/path and applying overrides. is_delegated marks delegated responses.
requirements: req must be initialized and in a state allowing reprocessing.
method, scheme, authority, path specify new target; their lifetimes must cover reprocess scheduling.
overrides may be NULL or point to valid overrides structure.

functions.name: h2o_reprocess_request_deferred
functions.signature: void h2o_reprocess_request_deferred(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_iovec_t method, const h2o_url_scheme_t *scheme, h2o_iovec_t authority, h2o_iovec_t path, h2o_req_overrides_t *overrides, int is_delegated);
functions.description: Deferred (zero-timeout) variant of h2o_reprocess_request.
requirements: Same as h2o_reprocess_request; arguments must remain valid until executed.

functions.name: h2o_replay_request
functions.description: Requests that the protocol handler replays the request (e.g., after 425 Too Early).
requirements: req must be associated with a protocol supporting replay semantics.
Typically set when req->reprocess_if_too_early is true.

functions.name: h2o_replay_request_deferred
functions.description: Deferred variant of h2o_replay_request.
requirements: Same as h2o_replay_request; req must stay valid until the deferred action runs.

functions.name: h2o_start_response
functions.description: Binds a generator to the request, signaling that headers are ready and body will be produced via proceed/send callbacks.
requirements: req must be in processing state; headers must be prepared in req->res.
generator must set proceed and optionally stop callbacks; remains valid until completion.

functions.name: h2o_add_ostream
functions.signature: h2o_ostream_t *h2o_add_ostream(h2o_req_t *req, size_t alignment, size_t sz, h2o_ostream_t **slot);
functions.description: Allocates and inserts an output stream filter into the chain at slot, returning the new ostream.
requirements: req must be valid and in response setup phase.
alignment must be a power-of-two appropriate for the filter struct.
sz must be the size of the filter struct; caller initializes its function pointers.

functions.name: h2o_req_setup
functions.description: Prepares the request for processing by analyzing method, URI, and headers; binds host/path configuration. Returns selected hostconf.
requirements: req->input fields (scheme/authority/path) must be set.
Called once per request prior to processing.

functions.name: h2o_req_apply_env
functions.description: Applies environment configuration (set/unset variables) to the request’s env.
requirements: env may be NULL or a valid env configuration (possibly chained via parent).
req must have an initialized env vector.

functions.name: h2o_req_bind_conf
functions.description: Binds host and path configurations to a request, establishing filters/loggers/handlers lists.
requirements: hostconf and pathconf must belong to the same global configuration.
req must be initialized.

functions.name: h2o_send_state_is_in_progress
functions.description: Convenience check that returns non-zero iff s == H2O_SEND_STATE_IN_PROGRESS.
requirements: s must be a valid h2o_send_state_t.

functions.name: h2o_send
functions.signature: void h2o_send(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_iovec_t *bufs, size_t bufcnt, h2o_send_state_t state);
functions.description: Sends response body data as iovec(s) with a send state. For partial sends, wait for proceed then call again.
requirements: req must have a generator bound via h2o_start_response.
bufs may be NULL when only signaling headers or finalization as permitted; bufcnt must match.
state must be IN_PROGRESS, FINAL, or ERROR; do not send empty body mid-stream unless signaling headers/closure.

functions.name: h2o_sendvec
functions.signature: void h2o_sendvec(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_sendvec_t *vecs, size_t veccnt, h2o_send_state_t state);
functions.description: Like h2o_send but accepts h2o_sendvec_t arrays (can reference files, pipes, etc.).
requirements: Same semantics as h2o_send. vecs/veccnt must describe valid send buffers for the duration of the call.

functions.name: h2o_send_from_pipe
functions.signature: void h2o_send_from_pipe(h2o_req_t *req, int pipefd, size_t len, h2o_send_state_t send_state);
functions.description: Wrapper around h2o_sendvec that sends len bytes from a pipe file descriptor using zero-copy where possible.
requirements: req must have a generator bound.
pipefd must be a valid readable pipe FD; ownership/lifetime managed by caller.
len is the number of bytes to forward; send_state signals stream state.

functions.name: h2o_add_prefilter
functions.description: Creates and inserts a request prefilter node used to capture/alter response before filters.
requirements: req must be initialized.
alignment must be appropriate for the prefilter struct; sz is its size; caller sets next/on_setup_ostream.

functions.name: h2o_setup_next_prefilter
functions.description: Requests the next prefilter to set up its ostream; if none, falls through to the first regular filter.
requirements: self may be NULL only if caller ensures direct fallback; normally pass the current prefilter.
req and slot must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_setup_next_ostream
functions.description: Requests the next filter (if any) to set up its ostream in the chain.
requirements: req must be bound to filters; slot points to the insertion point for the next ostream.

functions.name: h2o_ostream_send_next
functions.signature: void h2o_ostream_send_next(h2o_ostream_t *ostream, h2o_req_t *req, h2o_sendvec_t *bufs, size_t bufcnt, h2o_send_state_t state);
functions.description: For ostream filters to forward output to the next filter. Filters should free themselves after final chunk.
requirements: ostream and req must be valid and in sending state.
Filters must not set state to FINAL unless their do_send was invoked with final.
bufs/bufcnt describe the data to pass; can be NULL when signaling final/error appropriately.

functions.name: h2o_proceed_response
functions.description: Requests more output: invokes generator->proceed if present, otherwise drives ostream with FINAL and no data.
requirements: req must be in a response state; either a generator or an ostream chain top must exist.

functions.name: h2o_proceed_response_deferred
functions.description: Schedules a proceed of the response using zero-timeout (deferred).
requirements: req must remain valid until the deferred proceed executes.

functions.name: h2o_req_fill_mime_attributes
functions.description: Fills req->res.mime_attr if currently NULL, based on response headers/mime mapping.
requirements: req must be initialized and have res.headers set.

functions.name: h2o_req_getenv
functions.signature: inline h2o_iovec_t *h2o_req_getenv(h2o_req_t *req, const char *name, size_t name_len, int allocate_if_not_found);
functions.description: Returns pointer to the value of a request environment variable (creating an entry if requested).
requirements: req must be initialized; req->env must be usable.
name/name_len specify the variable name.
If allocate_if_not_found is non-zero, storage is allocated from req->pool and an empty value is inserted.

functions.name: h2o_req_unsetenv
functions.signature: inline void h2o_req_unsetenv(h2o_req_t *req, const char *name, size_t name_len);
functions.description: Removes a variable from the request environment if present.
requirements: req must be initialized; req->env valid.
name/name_len specify the variable to remove.

functions.name: h2o_config_create_envconf
functions.description: Creates a new environment configuration, optionally copying from parent src.
requirements: src may be NULL or an existing envconf to inherit from.

functions.name: h2o_config_setenv
functions.signature: void h2o_config_setenv(h2o_envconf_t *envconf, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Adds or sets an environment variable (name=value) in envconf.
requirements: envconf must be created by h2o_config_create_envconf.
name/value must be non-NULL strings.

functions.name: h2o_config_unsetenv
functions.description: Marks an environment variable to be removed when applying envconf.
requirements: envconf must be valid.
name must be non-NULL string.

functions.name: h2o_config_init_pathconf
functions.signature: void h2o_config_init_pathconf(h2o_pathconf_t *pathconf, h2o_globalconf_t *globalconf, const char *path, h2o_mimemap_t *mimemap);
functions.description: Initializes a path-level configuration under globalconf with an optional path and mimemap.
requirements: pathconf must be caller-allocated.
globalconf must be initialized.
path may be NULL (fallback or extension-level).
mimemap may be NULL (uses fallback/extension-level behavior).

functions.name: h2o_config_dispose_pathconf
functions.description: Disposes resources owned by a pathconf.
requirements: pathconf must have been initialized.
Do not use pathconf after disposal unless re-initialized.

functions.name: h2o_config_init
functions.description: Initializes the global configuration object with defaults.
requirements: config must be caller-allocated storage.

functions.name: h2o_config_register_host
functions.description: Registers a host (authority) context in the global configuration and returns it.
requirements: config must be initialized.
host.base must be a lower-cased, NUL-terminated host/hostport per comments; port is 65535 if default.

functions.name: h2o_config_register_path
functions.description: Registers a path configuration under hostconf. Since v2.0, matching honors exact or prefix-with-slash as documented.
requirements: hostconf must be valid.
path must be a NUL-terminated string representing the mount path.
flags must be zero (currently unused).

functions.name: h2o_config_register_status_handler
functions.description: Registers an extra status handler for the server-wide status endpoint.
requirements: config must be initialized.
status_handler->final is mandatory; init/per_thread are optional.

functions.name: h2o_config_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of resources allocated for the global configuration.
requirements: config must have been initialized by h2o_config_init.
After disposal, config fields must not be used.

functions.name: h2o_create_handler
functions.description: Allocates and attaches a handler object of size sz to the given pathconf.
requirements: conf must be a valid, initialized pathconf.
sz must be >= sizeof(h2o_handler_t). Caller initializes callbacks.

functions.name: h2o_create_filter
functions.description: Allocates and attaches a response filter of size sz to the given pathconf.
requirements: conf must be valid.
sz must be >= sizeof(h2o_filter_t). Caller sets callbacks.

functions.name: h2o_create_logger
functions.description: Allocates and attaches a logger of size sz to the given pathconf.
requirements: conf must be valid.
sz must be >= sizeof(h2o_logger_t). Caller sets callbacks.

functions.name: h2o_context_init
functions.description: Initializes a server context bound to an event loop and global configuration.
requirements: context must be caller-allocated.
loop must be a valid event loop (libuv or h2o evloop).
config must be initialized.

functions.name: h2o_context_dispose
functions.description: Disposes resources allocated for the context, including caches and pools.
requirements: context must have been initialized.
Do not reuse without re-initialization.

functions.name: h2o_context_request_shutdown
functions.description: Requests graceful shutdown of all connections governed by the context.
requirements: context must be valid.
Callers should expect connections to transition to shutdown state.

functions.name: h2o_context_init_pathconf_context
functions.description: Initializes per-context data for the given pathconf (invokes handlers/filters/loggers on_context_init).
requirements: ctx must be an initialized context.
pathconf must be initialized.

functions.name: h2o_context_dispose_pathconf_context
functions.description: Disposes per-context data previously set up for the given pathconf.
requirements: ctx and pathconf must correspond to a previously initialized pair.

functions.name: h2o_get_timestamp
functions.description: Returns the current timestamp (UTC) and links a shared stringified timestamp into the pool.
requirements: ctx must be an initialized context.
pool must be a valid memory pool to link the timestamp strings against.

functions.name: h2o_context_update_timestamp_string_cache
functions.description: Updates the preformatted timestamp strings cached in the context when the second changes.
requirements: ctx must be valid and initialized.

functions.name: h2o_context_close_idle_connections
functions.description: Closes up to max_connections_to_close connections that have been idle for at least min_age milliseconds.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
min_age is the inactivity threshold in milliseconds.

functions.name: h2o_conn_set_state
functions.description: Transitions a connection to a new state (idle, active, shutdown) and updates tracking lists/counters.
requirements: conn must be a connection managed by ctx.
state must be one of H2O_CONN_STATE_*.

functions.name: h2o_context_get_handler_context
functions.description: Returns per-module context pointer for the given handler within ctx.
requirements: ctx and handler must be valid and previously registered (slot assigned).

functions.name: h2o_context_set_handler_context
functions.description: Sets the per-module context pointer for the given handler within ctx.
requirements: ctx and handler must be valid; handler->_config_slot must be set.
handler_ctx may be NULL or a valid pointer owned by the module.

functions.name: h2o_context_get_filter_context
functions.description: Returns per-module context pointer for the given filter within ctx.
requirements: ctx and filter must be valid and registered.

functions.name: h2o_context_set_filter_context
functions.description: Sets per-module context pointer for the given filter within ctx.
requirements: ctx and filter must be valid; filter->_config_slot must be set.

functions.name: h2o_context_get_logger_context
functions.description: Returns per-module context pointer for the given logger within ctx.
requirements: ctx and logger must be valid and registered.

functions.name: h2o_context_get_storage
functions.description: Returns address of a storage slot in ctx keyed by *key, creating it if necessary and recording a dispose callback.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
*key should be set to (size_t)-1 on first use to allocate a new slot; function updates it.
dispose_cb may be NULL or a function to clean up the slot.

functions.name: h2o_context_set_logger_context
functions.description: Sets per-module context pointer for the given logger within ctx.
requirements: ctx and logger must be valid; logger->_config_slot must be set.

functions.name: h2o_resp_add_date_header
functions.description: Adds a Date header to the response if not present, using the context’s timestamp cache.
requirements: req must be valid and in response phase.

functions.name: h2o_send_inline
functions.signature: void h2o_send_inline(h2o_req_t *req, const char *body, size_t len);
functions.description: Sends a complete response body inline by copying the provided string. See notes about async usage and request lifetime.
requirements: req must be valid; typically call after setting status and headers.
body may be NULL if len is 0; data is copied immediately.
Beware of asynchronous invocation; see header comments for safe patterns.

functions.name: h2o_send_error_generic
functions.signature: void h2o_send_error_generic(h2o_req_t *req, int status, const char *reason, const char *body, int flags);
functions.description: Sends an error response with given status/reason/body using h2o_send_inline semantics.
requirements: req must be valid.
status should be a valid HTTP status code.
flags may include H2O_SEND_ERROR_HTTP1_CLOSE_CONNECTION, H2O_SEND_ERROR_KEEP_HEADERS, H2O_SEND_ERROR_BROKEN_REQUEST.

functions.name: h2o_send_error_deferred
functions.signature: void h2o_send_error_deferred(h2o_req_t *req, int status, const char *reason, const char *body, int flags);
functions.description: Schedules sending an error response using zero-timeout (safe from header-phase filters).
requirements: req must remain valid until the deferred send executes.
Flags/status/reason/body as per h2o_send_error_generic.

functions.name: h2o_send_redirect
functions.signature: void h2o_send_redirect(h2o_req_t *req, int status, const char *reason, const char *url, size_t url_len);
functions.description: Sends an HTTP redirect response with Location set to url.
requirements: req must be valid.
status must be a redirect code (e.g., 301, 303, 308).
url/url_len specify the redirect target; string is copied.

functions.name: h2o_send_redirect_internal
functions.signature: void h2o_send_redirect_internal(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_iovec_t method, const char *url_str, size_t url_len, int preserve_overrides);
functions.description: Handles redirect internally (internal reprocess) possibly changing method and preserving overrides.
requirements: req must be valid.
method is the method to use after redirect.
url_str/url_len specify target; preserve_overrides non-zero to keep req->overrides.

functions.name: h2o_get_redirect_method
functions.description: Determines the method to use after a redirect given original method and status.
requirements: Provide original method token; status is HTTP status.

functions.name: h2o_push_path_in_link_header
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_push_path_in_link_header(h2o_req_t *req, const char *value, size_t value_len);
functions.description: Parses a Link header, registers push paths as needed, and returns a version of the value with 'x-http2-push-only' links removed.
requirements: req must be valid.
value/value_len reference the Link header content.

functions.name: h2o_send_informational
functions.description: Sends an informational (1xx) response according to server policy (send_informational_mode).
requirements: req must be valid and in a state where 1xx is appropriate (e.g., before final response).

functions.name: h2o_req_can_stream_request
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the first handler supports request streaming.
requirements: req must be valid and bound to handlers.

functions.name: h2o_req_should_forward_expect
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the request should forward Expect/100-continue (requires streaming handler with handles_expect).
requirements: req must be valid; evaluates the first handler’s capabilities.

functions.name: h2o_req_resolve_internal_redirect_url
functions.description: Resolves an internal redirect target URL (dest) relative to req’s hostconf into resolved. Returns success as int.
requirements: req must be valid and have hostconf.
dest is the target path/URL; resolved must be non-NULL and writable.

functions.name: h2o_req_log_error
functions.signature: void h2o_req_log_error(h2o_req_t *req, const char *module, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
functions.description: Logs an error associated with a request, formatted like printf, optionally redirected via error_log_delegate.
requirements: req must be valid.
module must be a non-NULL module name string.
fmt and variadic args must be valid for printf-style formatting.

functions.name: h2o_write_error_log
functions.description: Writes an error log entry composed of prefix and msg.
requirements: prefix and msg must reference valid iovecs (NUL termination not required).

functions.name: h2o_logconf_compile
functions.description: Compiles a log format specification into an internal log configuration object.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string.
escape must be one of H2O_LOGCONF_ESCAPE_APACHE or H2O_LOGCONF_ESCAPE_JSON.
errbuf (if non-NULL) may receive an error description on failure.

functions.name: h2o_logconf_dispose
functions.description: Disposes a compiled log configuration.
requirements: logconf must be created by h2o_logconf_compile and not used after disposal.

functions.name: h2o_log_request
functions.description: Formats a log line for req using logconf. Returns pointer to the output buffer and length in len.
requirements: logconf must be valid.
req must be valid.
buf may be NULL to let the function allocate, or a caller-supplied buffer if supported (behavior depends on implementation).

functions.name: h2o__proxy_process_request
functions.description: Processes a request by proxying it upstream (internal handler entry).
requirements: req must be valid and configured for proxying (overrides, socketpool, etc.).

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_create
functions.description: Creates a new, refcounted mimemap object with defaults.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_clone
functions.description: Clones an existing mimemap (shares or copies as implementation-defined).
requirements: src must be a valid mimemap.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_on_context_init
functions.description: Notifies mimemap of context initialization (allocate per-context state).
requirements: mimemap and ctx must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_on_context_dispose
functions.description: Notifies mimemap of context disposal (free per-context state).
requirements: mimemap and ctx must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_has_dynamic_type
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the mimemap contains any dynamic types.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_set_default_type
functions.description: Sets the default MIME type and attributes used when no extension match is found.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.
mime must be a valid MIME string.
attr may be NULL or a pointer to attributes.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_define_mimetype
functions.signature: void h2o_mimemap_define_mimetype(h2o_mimemap_t *mimemap, const char *ext, const char *mime, h2o_mime_attributes_t *attr);
functions.description: Adds or replaces a mapping from file extension to a MIME type with attributes.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.
ext must be an extension string without dot.
mime must be a valid MIME string.
attr may be NULL or attributes pointer.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_define_dynamic
functions.description: Defines a dynamic type for the given extensions and returns its type object (containing a pathconf).
requirements: mimemap must be valid.
exts must be a NULL-terminated array of extension strings.
globalconf must be a valid global configuration.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_remove_type
functions.description: Removes a mapping for the given extension.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.
ext must be a valid extension string.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_clear_types
functions.description: Clears all explicit MIME-type mappings (default remains).
requirements: mimemap must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_get_default_type
functions.description: Returns the default type entry of the mimemap.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_get_type_by_extension
