functions.description: Looks up the type entry corresponding to an extension.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.
ext contains the extension bytes (no dot).

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_get_type_by_mimetype
functions.description: Looks up the type entry corresponding to a MIME string, optionally requiring exact match.
requirements: mimemap must be valid.
mime contains the MIME string.
exact_match_only non-zero requires exact equality.

functions.name: h2o_mimemap_get_default_attributes
functions.description: Returns default attributes for a given MIME type into attr.
requirements: mime must be a valid MIME string.
attr must be non-NULL pointer to receive attributes.

functions.name: h2o_access_log_open_log
functions.description: Opens the access log file at path, returning a file descriptor or negative on error.
requirements: path must be a valid filesystem path with permissions allowing open for append/write.

functions.name: h2o_access_log_open_handle
functions.signature: h2o_access_log_filehandle_t *h2o_access_log_open_handle(const char *path, const char *fmt, int escape);
functions.description: Opens an access log handle using path and a compiled format derived from fmt and escape mode.
requirements: path must be valid; file will be opened/created as needed.
fmt is a format string; escape is one of H2O_LOGCONF_ESCAPE_*.

functions.name: h2o_access_log_register
functions.description: Registers an access log logger on the given pathconf with the provided file handle.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
handle must be a handle from h2o_access_log_open_handle.

functions.name: h2o_access_log_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator that parses access-log configuration in the global configuration.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_server_timing_register
functions.description: Registers the Server-Timing response filter for a path. If enforce is non-zero, always emit timing.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_server_timing_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for Server-Timing filter.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_compress_register
functions.description: Registers gzip/brotli compression filter on a path with the given arguments (min size, qualities).
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
args may be NULL to use defaults; otherwise fields must be set appropriately. H2O_USE_BROTLI governs brotli availability.

functions.name: h2o_compress_transform
functions.signature: h2o_send_state_t h2o_compress_transform(h2o_compress_context_t *self, h2o_req_t *req, h2o_sendvec_t *inbufs, size_t inbufcnt, h2o_send_state_t state, h2o_sendvec_t **outbufs, size_t *outbufcnt);
functions.description: Compresses a chunk of output according to self, producing outbufs/outbufcnt and returning the send state.
requirements: self must be an initialized compressor/decompressor context.
req must be valid (used for decisions and buffers).
inbufs/inbufcnt describe input; outbufs/outbufcnt receive produced buffers (ownership per implementation).
state indicates partial/final/error; caller must respect streaming semantics.

functions.name: h2o_compress_gzip_open
functions.description: Creates a gzip compressor context with the given quality, allocated from pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid memory pool.
quality is an implementation-defined gzip quality (e.g., -1 to disable in args elsewhere; here must be valid for gzip).

functions.name: h2o_compress_gunzip_open
functions.description: Creates a gzip decompressor context allocated from pool.
requirements: pool must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_compress_brotli_open
functions.signature: h2o_compress_context_t *h2o_compress_brotli_open(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, int quality, size_t estimated_cotent_length, size_t preferred_chunk_size);
functions.description: Creates a brotli compressor context (if enabled) with quality and sizing hints.
requirements: pool must be valid.
Requires H2O_USE_BROTLI to be enabled in the build.
estimated_cotent_length/preferred_chunk_size are hints, may be 0.

functions.name: h2o_compress_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the compression filter configurator.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_throttle_resp_register
functions.description: Registers the throttling response filter on the path.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_throttle_resp_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for the throttling response filter.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_errordoc_register
functions.description: Registers an error-document filter mapping status codes to URLs for a path.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
errdocs must point to an array of cnt entries.

functions.name: h2o_errordoc_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for error-document filter.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_expires_register
functions.description: Registers an Expires/Cache-Control header filter with the given arguments (absolute or max-age).
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
args->mode must be H2O_EXPIRES_MODE_ABSOLUTE or H2O_EXPIRES_MODE_MAX_AGE; corresponding data field must be set.

functions.name: h2o_expires_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for the Expires filter.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_fastcgi_register
functions.description: Registers a FastCGI handler that forwards requests to upstream URL with vars.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
upstream must describe the FastCGI endpoint.
vars may be NULL or provide timeouts, document_root, callbacks.

functions.name: h2o_fastcgi_register_by_spawnproc
functions.description: Registers a FastCGI handler spawning a process with argv to handle requests.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
argv must be a NULL-terminated argv vector to spawn.
vars may be NULL or specify timeouts/behavior.

functions.name: h2o_fastcgi_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the FastCGI configurator.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_file_send
functions.signature: int h2o_file_send(h2o_req_t *req, int status, const char *reason, const char *path, h2o_iovec_t mime_type, int flags);
functions.description: Sends the file at path as a response with given status/reason and MIME type. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: req must be valid.
status and reason must describe the response.
path must be a readable filesystem path.
mime_type contains the Content-Type.
flags may include H2O_FILE_FLAG_* (NO_ETAG, DIR_LISTING, SEND_COMPRESSED, GUNZIP, IO_URING).

functions.name: h2o_file_register
functions.signature: h2o_file_handler_t *h2o_file_register(h2o_pathconf_t *pathconf, const char *real_path, const char **index_files, h2o_mimemap_t *mimemap, int flags);
functions.description: Registers a static file directory handler serving files under real_path, with optional index files and mimemap.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
real_path must be a filesystem path to serve.
index_files may be NULL or a NULL-terminated list.
mimemap may be NULL (one is created internally).
flags are H2O_FILE_FLAG_*.

functions.name: h2o_file_register_file
functions.signature: h2o_handler_t *h2o_file_register_file(h2o_pathconf_t *pathconf, const char *real_path, h2o_mimemap_type_t *mime_type, int flags);
functions.description: Registers a handler that serves exactly one file at real_path with specified mime_type.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
real_path must be a file path.
mime_type must be a valid mimemap type.
flags are H2O_FILE_FLAG_*.

functions.name: h2o_file_get_mimemap
functions.description: Returns the mimemap associated with a file handler.
requirements: handler must be a handler returned by h2o_file_register.

functions.name: h2o_file_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for file handlers.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_headers_register
functions.description: Registers a list of header rewrite commands (terminated by cmd==H2O_HEADERS_CMD_NULL) for a path.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
cmds must point to a properly terminated array of commands.

functions.name: h2o_headers_is_prohibited_name
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given header name token cannot be manipulated by the headers filter.
requirements: token must be a valid header token.

functions.name: h2o_headers_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for the headers filter.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_proxy_register_reverse_proxy
functions.description: Registers a reverse proxy handler on the path using provided config and socket pool.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
config must be filled with proxy settings; may be NULL to use defaults.
sockpool must be initialized for upstream origin(s).

functions.name: h2o_proxy_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the proxy configurator.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_redirect_register
functions.signature: h2o_redirect_handler_t *h2o_redirect_register(h2o_pathconf_t *pathconf, int internal, int status, const char *prefix);
functions.description: Registers a redirect handler for the path, performing internal or external redirects with the given status and prefix.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
internal non-zero indicates internal redirect; zero for external.
status must be a redirect code.
prefix must be a valid string prefix.

functions.name: h2o_redirect_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the redirect handler configurator.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_reproxy_register
functions.description: Registers the reproxy filter that follows upstream-provided reproxy headers.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_reproxy_register_configurator
functions.description: Registers the configurator for the reproxy filter.
requirements: conf must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_connect_register
functions.signature: void h2o_connect_register(h2o_pathconf_t *pathconf, h2o_proxy_config_vars_t *config, h2o_connect_acl_entry_t *acl_entries, size_t num_acl_entries);
functions.description: Registers a classic HTTP CONNECT handler with proxy config and ACL list.
requirements: pathconf must be valid.
config must be filled with proxy settings.

functions.name: h2o_absprio_urgency_to_chromium_weight
functions.description: Converts an absolute-priority urgency (0..7) into an HTTP/2 weight compatible with Chromium’s interpretation. Lower urgency values map to higher weights, roughly linearly, returning a value in the range [1, 256]. Provided as an inline helper in this header.

functions.name: h2o_cache_calchash
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit hash code for the key bytes at s of length len. Use to precompute keyhash values for cache operations to avoid recomputation.
requirements: s must point to a readable memory buffer of at least len bytes.
len may be 0; hashing an empty buffer is allowed (resulting hash is implementation-defined).
The returned hash code may be passed as keyhash to other cache APIs; otherwise pass 0 to let the cache compute it.

functions.name: h2o_cache_create
functions.signature: h2o_cache_t *h2o_cache_create(int flags, size_t capacity, uint64_t duration, void (*destroy_cb)(h2o_iovec_t value));
functions.description: Creates a new cache instance with the given capacity, entry duration, and a value destructor callback. Flags may include H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED to enable internal mutex protection and H2O_CACHE_FLAG_EARLY_UPDATE to trigger early updates.
requirements: flags is a bitmask; may include H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED and/or H2O_CACHE_FLAG_EARLY_UPDATE.
If H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED is not set, callers must not access the cache concurrently from multiple threads.
capacity specifies the cache capacity (units are implementation-defined within this library; not specified here).
duration specifies the lifetime for cache entries (time unit not specified here; callers must use a consistent time base with the now parameter used in other APIs).
destroy_cb must be a valid function pointer or NULL. If non-NULL, it will be called with the stored h2o_iovec_t value when the cache no longer needs it.
The returned pointer must be destroyed with h2o_cache_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: h2o_cache_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a cache previously created by h2o_cache_create, releasing all resources and invoking destroy_cb for any remaining stored values as appropriate.
requirements: cache must be a cache created by h2o_cache_create or NULL (behavior for NULL is not documented; pass a valid cache).
After calling, cache must not be used again by the caller or other threads.
Callers must ensure no outstanding h2o_cache_ref_t references remain (i.e., all fetched refs were released) before destroying, to avoid use-after-free.

functions.name: h2o_cache_clear
functions.description: Clears all entries from the cache, invoking destroy_cb for values as they are removed.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer returned by h2o_cache_create.
Callers must not hold or use references (h2o_cache_ref_t*) to entries after they are cleared; ensure any such refs are released before or they become invalid (behavior not specified).
If used without H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED, callers must serialize access themselves.

functions.name: h2o_cache_fetch
functions.signature: h2o_cache_ref_t *h2o_cache_fetch(h2o_cache_t *cache, uint64_t now, h2o_iovec_t key, h2o_cache_hashcode_t keyhash);
functions.description: Looks up an entry by key and returns a reference to it if found; otherwise returns NULL. The returned reference must be released with h2o_cache_release. Callers may pass a precomputed keyhash (use h2o_cache_calchash) or 0 to have it computed internally.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer returned by h2o_cache_create.
now must be provided using the same time base as used when setting entries (exact unit not specified here; be consistent across calls).
key must describe the lookup key (pointer/length in h2o_iovec_t) and must be readable during the call.
keyhash may be a precomputed hash for key (via h2o_cache_calchash) or 0 to indicate it should be computed by the cache.
On success, the caller must eventually call h2o_cache_release(cache, ref) exactly once for the returned ref.
Do not modify the contents of the returned h2o_cache_ref_t; treat as read-only.

functions.name: h2o_cache_release
functions.description: Releases a reference obtained from h2o_cache_fetch, decrementing its internal reference count and allowing the cache to recycle or evict the entry.
requirements: cache must be the same cache instance from which ref was fetched.
ref must be a non-NULL pointer previously returned by h2o_cache_fetch and not already released.
Each successful h2o_cache_fetch call that returned a non-NULL ref must be paired with exactly one h2o_cache_release.
Do not use ref after releasing it.

functions.name: h2o_cache_set
functions.signature: int h2o_cache_set(h2o_cache_t *cache, uint64_t now, h2o_iovec_t key, h2o_cache_hashcode_t keyhash, h2o_iovec_t value);
functions.description: Inserts or updates a value for key in the cache at time now. If a value for the key already existed, the function returns non-zero (per comment) and replaces or updates it according to the cache policy. The cache will call destroy_cb on the stored value when it is no longer needed.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer returned by h2o_cache_create.
now must be provided using the same time base as used for fetch/delete (unit not specified; be consistent).
key must describe the key to set; its memory must be readable during the call.
keyhash may be a precomputed hash for key (via h2o_cache_calchash) or 0 to indicate it should be computed by the cache.

value must be a valid h2o_iovec_t; ownership/lifetime: do not free the underlying value separately if destroy_cb will also free it—destroy_cb will be invoked by the cache when the value is no longer needed.
Return value semantics: non-zero if the specified value already existed; zero otherwise (exact meaning of the value is not further specified here).
If used without H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED, callers must serialize access themselves.

functions.name: h2o_cache_delete
functions.signature: void h2o_cache_delete(h2o_cache_t *cache, uint64_t now, h2o_iovec_t key, h2o_cache_hashcode_t keyhash);
functions.description: Deletes the entry named by key from the cache at time now. If present, the value will be removed (and destroy_cb invoked when appropriate).
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer returned by h2o_cache_create.
now must be provided using the same time base as used for set/fetch (unit not specified; be consistent).
key must describe the key to delete; its memory must be readable during the call.
keyhash may be a precomputed hash for key (via h2o_cache_calchash) or 0 to indicate it should be computed by the cache.
If used without H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED, callers must serialize access themselves.
Any outstanding references (h2o_cache_ref_t) to the entry should be released by callers; behavior of deleting while refs exist is not specified here.

functions.name: h2o_cache_get_capacity
functions.description: Returns the capacity of the cache that was configured at creation time.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer returned by h2o_cache_create.
Thread-safety depends on whether the cache was created with H2O_CACHE_FLAG_MULTITHREADED; without it, do not call concurrently with mutating operations.

functions.name: h2o_cache_get_duration
functions.description: Returns the default duration (lifetime) for cache entries configured at creation time.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer returned by h2o_cache_create.
Returned unit is not specified in this header; callers must treat it consistently with the now values they pass to other APIs.

functions.name: h2o_cache_digests_destroy
functions.description: Destroys (frees/releases) an h2o_cache_digests_t object and its internal resources. Use this to clean up a digests instance created/filled by h2o_cache_digests_load_header or equivalent. Purpose: prevent memory/resource leaks after you no longer need the cache digests. Usage: call once per live digests object when done. Notes: The header does not state whether passing NULL is permitted or a no-op; behavior on double-destroy is unspecified.
requirements: digests must point to a valid, fully-initialized h2o_cache_digests_t previously obtained/initialized by the library (e.g., via h2o_cache_digests_load_header).
Do not call this function more than once on the same object (no guarantee of idempotency).
Do not use the digests object after this call (it becomes invalid).
Thread-safety/ownership is unknown; ensure no concurrent access during destruction.

functions.name: h2o_cache_digests_load_header
functions.description: Parses and loads a Cache-Digest-like header value into an h2o_cache_digests_t structure. Purpose: build/update a digest set used to query if specific URLs (and optionally ETags) are fresh/stale/not cached. Usage: pass the address of a digests pointer (which may be NULL) and a header value buffer with its length; the function will allocate or update the digests object accordingly. Notes: The header explicitly states that *digests may be NULL. The header value need not be NUL-terminated as length is provided.
requirements: digests must be a valid pointer to an h2o_cache_digests_t* (i.e., &ptr), and the function may allocate and store a new object to *digests.
*digests may be NULL on entry (allowed by documentation).
value must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes; it may be non-NUL-terminated.
len must be the exact number of bytes in value to parse (0 is allowed but effect is unspecified).
The lifetime of value must extend for the duration of the call.

If *digests already points to an existing object, it must be a valid h2o_cache_digests_t compatible with being (re)loaded/updated by this function; behavior for incompatible or corrupted state is unknown.
Error reporting behavior (e.g., on parse failure) is not specified in this header; callers should assume no return value and rely on library invariants or separate validation.

functions.name: h2o_cache_digests_lookup_by_url
functions.description: Looks up the cache state for a resource identified solely by URL in the given digests. Purpose: determine whether a URL is known to be not cached, fresh, or stale. Returns an h2o_cache_digests_state_t: H2O_CACHE_DIGESTS_STATE_UNKNOWN, H2O_CACHE_DIGESTS_STATE_NOT_CACHED, H2O_CACHE_DIGESTS_STATE_FRESH, or H2O_CACHE_DIGESTS_STATE_STALE. Usage: call after loading digests via h2o_cache_digests_load_header; pass the URL bytes and length (need not be NUL-terminated). Notes: Behavior when digests is NULL is not documented.
requirements: digests must point to a valid, initialized h2o_cache_digests_t containing loaded data.
url must point to a readable buffer of at least url_len bytes; it may be non-NUL-terminated.
url_len must be the exact length of the URL bytes to query (0-length semantics are unspecified).
The lifetime of url must extend for the duration of the call.
Interpretation of the return value is the caller’s responsibility; no separate error indicator is specified.

functions.name: h2o_cache_digests_lookup_by_url_and_etag
functions.signature: h2o_cache_digests_state_t h2o_cache_digests_lookup_by_url_and_etag(h2o_cache_digests_t *digests, const char *url, size_t url_len, const char *etag, size_t etag_len);
functions.description: Looks up the cache state for a resource identified by URL and ETag in the given digests. Usage: call after loading digests via h2o_cache_digests_load_header; supply URL/ETag byte sequences and their lengths. Notes: URL and ETag buffers need not be NUL-terminated; behavior when digests is NULL is not documented.
requirements: digests must point to a valid, initialized h2o_cache_digests_t containing loaded data.
url must point to a readable buffer of at least url_len bytes; it may be non-NUL-terminated.
etag must point to a readable buffer of at least etag_len bytes; it may be non-NUL-terminated.
url_len and etag_len must reflect the exact lengths of their respective buffers (0-length semantics are unspecified).
The lifetimes of url and etag must extend for the duration of the call.
Interpretation of the return value is the caller’s responsibility; no separate error indicator is specified.

functions.name: h2o_configurator_create

functions.name: h2o_configurator_define_command

functions.name: h2o_configurator_apply
functions.description: Applies configuration represented by the given YOML node to the provided global configuration. If dry_run is non-zero, performs a validation-only pass without mutating persistent state (behavior inferred). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.signature: int h2o_configurator_apply_commands(h2o_configurator_context_t *ctx, yoml_t *node, int flags_mask, const char **ignore_commands);

functions.name: h2o_configurator_at_extension_level

functions.name: h2o_configurator__do_parse_mapping
functions.signature: int h2o_configurator__do_parse_mapping(h2o_configurator_command_t *cmd, yoml_t *node, const char *keys_required, const char *keys_optional, yoml_t ****values, size_t num_values);

functions.name: h2o_configurator_get_cmd_path

functions.description: Disposes configurators registered within the given global configuration. Intended to be called during teardown of the configuration system.

functions.name: h2o_file_read
functions.description: Reads the contents of the file specified by path fn and returns them as an h2o_iovec_t (typically a base pointer and length). The created file is unlinked before returning, so its name is not available to the caller; only the open file descriptor is returned. Returns the file descriptor on success, or -1 on failure with errno set as mkstemp would.
requirements: fn_template must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string suitable for mkstemp(3), typically containing a suffix of six 'X' characters (e.g., ".XXXXXX").
The template should reference a directory the process can create files in.
On success, the returned file descriptor refers to an unlinked (nameless) file; the caller must close the descriptor when finished.
On failure, the function returns -1 and sets errno in the same manner as mkstemp(3).

functions.name: h2o_filecache_create
functions.description: Creates a file-cache instance with the requested capacity. Intended to be used as a long-lived cache object from which files can be opened and cached. Details about eviction policy and exact capacity semantics are not documented in this header; based on naming and members, an LRU-like policy is likely.
requirements: capacity is a nonnegative size; specific bounds are not documented.
Must be called before using the returned cache in other filecache APIs.
Caller owns the returned pointer and must eventually destroy it via h2o_filecache_destroy.
Thread-safety/side-effects are not specified; if used across threads, consult implementation.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a file-cache instance, releasing all associated resources and any cached file references the cache still holds. Use when the cache is no longer needed.
requirements: cache must be a valid pointer previously returned by h2o_filecache_create (not NULL).
After this call, cache must not be used again.
Behavior is undefined if called more than once on the same cache pointer.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_clear
functions.description: Clears the contents of the file cache (e.g., evicts cached entries) without destroying the cache object itself. Use to drop all cached files while keeping the cache alive.
requirements: cache must be a valid, initialized cache created by h2o_filecache_create.
Effect on outstanding h2o_filecache_ref_t held by callers is not documented; avoid clearing while holding refs unless implementation guarantees safety.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_open_file
functions.description: Opens (and possibly caches) a file at path using open flags oflag, returning a reference object that holds the file descriptor and cached metadata (stat, Last-Modified, ETag) when successful. On failure, the reference may indicate an open error internally. Use this to retrieve a ref-counted handle to a cached file.
requirements: cache must be a valid cache created by h2o_filecache_create.
path must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointing to the filesystem path.
oflag should be a bitwise OR of platform open(2) flags (e.g., O_RDONLY); required flags are not specified here.
The returned h2o_filecache_ref_t must be closed with h2o_filecache_close_file when no longer needed.
Do not assume fd is valid; callers should be prepared that the ref may represent an open error (see ref->open_err) though the accessor contract is not detailed in this header.
Thread-safety is not documented; avoid concurrent opens of the same path unless implementation guarantees safety.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_close_file
functions.description: Releases a reference returned by h2o_filecache_open_file. Internally decrements the reference count and may close the underlying file descriptor when the last reference is released.
requirements: ref must be a valid pointer previously returned by h2o_filecache_open_file.
Each successful open that returns a non-NULL ref should be paired with exactly one close.
After this call, ref must not be accessed again by the caller.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_get_last_modified
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a struct tm representing the file's Last-Modified time in GMT for the given file reference, and writes a formatted RFC 1123 date string to outbuf. Intended to provide cached Last-Modified metadata for HTTP use.
requirements: ref must be a valid, opened file reference (from h2o_filecache_open_file) whose fd is valid; behavior is unknown if ref represents an open error.
outbuf must point to a writable buffer of at least H2O_TIMESTR_RFC1123_LEN + 1 bytes to hold the null-terminated string.
The returned struct tm pointer is valid as long as the ref remains valid; do not free it.
Function behavior is unspecified if ref is NULL or outbuf is NULL.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_get_etag
functions.description: Computes or retrieves the strong ETag string for the referenced file and writes it into outbuf, returning the length of the tag. Intended for HTTP caching headers.
requirements: ref must be a valid, opened file reference (from h2o_filecache_open_file) with a valid fd; behavior is unknown if ref represents an open error.
outbuf must point to a writable buffer sized for at least H2O_FILECACHE_ETAG_MAXLEN + 1 bytes to store a null-terminated tag.
Return value is the tag length in bytes; whether it includes the terminating null is not stated (likely excludes, based on typical conventions).
Function behavior is unspecified if ref is NULL or outbuf is NULL.

functions.name: h2o_filecache_compare_etag_strong
functions.signature: int h2o_filecache_compare_etag_strong(const char *tag1, size_t tag1_len, const char *tag2, size_t tag2_len);
functions.description: Compares two ETag values for strong equality according to HTTP semantics. Returns an integer indicating equality; exact return convention is not documented, but typically nonzero for equal and zero for not equal.
requirements: tag1 and tag2 must be valid pointers to the tag character buffers, not NULL.
tag1_len and tag2_len must match the actual lengths (in bytes) of tag1 and tag2 respectively; include only the tag characters (do not include any terminating null).
The function expects strong-tag formatting; callers should not pass weak tags (e.g., those prefixed with W/).

functions.name: h2o_find_header
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_find_header(const h2o_headers_t *headers, const h2o_token_t *token, ssize_t cursor);
functions.description: Searches the header list for a header with a given token (fast path using tokens). Use cursor = -1 to begin a new search; pass the previous returned index to find subsequent matches. Returns the index of a matching header, or -1 if not found.
requirements: headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list
token must point to a valid h2o_token_t representing the target header name
cursor must be -1 to start a new search, or a previously returned index to continue searching
caller must handle the return value -1 as 'not found'

functions.name: h2o_find_header_by_str
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_find_header_by_str(const h2o_headers_t *headers, const char *name, size_t name_len, ssize_t cursor);
functions.description: Searches the header list for a header with a given name (string comparison). Use cursor = -1 to start; pass the previous returned index to find subsequent matches. Returns the index of a matching header, or -1 if not found.
requirements: headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list
name must point to a buffer containing the header name to search
name_len must be the length of name in bytes
cursor must be -1 to start a new search, or a previously returned index to continue searching
caller must handle the return value -1 as 'not found'

functions.name: h2o_add_header
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_add_header(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_headers_t *headers, const h2o_token_t *token, const char *orig_name, const char *value, size_t value_len);
functions.description: Adds a header to the list using a known header token (fast path). The header value is taken from value/value_len and the original header-name casing can be supplied via orig_name. Returns the index of the inserted header.
requirements: pool must point to a valid initialized h2o_mem_pool_t able to allocate storage for the header and value
headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list (initialized)
token must point to a valid h2o_token_t representing the header name

orig_name, if provided, should be the original-casing header name with the same length as the tokenized name (per struct doc); if unknown, pass an appropriate pointer or null per library conventions (behavior if NULL is not documented here)
value must point to a buffer containing the header value
value_len must be the length in bytes of value
caller must use the returned index for later reference if needed

functions.name: h2o_add_header_by_str
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_add_header_by_str(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_headers_t *headers, const char *lowercase_name, size_t lowercase_name_len, int maybe_token, const char *orig_name, const char *value, size_t value_len);
functions.description: Adds a header to the list by string name. The name provided should be lowercase (for internal canonicalization). Optionally hints whether the name may correspond to a known token via maybe_token. Returns the index of the inserted header.
requirements: pool must point to a valid initialized h2o_mem_pool_t able to allocate storage for the header and value
headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list (initialized)
lowercase_name must point to the lowercase header name
lowercase_name_len must be the length in bytes of lowercase_name
maybe_token is an int flag indicating whether the name may match a known token (0 or non-zero)

orig_name, if provided, should be the original-casing header name with the same length as lowercase_name (per struct doc); if unknown, pass an appropriate pointer or null per library conventions (behavior if NULL is not documented here)
value must point to a buffer containing the header value
value_len must be the length in bytes of value

functions.name: h2o_set_header
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_set_header(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_headers_t *headers, const h2o_token_t *token, const char *value, size_t value_len, int overwrite_if_exists);
functions.description: Adds a header identified by token or replaces existing ones depending on overwrite_if_exists. If overwrite_if_exists is set, existing headers of that name are replaced; otherwise, a new header may be added. Returns the index of the affected/inserted header.
requirements: pool must point to a valid initialized h2o_mem_pool_t
headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list (initialized)
token must point to a valid h2o_token_t representing the header name
value must point to the header value buffer
value_len must be the length in bytes of value
overwrite_if_exists controls replacement behavior (0 or non-zero)
caller must handle the returned index for subsequent operations if needed

functions.name: h2o_set_header_by_str
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_set_header_by_str(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_headers_t *headers, const char *lowercase_name, size_t lowercase_name_len, int maybe_token, const char *value, size_t value_len, int overwrite_if_exists);
functions.description: Adds or replaces a header identified by a lowercase string name. If overwrite_if_exists is set, existing headers of that name are replaced; otherwise, a new header may be added. maybe_token hints whether the name may match a known token. Returns the index of the affected/inserted header.
requirements: pool must point to a valid initialized h2o_mem_pool_t
headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list (initialized)
lowercase_name must point to the lowercase header name
lowercase_name_len must be the length in bytes of lowercase_name
maybe_token is an int flag indicating whether the name may match a known token (0 or non-zero)
value must point to the header value buffer
value_len must be the length in bytes of value
overwrite_if_exists controls replacement behavior (0 or non-zero)

functions.name: h2o_set_header_token
functions.signature: ssize_t h2o_set_header_token(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_headers_t *headers, const h2o_token_t *token, const char *value, size_t value_len);
functions.description: Sets a header identified by token. Semantics are similar to set/replace, but details beyond taking a tokenized name are not documented here. Returns the index of the affected/inserted header.
requirements: pool must point to a valid initialized h2o_mem_pool_t
headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list (initialized)
token must point to a valid h2o_token_t representing the header name
value must point to the header value buffer
value_len must be the length in bytes of value

functions.name: h2o_delete_header
functions.description: Deletes a header at the given index from the list. Returns an index (semantics not documented here) or possibly the next index; consult implementation for exact behavior.
requirements: headers must point to a valid h2o_headers_t list (initialized)
cursor must be a valid index of an existing header entry, typically obtained from a previous search or add/set operation

functions.name: h2o_header_name_is_equal
functions.signature: inline int h2o_header_name_is_equal(const h2o_header_t *x, const h2o_header_t *y);
functions.description: Compares two headers for name equality. Fast-path compares name pointers; otherwise compares the name byte sequences. Returns non-zero if names are equal, 0 otherwise. Intended to be used when checking if two header entries refer to the same header name.
requirements: x must be a non-null pointer to a valid h2o_header_t with x->name set
y must be a non-null pointer to a valid h2o_header_t with y->name set

functions.name: h2o_hostinfo_getaddr
functions.signature: h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_req_t *h2o_hostinfo_getaddr(h2o_multithread_receiver_t *receiver, h2o_iovec_t name, h2o_iovec_t serv, int family, int socktype, int protocol, int flags, h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_cb cb, void *cbdata)
functions.description: Dispatches a (possibly) asynchronous hostname/service lookup (getaddrinfo-style). Callers provide a multithread receiver to which completion messages are posted, a host name and service, standard getaddrinfo hint fields (family, socktype, protocol, flags), and a callback that will receive either an error string or an addrinfo result list along with cbdata. Intended for use with H2O’s multithread message-passing; the returned handle can be used to cancel the request.
requirements: receiver must point to a valid, initialized h2o_multithread_receiver_t capable of receiving messages for this requester (inferred from parameter type and comment).
name and serv are h2o_iovec_t values representing the host and service; their contents must represent valid inputs for getaddrinfo (inferred from naming and parameters).
family, socktype, protocol, and flags should match the corresponding fields accepted by getaddrinfo (inferred).
cb must be a valid function pointer of type h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_cb; it will be invoked with (req, errstr, res, cbdata).
The returned h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_req_t* is a request handle used for cancellation; do not reuse it after completion or cancellation (inferred).
Error reporting is via the errstr argument to the callback; when non-NULL, it indicates the error; callers should not use res when errstr is non-NULL (inferred from callback signature).

functions.name: h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_cancel
functions.description: Cancels a previously dispatched getaddr request. After cancellation, the request handle should be considered invalid. Useful for aborting outstanding DNS lookups when no longer needed.
requirements: req must be a request handle previously returned by h2o_hostinfo_getaddr and not NULL (inferred).
Do not use req after calling this function (inferred).
Callback invocation semantics on cancellation are unspecified; callers should be prepared that the callback may or may not be invoked after cancellation (unknown; not stated).

functions.name: h2o_hostinfo_getaddr_receiver
functions.description: Message handler to receive and dispatch completion messages for asynchronous getaddr requests via H2O’s multithread system. Typically registered as the receiver callback and invoked by the multithread loop when messages are available.
requirements: receiver must be a valid h2o_multithread_receiver_t corresponding to the getaddr request subsystem (inferred from name and comment).
messages must point to a valid list of queued messages produced by the worker side (inferred).
Must be called from the thread/context that processes messages for the given receiver (inferred).

functions.name: h2o_hostinfo_select_one
functions.description: Selects and returns a single addrinfo entry at random from a linked list of results. If the list has only one element, that element is returned. Uses rand() to choose uniformly across the list length.
requirements: res must be a non-NULL pointer to the head of a valid, well-formed addrinfo singly-linked list via ai_next; the function dereferences res and traverses ai_next.
The list must be finite and acyclic (required for traversal).
rand() must be seeded appropriately elsewhere if repeatability or distribution control is desired (inferred).
The returned pointer aliases one of the nodes from the input list; caller must not free it independently of the original list’s lifetime.

functions.name: h2o_hostinfo_aton
functions.description: Parses a textual IPv4 address into a struct in_addr, equivalent to inet_pton(AF_INET, ...). Returns an int status (exact convention not stated in the header) and writes the parsed address into addr on success.
requirements: host must contain a numeric IPv4 address string (e.g., "192.0.2.1"); hostname resolution is not performed (inferred from inet_pton equivalence).
addr must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for the resulting IPv4 address.
Return value semantics are not specified here; callers should treat non-success as a parse failure (unknown exact values; inferred from inet_pton pattern).

functions.name: h2o_hpack_encode_int
functions.description: Encodes a non-negative integer using HPACK integer representation into dst and returns a pointer to the byte immediately following the written data. Intended for building HPACK-encoded fields where the first octet has a limited prefix width.
requirements: dst must reference a writable buffer large enough to hold up to H2O_HPACK_ENCODE_INT_MAX_LENGTH bytes (excluding the first-octet space semantics implied by HPACK).
value must be non-negative (HPACK integers are unsigned).
prefix_bits must be in the range 1..8 (typical HPACK usage).
Caller is responsible for placing any first-octet prefix value before invoking this helper (per HPACK encoding pattern).

functions.name: h2o_hpack_encode_huffman
functions.signature: size_t h2o_hpack_encode_huffman(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src, size_t len);
functions.description: Encodes src[0..len) using HPACK static Huffman coding into dst. Returns the encoded byte length, or SIZE_MAX if the encoded output would be longer than the input (in which case the caller can choose to send literal without Huffman).
requirements: dst must reference a writable buffer large enough for the encoded output; the function may return SIZE_MAX instead of writing if encoding would not be smaller.
src must be a valid pointer to len bytes; len may be zero.
Caller must check the return value; SIZE_MAX indicates the caller should not use the (potentially partial) output.

functions.name: h2o_hpack_decode_int
functions.signature: int64_t h2o_hpack_decode_int(const uint8_t **src, const uint8_t *src_end, unsigned prefix_bits);
functions.description: Decodes an HPACK integer from the buffer range [*src, src_end). Advances *src past the decoded integer. Returns the decoded value, or an error code (either H2O_HTTP2_ERROR_COMPRESSION or H2O_HTTP2_ERROR_INCOMPLETE).
requirements: *src must point to the current read position; src_end must point one past the last readable byte; *src <= src_end.
prefix_bits must be in the range 1..8.
Caller must check the return value and handle error codes H2O_HTTP2_ERROR_COMPRESSION or H2O_HTTP2_ERROR_INCOMPLETE appropriately before using the value.
On success, *src is advanced exactly past the encoded integer; on error, advancement may be partial or none (caller should not reuse consumed bytes without handling the error).

functions.name: h2o_hpack_decode_huffman
functions.signature: size_t h2o_hpack_decode_huffman(char *dst, unsigned *soft_errors, const uint8_t *src, size_t len, int is_name, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Decodes an HPACK Huffman-encoded string from src[0..len) into dst and returns the decoded length. Returns SIZE_MAX on hard failure and sets *err_desc to a description. On success, may set bits in *soft_errors (H2O_HPACK_SOFT_ERROR_BIT_INVALID_NAME / H2O_HPACK_SOFT_ERROR_BIT_INVALID_VALUE) if soft validation issues are detected. The is_name flag indicates the input represents a header name (stricter validation).
requirements: dst must reference a writable buffer of at least 2 * len bytes (destination must be at least double the size of the input).
soft_errors must be a valid pointer; the function will set bit flags for soft validation issues on success.
src must be a valid pointer to len bytes; len may be zero.
err_desc must be a valid pointer to receive an error description on hard failure; on success it may be left unchanged.
Caller must check for SIZE_MAX to detect hard failure before using the output.
is_name should be non-zero when decoding a header name and zero for a header value to ensure appropriate validation.

functions.name: h2o_hpack_validate_header_name
functions.signature: int h2o_hpack_validate_header_name(unsigned *soft_errors, const char *s, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Validates an HTTP/2 header field name. Returns non-zero if hard validation succeeds and zero on hard failure. On failure, sets *err_desc to a description. On success, may set bits in *soft_errors to report soft validation issues (e.g., invalid chars reported as soft errors).
requirements: s must point to a buffer of length len bytes (not necessarily NUL-terminated).
soft_errors must be a valid pointer; bits may be set on success to indicate soft issues.
err_desc must be a valid pointer; on hard failure it will be set to a description string.
Caller must check the return value: zero indicates hard failure and the header name must be rejected.
If name validation depends on HPACK rules, pass lowercase, pseudo-header rules, etc., as appropriate; soft error bits H2O_HPACK_SOFT_ERROR_BIT_INVALID_NAME may be set.

functions.name: h2o_hpack_validate_header_value
functions.signature: void h2o_hpack_validate_header_value(unsigned *soft_errors, const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Validates an HTTP/2 header field value for soft validation issues and sets corresponding bits in *soft_errors. There is no hard failure return; the function only reports soft errors.
requirements: s must point to a buffer of length len bytes (not necessarily NUL-terminated).
soft_errors must be a valid pointer; on return, bits such as H2O_HPACK_SOFT_ERROR_BIT_INVALID_VALUE may be set to report issues.
Caller must initialize *soft_errors as desired before calling; this function will OR-in bits as applicable.

functions.name: h2o_hpack_decode_header
functions.signature: int h2o_hpack_decode_header(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, void *_hpack_header_table, h2o_iovec_t **name, h2o_iovec_t *_value, const uint8_t **const src, const uint8_t *src_end, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: HPACK implementation of the h2o_hpack_decode_header_cb callback. Decodes one header field from the HPACK header block in [*src, src_end), updates *src to the new read position, and returns a status code. On error or soft issues, it uses error codes and sets *err_desc to appropriate descriptions. Allocates output name/value using the provided memory pool (as applicable).
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t used to allocate output strings as needed.
_hpack_header_table must point to a valid HPACK dynamic table/context compatible with this implementation.
name must be a valid pointer to receive the allocated header name (may be a pointer to a static token or a pool-allocated buffer as per implementation).
_value must be a valid pointer to receive the header value.
*src must point to the current read position; src_end must be one past the last readable byte; *src <= src_end. The function will advance *src past the decoded header field.
err_desc must be a valid pointer; on errors, an explanatory string will be stored.
Caller must honor the callback contract: check the returned int for success vs error/soft error codes, and handle *err_desc accordingly before proceeding.

functions.name: h2o_hpack_parse_request
functions.signature: int h2o_hpack_parse_request(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_hpack_decode_header_cb decode_cb, void *decode_ctx, h2o_iovec_t *method, const h2o_url_scheme_t **scheme, h2o_iovec_t *authority, h2o_iovec_t *path, h2o_iovec_t *protocol, h2o_headers_t *headers, int *pseudo_header_exists_map, size_t *content_length, h2o_iovec_t *expect, h2o_cache_digests_t **digests, h2o_iovec_t *datagram_flow_id, const uint8_t *src, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses an HPACK-encoded request header block using the provided decode_cb. Populates method, scheme, authority, path, optional protocol, regular headers, and auxiliary outputs (content_length, expect, cache digests, DATAGRAM flow ID). Tracks presence of HTTP/2 request pseudo-headers via pseudo_header_exists_map bits. Returns a status code and sets *err_desc on error.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t for allocations.
decode_cb must implement h2o_hpack_decode_header_cb semantics (indicate soft errors using error codes and set *err_desc appropriately).
decode_ctx is passed through to decode_cb and must be appropriate for that decoder.
method, scheme, authority, path, protocol, headers, pseudo_header_exists_map, content_length, expect, digests, datagram_flow_id must be valid pointers to receive parsed results.
pseudo_header_exists_map will be updated with bitwise OR of H2O_HPACK_PARSE_HEADERS_{METHOD,SCHEME,PATH,AUTHORITY,PROTOCOL}_EXISTS as pseudo-headers are seen.
src must point to the HPACK-compressed header block of length len bytes; the function will iterate until the block is fully consumed by decode_cb.

Caller must check the return code and use *err_desc to surface parsing/validation errors (including missing/invalid mandatory pseudo-headers, invalid content-length, connection-specific header, uppercase in names, etc., as signaled by underlying code).

functions.name: h2o_hpack_parse_response
functions.signature: int h2o_hpack_parse_response(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_hpack_decode_header_cb decode_cb, void *decode_ctx, int *status, h2o_headers_t *headers, h2o_iovec_t *datagram_flow_id, const uint8_t *src, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses an HPACK-encoded response header block using the provided decode_cb. Extracts the :status pseudo-header into status and collects regular headers and optional DATAGRAM flow ID. Returns a status code and sets *err_desc on error.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t for allocations.
decode_cb must implement h2o_hpack_decode_header_cb semantics (indicate soft errors via codes and set *err_desc).
decode_ctx is opaque and passed through to decode_cb as its context.
status, headers, datagram_flow_id must be valid pointers to receive parsed results.
src must point to the HPACK-compressed header block of length len bytes; the function will repeatedly call decode_cb to consume it.
Caller must check the return code and use *err_desc on errors (compression/format issues, invalid headers, etc.).

functions.name: h2o_http1_accept
functions.signature: void h2o_http1_accept(h2o_accept_ctx_t *ctx, h2o_socket_t *sock, struct timeval connected_at);
functions.description: Accepts and initializes handling of a new HTTP/1.x connection for the H2O server. Intended to be called by the listener/accept loop after a socket is accepted. The function associates the accepted socket with the provided accept context and records the connection time.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized h2o_accept_ctx_t pointer associated with the listener/reactor that will manage the connection.
sock must be a valid, open, non-null h2o_socket_t representing a newly accepted connection; it must be ready for I/O as expected by H2O (typically non-blocking).
connected_at must be a valid struct timeval value indicating when the connection was established; its fields should contain a sensible timestamp.
This function should be called once per accepted socket, before any HTTP I/O is attempted on that socket.
Pointers passed (ctx, sock) must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: h2o_http1_upgrade
functions.signature: void h2o_http1_upgrade(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_iovec_t *inbufs, size_t inbufcnt, h2o_http1_upgrade_cb on_complete, void *user_data);
functions.description: Performs an HTTP/1.x protocol upgrade (e.g., switching protocols per an Upgrade request header) on the given request. Any already-received, unconsumed bytes for the upgraded protocol can be supplied via inbufs/inbufcnt. When the upgrade is finalized, the on_complete callback (typedef: void (*h2o_http1_upgrade_cb)(void *user_data, h2o_socket_t *sock, size_t reqsize)) is invoked with the resulting socket and context information.
requirements: req must be a valid, currently active h2o_req_t corresponding to an HTTP/1.x request eligible for upgrade.
inbufs must either be NULL with inbufcnt == 0, or point to an array of h2o_iovec_t of length inbufcnt containing any initial bytes for the upgraded protocol.
inbufcnt must accurately reflect the number of elements in inbufs; zero is allowed.
on_complete, if non-NULL, must be a function matching h2o_http1_upgrade_cb and must be safe to call from the H2O event loop context; it may be called asynchronously as part of the upgrade completion.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed through unchanged to on_complete; if used, it must remain valid until the callback is invoked.
The function should be called at most once per request for a single upgrade transaction.

functions.signature: void h2o_hpack_flatten_push_promise(h2o_buffer_t **buf, h2o_hpack_header_table_t *header_table, uint32_t hpack_capacity, uint32_t stream_id, size_t max_frame_size, const h2o_url_scheme_t *scheme, h2o_iovec_t authority, h2o_iovec_t method, h2o_iovec_t path, const h2o_header_t *headers, size_t num_headers, uint32_t parent_stream_id);

requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/2 connection.

If the stream is blocked_by_server, the implementation will clear that flag during END_STREAM transition (based on inline state machine).

functions.name: h2o_http2_stream_reset
functions.description: Resets the stream, aborting it and signaling a reset condition (e.g., by sending RST_STREAM to the peer and cleaning up local state).
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/2 connection.
stream must be a valid stream associated with conn.
Use when terminating the stream due to error or policy; subsequent operations on the stream are not allowed.

functions.name: h2o_http2_stream_send_pending_data
functions.description: Attempts to send any data buffered on the stream (stream->_data) subject to flow control and scheduling. Intended to flush pending sendvecs into HTTP/2 DATA frames.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/2 connection with write buffers initialized.
stream must be a valid stream associated with conn.
Stream should have pending data (h2o_http2_stream_has_pending_data(stream) != 0) to have effect; otherwise call may be a no-op.
Peer flow-control window and connection buffer/window must allow sending; otherwise data may remain pending.

functions.name: h2o_http2_stream_proceed
functions.description: Advances a stream’s send/receive state machine, typically invoked when more data is available, flow-control allows progress, or after being scheduled via the proceed callback registration.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/2 connection.
stream must be a valid stream associated with conn.
Usually called after h2o_http2_conn_register_for_proceed_callback or when new output/state is ready; calling with no pending work is a no-op.

functions.name: h2o_http2_get_debug_state
functions.description: Produces a debug snapshot for the given request’s HTTP/2 state, optionally including HPACK-related information when hpack_enabled is non-zero. Useful for diagnostics and observability.
requirements: req must point to a valid, initialized h2o_req_t associated with an HTTP/2 stream/connection.
hpack_enabled is an integer flag; non-zero enables inclusion of HPACK details.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned h2o_http2_debug_state_t is unknown; caller may need to free it or treat it as ephemeral depending on implementation (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_init
functions.description: Initializes an HTTP/2 priority scheduler root node. Use this on the root node of a dependency tree before opening any stream references. Unknown whether it zeroes internal lists beyond establishing an empty tree.
requirements: root must point to a valid, writable h2o_http2_scheduler_node_t storage that will serve as the scheduler root
Must be called before using the node with other scheduler APIs
The node memory must outlive all references that will be attached to it

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of the scheduler data associated with the given root node. Intended to clean up internal structures after all streams (open references) are closed.
requirements: All open references belonging to the node must be closed before calling this function (explicitly stated)
root must point to a previously initialized scheduler root
Do not use the root with other scheduler APIs after disposal unless re-initialized

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_open
functions.signature: void h2o_http2_scheduler_open(h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t *ref, h2o_http2_scheduler_node_t *parent, uint16_t weight, int exclusive);
functions.description: Opens (registers) a stream reference in the scheduler with the specified parent dependency, weight, and exclusivity. Used when a new HTTP/2 stream becomes tracked by the scheduler.
requirements: ref must point to writable storage for an h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t that is not already open
parent must be a valid node in the same scheduler tree (typically the root or another open reference's node)
weight is a 16-bit value; exact valid range beyond the type is unknown from this header
exclusive determines exclusive reprioritization semantics; details are not documented here
The lifetime of ref must extend until it is closed (and any relocation completed)

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_close
functions.description: Closes a previously opened reference (stream) in the scheduler. Any dependents of the closed reference are reattached to the closed reference’s parent.
requirements: ref must refer to a currently open reference (i.e., previously opened and not yet closed)
After closing, ref must not be used with other scheduler APIs except potential relocation that has already been performed (details unknown)

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_relocate
functions.description: Relocates an open reference’s scheduler bookkeeping from src to dst (e.g., when the enclosing object moves in memory). Intended to update internal links to a new memory location for the same logical stream.
requirements: src must refer to an existing open reference
dst must be valid writable storage and not already part of the scheduler (fresh/unlinked)
After relocation, callers should stop using src and use dst instead
Exact constraints on when during stream lifecycle relocation may occur are not documented

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_rebind
functions.signature: void h2o_http2_scheduler_rebind(h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t *ref, h2o_http2_scheduler_node_t *new_parent, uint16_t weight, int exclusive);
functions.description: Reprioritizes an open reference by rebinding it to a new parent with a new weight and optional exclusivity, following HTTP/2 priority rules.
requirements: ref must refer to a currently open reference
new_parent must be a valid node in the same scheduler tree
weight is a 16-bit value; precise acceptable range beyond type is unknown here
exclusive applies HTTP/2 exclusive dependency semantics; exact behavior not detailed in this header

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_is_open
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the reference is currently open (linked into the scheduler), otherwise 0. Implemented by checking whether ref->_all_link is linked.
requirements: ref must be a valid pointer to an h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t
Safe to call regardless of open/closed state

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_get_weight
functions.description: Returns the current scheduling weight associated with the reference.
requirements: ref must be a valid pointer to an h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t that has an initialized weight (typically an open reference)

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_get_parent
functions.description: Returns the current parent node of the reference in the dependency tree. May be NULL if the node is the root.
requirements: ref must be a valid pointer to an h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t
Returned pointer may be NULL for a root node; callers must handle NULL

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_activate
functions.description: Marks a reference as active so it can be selected and passed to the callback during h2o_http2_scheduler_run when resources are allocated.
requirements: ref must refer to an open reference
Repeated activations on an already active reference are not documented; behavior unknown

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_deactivate
functions.description: Deactivates a reference while keeping it in the scheduler, preventing it from being selected by h2o_http2_scheduler_run until reactivated.
requirements: ref must refer to an open reference
It is intended for previously activated references; effect on an already inactive reference is not documented

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_run
functions.description: Traverses the dependency tree and invokes cb for active references in priority/weight order. The callback can consume resources, decide if the reference remains active via still_is_active, and return non-zero to stop traversal.
requirements: root must be a valid scheduler root node
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with: (h2o_http2_scheduler_openref_t *ref, int *still_is_active, void *cb_arg)
The callback should set *still_is_active to indicate whether ref remains active after the call
The callback may return non-zero to stop traversal, or 0 to continue
cb_arg is passed through unchanged to the callback

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_is_active
functions.description: Returns whether there are any active entries in the scheduler. May return false positives, but no false negatives (i.e., if it returns 0, there are definitely no active entries).
requirements: root must be a valid scheduler node (typically the root)
Callers must tolerate potential false positives

functions.name: h2o_http2_scheduler_find_parent_by_weight
functions.description: Finds and returns a parent node whose weight is >= new_weight, or returns root if none exists. Intended for trees generated by Chromium: a linear dependency chain ordered by descending weight.
requirements: root must be a valid scheduler root for the tree being examined
new_weight is a 16-bit value; exact semantics beyond comparison are not specified here

The algorithm assumes a Chromium-style priority tree: (1) streams form a linear list (each stream has at most one child), and (2) the list is ordered in descending weight; results are meaningful under this assumption

functions.name: h2o_http3_priority_update_frame_capacity
functions.description: Computes the number of bytes required to encode a PRIORITY_UPDATE frame for the given frame object (including type and length fields as applicable). Intended for sizing buffers before encoding.
requirements: frame must point to a valid, initialized h2o_http3_priority_update_frame_t instance
The frame's value field (h2o_iovec_t) should reference the priority field-value to be encoded

functions.name: h2o_http3_encode_priority_update_frame
functions.description: Encodes a PRIORITY_UPDATE frame into the buffer at dst. Returns a pointer to the position just past the last written byte (typical buffer writer pattern).
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the frame as determined by h2o_http3_priority_update_frame_capacity(frame)
frame must be a valid, initialized pointer; its fields (element_is_push, element, value) must contain the data to encode

functions.name: h2o_http3_decode_priority_update_frame
functions.signature: int h2o_http3_decode_priority_update_frame(h2o_http3_priority_update_frame_t *frame, int is_push, const uint8_t *payload, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses a PRIORITY_UPDATE frame payload into frame. The is_push flag tells whether the element refers to a push stream. On error, returns a non-zero value and optionally sets err_desc to a message.
requirements: payload must point to the start of the PRIORITY_UPDATE frame payload and contain len bytes
frame must be non-NULL and writable
err_desc may be NULL if caller does not need error detail; otherwise must be a valid pointer to receive a static or ephemeral error string
is_push should be non-zero when decoding PRIORITY_UPDATE_PUSH and zero for PRIORITY_UPDATE_REQUEST (inferred from naming)

functions.name: h2o_http3_goaway_frame_capacity
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes needed to encode a GOAWAY frame for the provided stream or push ID (including type/length as applicable). Use to pre-size output buffers.
requirements: stream_or_push_id must be the ID that will be encoded into the GOAWAY frame

functions.name: h2o_http3_encode_goaway_frame
functions.description: Encodes a GOAWAY frame carrying stream_or_push_id into buff. Returns a pointer advanced past the written frame.
requirements: buff must point to a writable buffer large enough for the frame as indicated by h2o_http3_goaway_frame_capacity(stream_or_push_id)
stream_or_push_id must be the intended last accepted stream/push ID for GOAWAY semantics

functions.name: h2o_http3_decode_goaway_frame
functions.signature: int h2o_http3_decode_goaway_frame(h2o_http3_goaway_frame_t *frame, const uint8_t *payload, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Decodes a GOAWAY frame payload into frame. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on error, optionally setting err_desc.
requirements: payload must address len bytes that comprise the GOAWAY payload
frame must be a valid, writable pointer
err_desc may be NULL if error detail is not required; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to receive an error description

functions.name: h2o_quic_send_datagrams
functions.signature: int h2o_quic_send_datagrams(h2o_quic_ctx_t *ctx, quicly_address_t *dest, quicly_address_t *src, struct iovec *datagrams, size_t num_datagrams);
functions.description: Sends one or more UDP datagrams from source address src to destination dest using the QUIC context. Returns a boolean indicating if the connection remains maintainable (false if the designated source address cannot be used). When sending more than one datagram, all datagrams except the last must have the same size to allow use of UDP GSO.
requirements: ctx must be initialized via h2o_quic_init_context
dest and src must point to valid, initialized addresses suitable for sendmsg
datagrams must point to an array of iovec entries describing buffers to send; num_datagrams specifies the count
If num_datagrams > 1, the sizes of all datagrams except the last must be equal (GSO requirement per comment)

functions.name: h2o_http3_on_create_unidirectional_stream
functions.description: Creates and initializes an HTTP/3 unidirectional stream object bound to the provided quicly stream (e.g., control, QPACK encoder/decoder, or push stream). Intended to be called when a unidirectional stream is created.
requirements: qs must be a valid quicly_stream_t pointer representing a newly created unidirectional stream

functions.name: h2o_http3_read_frame
functions.signature: int h2o_http3_read_frame(h2o_http3_read_frame_t *frame, int is_client, uint64_t stream_type, size_t max_frame_payload_size, const uint8_t **src, const uint8_t *src_end, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses data from [*src, src_end) as an HTTP/3 frame. For DATA frames it may return only the header; for other frames it can return the complete frame. On success, updates frame with the parsed information and advances *src past consumed bytes. On error, returns non-zero and may set err_desc.
requirements: frame must be a valid, writable pointer
src must point to a pointer to the current read position; on success it may be advanced; src_end must be the end pointer of the available buffer
max_frame_payload_size limits the maximum frame payload parsed; callers should set an appropriate bound to avoid excessive memory use
is_client indicates the endpoint role for context-dependent validation; stream_type must be the stream type on which the frame is being read
err_desc may be NULL if error details are not needed; otherwise must be a valid pointer

functions.name: h2o_quic_init_context
functions.signature: void h2o_quic_init_context(h2o_quic_ctx_t *ctx, h2o_loop_t *loop, h2o_socket_t *sock, quicly_context_t *quic, quicly_cid_plaintext_t *next_cid, h2o_quic_accept_cb acceptor, h2o_quic_notify_connection_update_cb notify_conn_update, uint8_t use_gso, h2o_quic_stats_t *quic_stats);
functions.description: Initializes the QUIC runtime context, binding the event loop, UDP socket, quicly context, CID seed, callbacks, and options. next_cid should be thread-local CID seed to use for connections.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable context object
loop must be a valid event loop instance
sock must be a valid, open UDP socket wrapped by h2o_socket_t
quic must be a valid quicly_context_t configured for the application
next_cid should point to thread-local CID seed storage as described in the comment
acceptor and notify_conn_update callbacks are optional per comment; they may be NULL
use_gso is a flag indicating whether to use UDP GSO
quic_stats may be NULL or a valid stats object to accumulate counters

functions.name: h2o_quic_dispose_context
functions.description: Disposes and cleans up resources associated with a previously initialized QUIC context.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via h2o_quic_init_context
After disposal, ctx must not be used until re-initialized

functions.name: h2o_quic_set_forwarding_context
functions.signature: void h2o_quic_set_forwarding_context(h2o_quic_ctx_t *ctx, uint32_t accept_thread_divisor, uint8_t ttl, h2o_quic_forward_packets_cb forward_cb, h2o_quic_preprocess_packet_cb preprocess_cb);
functions.description: Configures the context for packet forwarding between threads/nodes with encapsulation. Registers callbacks to forward packets and optionally preprocess forwarded datagrams, and adjusts context parameters to support forwarding.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized via h2o_quic_init_context
forward_cb may be NULL if forwarding is not used; preprocess_cb is optional (may be NULL)
accept_thread_divisor controls load distribution (0 disables internal distribution per earlier field comment)
ttl is used to prevent infinite forwarding loops (value semantics not otherwise constrained in the header)

functions.name: h2o_quic_read_socket
functions.description: Reads and processes incoming QUIC datagrams from the given socket within the provided context, driving connection input handling.
requirements: ctx must be initialized
sock must be the underlying unbound UDP socket associated with the context (or otherwise a valid socket to read from)

functions.name: h2o_quic_close_connection
functions.signature: void h2o_quic_close_connection(h2o_quic_conn_t *conn, quicly_error_t err, const char *reason_phrase);
functions.description: Closes a specific QUIC connection with the given application or transport error code and an optional reason phrase.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection initialized via h2o_quic_init_conn/h2o_quic_setup
err must be a valid quicly_error_t (may be 0 or an application-mapped error code)
reason_phrase may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string; if provided, it should remain valid for the duration of the close operation (exact ownership unspecified)

functions.name: h2o_quic_close_all_connections
functions.description: Closes all active QUIC connections tracked by the context.
requirements: ctx must be initialized
Caller should ensure this is appropriate for the application's shutdown or error state

functions.name: h2o_quic_num_connections
functions.description: Returns the number of QUIC connections currently tracked by the context.
requirements: ctx must be initialized

functions.name: h2o_quic_init_conn
functions.description: Initializes a connection wrapper object and associates it with the QUIC context and callbacks.
requirements: conn must be a valid, writable object
ctx must be initialized and remain alive for the lifetime of conn
callbacks must point to a valid callbacks vtable for lifecycle hooks

functions.name: h2o_quic_dispose_conn
functions.description: Disposes resources held by a connection wrapper object.
requirements: conn must have been initialized via h2o_quic_init_conn
After disposal, conn must not be used unless re-initialized

functions.name: h2o_quic_setup
functions.description: Binds an initialized wrapper connection to an underlying quicly_conn_t instance, completing transport setup.
requirements: conn must be initialized via h2o_quic_init_conn
quic must be a valid quicly_conn_t returned/created by the quicly stack

functions.name: h2o_http3_init_conn
functions.signature: void h2o_http3_init_conn(h2o_http3_conn_t *conn, h2o_quic_ctx_t *ctx, const h2o_http3_conn_callbacks_t *callbacks, const h2o_http3_qpack_context_t *qpack_ctx, size_t max_frame_payload_size);
functions.description: Initializes an HTTP/3 connection object layered on a QUIC connection. Sets callbacks, QPACK context, and the maximum frame payload size (which effectively bounds HEADERS frame size).
requirements: conn must be a valid, writable h2o_http3_conn_t
ctx must be an initialized QUIC context
callbacks must be a valid callback table for HTTP/3 events
qpack_ctx must be provided to configure encoder/decoder behavior
max_frame_payload_size must be chosen so that stream-level flow control credit is at least h2o_http3_calc_min_flow_control_size(max_frame_payload_size), per the comment on the field

functions.name: h2o_http3_dispose_conn
functions.description: Cleans up an HTTP/3 connection object and associated resources (including QPACK state and control streams).
requirements: conn must have been initialized via h2o_http3_init_conn
Do not use conn after disposal without re-initializing

functions.name: h2o_http3_setup
functions.description: Completes HTTP/3 setup on top of a created QUIC connection, wiring protocol state and control streams. Returns 0 on success or a QUIC/HTTP3 error code on failure.
requirements: conn must be initialized via h2o_http3_init_conn
quic must be a valid, established or establishing quicly connection to bind to
Caller must handle non-zero return values as errors

functions.name: h2o_quic_send
functions.description: Immediately sends pending QUIC packets for the given connection (invokes quicly_send and underlying sendmsg). The comment mentions boolean semantics about connection survival; the function returns a quicly_error_t indicating success (0) or an error code.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection set up via h2o_quic_setup
Caller should handle non-zero return values as send/connection errors

functions.name: h2o_http3_update_recvbuf
functions.signature: void h2o_http3_update_recvbuf(h2o_buffer_t **buf, size_t off, const void *src, size_t len);
functions.description: Updates or appends data into an HTTP/3 receive buffer, starting at offset off, copying len bytes from src. Utility to manage stream buffering.
requirements: buf must be a valid pointer to an h2o_buffer_t* (buffer may be NULL depending on implementation)
src must point to at least len bytes of readable memory
off must be within or adjacent to the current buffer extent as required by the implementation (exact constraints not specified)

functions.name: h2o_quic_schedule_timer
functions.description: Schedules the transport timer for a connection. Applications must call this when they write data, though it is also called automatically when packets are sent or received.
requirements: conn must be a valid, initialized connection
Caller should invoke after writing application data to ensure timely timeouts

functions.name: h2o_http3_handle_settings_frame
functions.signature: int h2o_http3_handle_settings_frame(h2o_http3_conn_t *conn, const uint8_t *payload, size_t length, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses and applies an incoming HTTP/3 SETTINGS frame to the connection (peer settings). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error and may set err_desc.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection
payload must reference length bytes of a SETTINGS frame payload
err_desc may be NULL if not needed; otherwise must be a valid pointer to receive an error description

functions.name: h2o_http3_send_qpack_stream_cancel
functions.description: Enqueues a QPACK Stream Cancellation instruction for the given request stream ID to inform the encoder/decoder that the stream is no longer needed.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection with QPACK set up
stream_id must identify the request stream being canceled

functions.name: h2o_http3_send_qpack_header_ack
functions.description: Enqueues a QPACK Header Acknowledgement for a header block (bytes/len).
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection with QPACK set up
bytes must point to len bytes corresponding to the header block being acknowledged

functions.name: h2o_http3_send_shutdown_goaway_frame
functions.description: Enqueues a GOAWAY frame crafted for graceful shutdown, signaling clients not to initiate new requests.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection

functions.name: h2o_http3_send_goaway_frame
functions.description: Enqueues a GOAWAY frame conveying the specified last stream or push ID.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection
stream_or_push_id must be the intended ID limit to advertise to the peer

functions.name: h2o_http3_send_h3_datagrams
functions.signature: void h2o_http3_send_h3_datagrams(h2o_http3_conn_t *conn, uint64_t flow_id, h2o_iovec_t *datagrams, size_t num_datagrams);
functions.description: Sends one or more RFC 9297 HTTP/3 DATAGRAMs on the given connection with the specified flow_id. To send RFC 9298-style UDP payloads, include Context ID 0 in the payload.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection
datagrams must point to an array of h2o_iovec_t buffers; num_datagrams is the count
For RFC 9298-style usage, the application must include Context ID 0 in the payload as noted in the comment
It is inferred that H3 datagrams should only be used if negotiated/allowed (peer_settings.h3_datagram)

functions.name: h2o_http3_decode_h3_datagram
functions.signature: uint64_t h2o_http3_decode_h3_datagram(h2o_iovec_t *payload, const void *_src, size_t len);
functions.description: Decodes an HTTP/3 datagram from the provided bytes. On success, returns the flow ID and sets *payload to the datagram payload; on failure, returns UINT64_MAX.
