requirements: _src must point to len bytes comprising a candidate H3 datagram
payload must be a valid, writable h2o_iovec_t pointer to receive the decoded payload slice
Caller must check for return value UINT64_MAX to detect decode failure

functions.name: h2o_http3_has_received_settings
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the connection has received peer HTTP/3 SETTINGS (specifically, if QPACK encoder state is initialized). Inline implementation returns whether conn->qpack.enc is non-NULL.
requirements: conn must be a valid HTTP/3 connection object

functions.name: h2o_http3_calc_min_flow_control_size
functions.description: Given a maximum allowed HEADERS block payload size, computes the minimum stream-level flow control credit that must be guaranteed so that a complete frame can be received (8 bytes for type + 8 bytes for length + payload).
requirements: max_headers_length is the maximum header block size the application expects to receive in a single frame

functions.name: h2o_http3_server_init_context
functions.signature: void h2o_http3_server_init_context(h2o_context_t *h2o, h2o_quic_ctx_t *ctx, h2o_loop_t *loop, h2o_socket_t *sock, quicly_context_t *quic, quicly_cid_plaintext_t *next_cid, h2o_quic_accept_cb acceptor, h2o_quic_notify_connection_update_cb notify_conn_update, uint8_t use_gso)
functions.description: Initializes HTTP/3 server-side QUIC context and wiring with the H2O event loop, listening socket, and QUIC (quicly) context. Typical usage is to call this during server startup to prepare QUIC/HTTP3 handling, providing the event loop, listening socket, QUIC context, the next CID seed, and accept/notify callbacks. The use_gso flag enables/disables Generic Segmentation Offload when supported.
requirements: h2o must point to a valid, initialized h2o_context_t.
ctx must be a valid h2o_quic_ctx_t storage that will be initialized by this call.
loop must be a valid h2o_loop_t associated with the process event loop.
sock must be a valid, open h2o_socket_t bound to the listening address for QUIC traffic.
quic must be a valid, configured quicly_context_t to be used by the server (typically amended for server use beforehand).
next_cid must point to a valid quicly_cid_plaintext_t used as the initial/next connection ID seed.
acceptor must be a valid function pointer of type h2o_quic_accept_cb.
notify_conn_update must be a valid function pointer of type h2o_quic_notify_connection_update_cb (or NULL if permitted by the API; not specified here).
use_gso should be 0 or 1 to disable/enable GSO; values are treated as a boolean.

functions.name: h2o_http3_server_accept
functions.signature: h2o_http3_conn_t *h2o_http3_server_accept(h2o_http3_server_ctx_t *ctx, quicly_address_t *destaddr, quicly_address_t *srcaddr, quicly_decoded_packet_t *packet, quicly_address_token_plaintext_t *address_token, const h2o_http3_conn_callbacks_t *h3_callbacks)
functions.description: Acceptor callback for HTTP/3: processes an incoming decoded QUIC packet and, on success, creates and returns a new HTTP/3 connection bound to the provided server context. On failure, returns NULL or the special value H2O_QUIC_ACCEPT_CONN_DECRYPTION_FAILED. Use this as the accept callback in the QUIC I/O path for HTTP/3 traffic.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized h2o_http3_server_ctx_t intended for server use with HTTP/3.
destaddr and srcaddr must point to valid quicly_address_t structures representing destination and source addresses of the packet.
packet must point to a valid quicly_decoded_packet_t representing the received QUIC packet.
address_token may point to a valid quicly_address_token_plaintext_t if address validation is used; NULL may be acceptable depending on configuration (not specified here).
h3_callbacks must point to a valid h2o_http3_conn_callbacks_t table for connection-level callbacks.
Callers must check the return value: it may be NULL or H2O_QUIC_ACCEPT_CONN_DECRYPTION_FAILED on failure and a valid h2o_http3_conn_t* on success. Do not dereference on failure.

functions.name: h2o_http3_server_amend_quicly_context
functions.description: Adjusts (amends) a quicly_context_t so it is suitable for HTTP/3 server operation under the given H2O global configuration. Call this before using the quicly context to accept or create server-side QUIC connections for HTTP/3.
requirements: conf must point to a valid, initialized h2o_globalconf_t representing the server configuration.
quic must point to a valid quicly_context_t that will be modified for server use.
Should be called before the quicly context is used to handle server connections (inferred from the function’s purpose).

functions.name: h2o_http3_get_connection
functions.description: Returns the application-level H2O connection object (h2o_conn_t) associated with a given QUIC connection. Intended for QUIC connections that back HTTP/3 server responses; not for client or non-HTTP uses.
requirements: quic must be a valid quicly_conn_t associated with an HTTP/3 server connection managed by H2O.
Caller must not supply QUIC connections used for purposes other than serving HTTP responses (e.g., connections created by http3client), as explicitly documented.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient_connection_pool_init
functions.description: Initializes a per-thread HTTP client connection pool, associating it with a (possibly shared) socket pool used to establish and reuse HTTP/1 connections. Use this before issuing requests that should reuse connections via the pool.
requirements: connpool must be a valid, writable pointer to an uninitialized or reset h2o_httpclient_connection_pool_t instance.
sockpool must point to a valid, initialized h2o_socketpool_t; it may be shared across threads, while connpool is per-thread.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient_connect
functions.signature: void h2o_httpclient_connect(h2o_httpclient_t **client, h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, void *data, h2o_httpclient_ctx_t *ctx, h2o_httpclient_connection_pool_t *connpool, h2o_url_t *target, const char *upgrade_to, h2o_httpclient_connect_cb on_connect);
functions.description: Issues a HTTP request using the provided connection pool and client context. The function selects HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 (and possibly HTTP/3 via context) per policy and invokes on_connect when the protocol stack is ready for the application to provide request fields. If upgrade_to is non-NULL, it influences Upgrade or extended CONNECT behavior.
requirements: client must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive/hold the client handle; the pointer it points to may be NULL on entry.
pool must be a valid memory pool that remains alive for the lifetime of the client/request.
ctx must be a valid, initialized h2o_httpclient_ctx_t with desired timeouts and protocol settings.
connpool must be a valid, initialized h2o_httpclient_connection_pool_t when using pooled connections.
target must be a valid, initialized h2o_url_t designating the request URL.
on_connect must be a valid function pointer; it will be called back by the stack to obtain request parameters.
upgrade_to may be NULL; if non-NULL, it is a protocol label (e.g., h2o_httpclient_upgrade_to_connect) directing Upgrade/CONNECT behavior.

The application must set all output parameters requested by on_connect (method, url, headers, body, proceed_req_cb, props, origin) before returning from on_connect, as documented in the header comments.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient__h1_on_connect
functions.description: Internal hook invoked when an HTTP/1 connection is established. Binds the client to the underlying socket and origin for issuing a request over HTTP/1.
requirements: client must be a valid, initialized h2o_httpclient_t.
sock must be a valid, connected h2o_socket_t representing the HTTP/1 TCP connection.
origin must be a valid h2o_url_t describing the origin (path ignored), as indicated by the comment for H2; similar expectation applies.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient__h2_on_connect
functions.description: Internal hook invoked when an HTTP/2 connection is established. Attaches the client to the H2 socket and origin so the request can be sent over an existing or new H2 session.
requirements: client must be a valid, initialized h2o_httpclient_t.
sock must be a valid, connected h2o_socket_t carrying the HTTP/2 connection (TLS/ALPN as applicable).
origin must be a valid h2o_url_t describing the origin server; for H2, the path is ignored per the connection struct comment.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient__h2_get_max_concurrent_streams
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of concurrent streams permitted on the given HTTP/2 client connection. Useful for scheduling or pooling decisions.
requirements: conn must be a valid pointer to an active h2o_httpclient__h2_conn_t.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient_set_conn_properties_of_socket
functions.description: Populates h2o_httpclient_conn_properties_t with details obtained from the underlying socket (e.g., TLS protocol version, cipher, session reuse, and the socket pointer). Use to query connection/TLS properties for diagnostics or telemetry.
requirements: sock must be a valid h2o_socket_t (the underlying TCP/TLS connection), if any.
properties must be a valid, writable pointer to h2o_httpclient_conn_properties_t.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient_http3_notify_connection_update
functions.description: HTTP/3-specific API: notifies the HTTP/3 client implementation that the QUIC connection’s state has updated. Allows the client to react to QUIC-level events. Available only when built with QUIC/HTTP3 support (quicly_h defined).
requirements: This function is available only when quicly_h is defined (i.e., HTTP/3 support compiled in).
ctx must be a valid h2o_quic_ctx_t for the QUIC/HTTP3 stack.
conn must be a valid h2o_quic_conn_t representing the QUIC connection.

functions.name: h2o_httpclient__connect_h3
functions.signature: void h2o_httpclient__connect_h3(h2o_httpclient_t **client, h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, void *data, h2o_httpclient_ctx_t *ctx, h2o_httpclient_connection_pool_t *connpool, h2o_url_t *target, const char *upgrade_to, h2o_httpclient_connect_cb cb);
functions.description: Internal HTTP/3 connection routine: initiates an HTTP/3 request over QUIC using the provided context and connection pool, then invokes cb when ready for the application to supply request parameters. Available only when built with HTTP/3 (quicly_h defined).
requirements: Available only when quicly_h is defined at compile time.
client must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive/hold the client handle; the pointed value may be NULL on entry.
pool must be a valid memory pool that outlives the request.
ctx must be a valid, initialized h2o_httpclient_ctx_t with its http3 field configured.
connpool must be a valid, initialized h2o_httpclient_connection_pool_t appropriate for HTTP/3 usage.
target must be a valid, initialized h2o_url_t for the destination.
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be called to obtain request parameters.
upgrade_to may be NULL or a protocol label (e.g., h2o_httpclient_upgrade_to_connect).

functions.name: h2o_httpclient__tunnel_is_ready
functions.signature: static int h2o_httpclient__tunnel_is_ready(h2o_httpclient_t *client, int status, int http_version);
functions.description: Internal helper that determines if the HTTP stream should transition to a tunnel (e.g., Upgrade or extended CONNECT). It returns 1 if client->upgrade_to is set and the response/status indicates a successful upgrade/tunnel: for HTTP/1.x, 101 Switching Protocols or 2xx when using CONNECT; for HTTP/2+, 2xx; otherwise 0. Implemented as a static inline in the header.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer; client->upgrade_to may be NULL.
status is the HTTP response status code; for CONNECT (upgrade_to == h2o_httpclient_upgrade_to_connect) a 2xx indicates readiness.
http_version is compared numerically with 0x200 (HTTP/2 threshold); values < 0x200 are treated as HTTP/1.x.

functions.name: h2o_linklist_init_anchor
functions.description: Initializes a list anchor (sentinel/head) for the intrusive circular doubly linked list. After calling, anchor->next and anchor->prev point to the anchor itself, representing an empty list. Typical usage: declare an h2o_linklist_t to serve as the head and call this once before using the list.
requirements: anchor must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
anchor must designate the list head (anchor).
Must be called before any other list operations that use this anchor.

functions.name: h2o_linklist_is_empty
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the list designated by the given anchor (head) is empty, i.e., when anchor->next == anchor. Intended to be used on a list head initialized by h2o_linklist_init_anchor.
requirements: anchor must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
anchor must have been initialized with h2o_linklist_init_anchor.

functions.name: h2o_linklist_is_linked
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the node is currently linked into some list (i.e., node->next != NULL). Newly initialized/zero-filled nodes will return false until inserted; nodes become unlinked again after h2o_linklist_unlink sets next/prev to NULL.
requirements: node must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
Nodes should be zero-filled upon initialization (per header comment) so that an unlinked node has next == NULL.

functions.name: h2o_linklist_insert
functions.description: Inserts node into the list immediately before pos. Works with an anchor (to insert at the tail when pos is the anchor) or with any existing node. The operation is O(1).
requirements: pos must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an element that is currently linked into a properly initialized list (either the list anchor or a node).
node must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
node must not be currently linked into any list (asserts that h2o_linklist_is_linked(node) is false; i.e., node->next == NULL).
The list containing pos must have been initialized (its anchor initialized with h2o_linklist_init_anchor).
Do not reuse node in another list until it has been unlinked.

functions.name: h2o_linklist_insert_list
functions.description: Splices (moves) all elements from the list anchored by list and inserts them before pos in O(1), leaving list empty (reinitialized). If list is empty, this is a no-op. This is a list-to-list splice; elements are not copied.
requirements: pos must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an element currently linked into a properly initialized destination list (either its anchor or a node).
list must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a list anchor (head) that has been initialized with h2o_linklist_init_anchor.
list must designate a list anchor, not a regular node; passing a non-anchor node as list will corrupt lists.
It is permitted for list to be empty; in that case, the function returns without modification.
After the call, list is reinitialized (empty) and must not be assumed to still reference its previous elements.

functions.name: h2o_linklist_unlink
functions.description: Unlinks a node from the list it is part of, fixing neighbor links and then setting node->next and node->prev to NULL to mark it as unlinked. O(1).
requirements: node must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node that is currently linked into a list (node->next and node->prev must be non-NULL and consistent).
node must not be the list anchor (unlinking an anchor would break the list invariants).
After unlinking, node is considered unlinked (node->next == NULL) and may be inserted into a list again.

functions.name: h2o_memcached_create_context
functions.signature: h2o_memcached_context_t *h2o_memcached_create_context(const char *host, uint16_t port, int text_protocol, size_t num_threads, const char *prefix);
functions.description: Creates and returns a memcached client context configured to talk to the given host:port. The context likely manages one or more background threads (num_threads) and may use either the text or a non-text protocol depending on text_protocol. If provided, prefix is prepended to keys (exact semantics are library-defined). Typical usage: create one context during initialization and reuse it for get/set/delete operations and for wiring a receiver to process responses.
requirements: host must point to a valid, null-terminated string naming the memcached server.
port is the TCP port number for the memcached server (uint16_t).
text_protocol is an integer flag selecting protocol; exact accepted values and semantics are library-defined/unknown.
num_threads indicates how many internal threads the context may use; exact constraints are not documented here; typical expectation is >= 1 (unknown if 0 is allowed).
prefix may be NULL or a valid, null-terminated string; when non-NULL it is applied to keys (exact format/encoding is unknown).
The returned h2o_memcached_context_t* must be non-NULL before use; if NULL is returned, context creation failed and callers must not use it.
The returned context must remain alive for the lifetime of any operations issued through it. The caller is responsible for eventual destruction by the owning library (not shown here).

functions.name: h2o_memcached_receiver
functions.description: Processes queued memcached-related messages on a multithread receiver. Intended to be installed or invoked as the message handler for an h2o_multithread_receiver_t that is associated with the memcached context, so that responses/completions are delivered to the main thread/event loop.
requirements: receiver must be a valid, initialized h2o_multithread_receiver_t associated with the H2O multithread system.
messages must point to a valid h2o_linklist_t list of messages provided by the H2O multithread framework when dispatching.
This function is typically called by the multithread dispatching mechanism; callers should not pass arbitrary lists (exact calling contract is defined by h2o_multithread.h).

functions.name: h2o_memcached_get
functions.signature: h2o_memcached_req_t *h2o_memcached_get(h2o_memcached_context_t *ctx, h2o_multithread_receiver_t *receiver, h2o_iovec_t key, h2o_memcached_get_cb cb, void *cb_data, int flags);
functions.description: Issues an asynchronous GET for the given key and returns a handle for the outstanding request. On completion, cb is invoked with the retrieved value (or an empty/indicator value depending on implementation). Use the provided receiver (typically wired to h2o_memcached_receiver) to deliver the completion on the appropriate thread.
requirements: ctx must be a valid h2o_memcached_context_t created by h2o_memcached_create_context and must remain valid until the request completes or is cancelled.
receiver must be a valid, initialized h2o_multithread_receiver_t that will receive messages for this request; it should be set up to call h2o_memcached_receiver when messages arrive.

key must be a valid h2o_iovec_t; if key.len > 0 then key.base must point to at least key.len bytes of readable memory. The key content should conform to memcached key requirements; exact encoding/range constraints are unknown.
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with the result on completion. The callback must be prepared to run on the thread associated with receiver.
cb_data is an opaque pointer that will be passed back to cb; it may be NULL or any pointer value.
flags is a bitmask; supported bits include H2O_MEMCACHED_ENCODE_KEY and possibly others; exact semantics of encoding are library-defined/unknown.

The returned h2o_memcached_req_t* may be used with h2o_memcached_cancel_get to cancel the request; callers must not use it after completion or cancellation (lifetime rules beyond this are not documented here).
If NULL is returned, the GET could not be issued; callers must handle this error and must not attempt to cancel via a NULL handle.

functions.name: h2o_memcached_cancel_get
functions.description: Attempts to cancel a previously issued asynchronous GET request identified by req within the given context. After cancellation, the completion callback should not be invoked (behavior on races is implementation-defined/unknown).
requirements: ctx must be the same valid context used to create the request via h2o_memcached_get.
req must be a request handle returned by h2o_memcached_get that has not yet completed or been cancelled.
Do not use req after calling this function; its lifetime ends once cancellation is processed (exact timing is implementation-defined/unknown).
Calling with a NULL req is not documented; callers should pass a valid handle only (behavior for NULL is unknown).

functions.name: h2o_memcached_set
functions.signature: void h2o_memcached_set(h2o_memcached_context_t *ctx, h2o_iovec_t key, h2o_iovec_t value, uint32_t expiration, int flags);
functions.description: Issues a SET/STORE operation to memcached to associate value with key, with an expiration time. Operation is asynchronous with no direct return status from this call; completion/error handling (if any) is handled internally or via the multithread system (details not shown here).
requirements: ctx must be a valid h2o_memcached_context_t created by h2o_memcached_create_context and must remain valid until the operation has been dispatched.
key must be a valid h2o_iovec_t; if key.len > 0 then key.base must point to at least key.len bytes of readable memory.
value must be a valid h2o_iovec_t; if value.len > 0 then value.base must point to at least value.len bytes of readable memory.
expiration is a uint32_t TTL/expiry parameter; exact unit/semantics (seconds/absolute) are unknown.
flags is a bitmask; supported bits include H2O_MEMCACHED_ENCODE_KEY and H2O_MEMCACHED_ENCODE_VALUE; exact encoding semantics are library-defined/unknown.

functions.name: h2o_memcached_delete
functions.description: Issues a DELETE operation to remove the given key from memcached. This call is asynchronous and does not return a status directly; completion behavior is managed internally (details not shown here).
requirements: ctx must be a valid h2o_memcached_context_t created by h2o_memcached_create_context.
key must be a valid h2o_iovec_t; if key.len > 0 then key.base must point to at least key.len bytes of readable memory.
flags is a bitmask; supported bits include H2O_MEMCACHED_ENCODE_KEY; exact encoding semantics are library-defined/unknown.

functions.name: h2o_perror
functions.description: Prints an error message to the error stream, typically including the current errno description (implementation is external). Use for reporting system-call failures.
requirements: msg should be a valid, null-terminated string
Thread-safety and destination stream semantics are unknown (implementation-dependent)

functions.name: h2o_strerror_r
functions.description: Thread-safe strerror variant: formats the error corresponding to err into buf and returns a pointer to a string containing the message (typically buf).
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes
len should be greater than 0 to store any message
Returned pointer may be buf or an internal static string depending on platform-specific implementation

functions.name: h2o_memcpy
functions.signature: static void *h2o_memcpy(void *dst, const void *src, size_t n);
functions.description: Safe wrapper around memcpy that allows src to be NULL only when n == 0; otherwise aborts via h2o_fatal to avoid undefined behavior.
requirements: If n > 0, dst must be non-NULL and point to at least n writable bytes
If n > 0, src must be non-NULL and point to at least n readable bytes
If n == 0, src may be NULL
Overlapping regions are undefined (same as memcpy)

functions.name: h2o_iovec_init
functions.signature: static h2o_iovec_t h2o_iovec_init(const void *base, size_t len);
functions.description: Constructs an h2o_iovec_t from a pointer and length without copying the data. The base pointer is stored as a char*.
requirements: base may be NULL if len == 0; otherwise it should point to at least len bytes
The caller must ensure the lifetime of base covers all uses of the returned iovec

functions.name: h2o_mem_alloc
functions.description: malloc wrapper that aborts the process (via h2o_fatal) on allocation failure. Returns a non-NULL pointer.
requirements: sz may be 0; behavior follows malloc(0) (implementation may return unique or reused pointer)
Caller must free with free or corresponding deallocator for the owning subsystem

functions.name: h2o_mem_aligned_alloc
functions.signature: H2O_RETURNS_NONNULL static void *h2o_mem_aligned_alloc(size_t alignment, size_t sz);
functions.description: Wrapper of posix_memalign; if alignment <= 1, falls back to h2o_mem_alloc. Aborts on allocation failure.
requirements: If alignment <= 1, behaves like malloc
If alignment > 1, alignment should be a nonzero power of two and a multiple of sizeof(void*) as required by posix_memalign
Caller must free with free (pointer returned by posix_memalign is compatible with free)

functions.name: h2o_mem_realloc
functions.description: realloc wrapper that aborts the process on allocation failure. Returns the new pointer on success.
requirements: oldp may be NULL (behaves like malloc)
If realloc fails, the function aborts; it does not return a NULL pointer
The returned pointer must be freed with free or reallocated again by realloc

functions.name: h2o_mem_alloc_recycle
functions.description: Allocates a memory chunk using the recycling allocator defined by allocator (implementation external). Intended to reuse freed chunks of a fixed size class.
requirements: allocator must be initialized and configured with a valid h2o_mem_recycle_conf_t
Returned chunk must be released back using h2o_mem_free_recycle with the same allocator
Size and alignment characteristics depend on allocator->conf (unknown specifics)

functions.name: h2o_mem_free_recycle
functions.description: Returns a previously allocated chunk to the recycling allocator so it can be reused.
requirements: allocator must be the same allocator from which p was obtained
p must be a pointer previously returned by h2o_mem_alloc_recycle (not NULL unless allocator accepts it; behavior for NULL is unknown)
After returning p, the pointer must not be used by the caller

functions.name: h2o_mem_clear_recycle
functions.description: Releases memory chunks cached by the recycling allocator back to the system. If full is non-zero, may release more aggressively.
requirements: allocator must be initialized
The meaning of full is implementation-defined; callers should pass 0 or 1

functions.name: h2o_mem_recycle_is_empty
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the recycling allocator holds no cached chunks (chunks.size == 0).
requirements: allocator must be non-NULL and initialized

functions.name: h2o_mem_init_pool
functions.description: Initializes a memory pool for pooled allocations and shared references.
requirements: pool must be a valid pointer to storage for h2o_mem_pool_t
Must be called before allocating from the pool

functions.name: h2o_mem_clear_pool
functions.description: Clears and frees resources held by the memory pool. The pool may be reused afterward without re-initialization or can be disposed by the application.
requirements: pool must have been initialized by h2o_mem_init_pool
After this call, any pooled allocations not externally retained are invalid
It is safe to call h2o_mem_init_pool again before reuse, but not required

functions.name: h2o_mem_alloc_pool_aligned
functions.signature: static void *h2o_mem_alloc_pool_aligned(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, size_t alignment, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates size bytes from the memory pool with the requested alignment (asserts alignment is a non-zero power of two). Aborts on internal allocation failure.
requirements: pool must be initialized
alignment must be a non-zero power of two (enforced by assert)
size may be any value; behavior for 0-size depends on pool implementation

functions.name: h2o_mem__do_alloc_pool_aligned
functions.description: Implementation function performing the aligned allocation from the pool. Called by h2o_mem_alloc_pool_aligned.
requirements: pool must be initialized
alignment should be a non-zero power of two
Returns a valid pointer or aborts internally on failure (behavior inferred from wrapper)

functions.name: h2o_mem_alloc_shared
functions.description: Allocates a ref-counted memory chunk of size sz. The initial ref-count is 1. If pool is non-NULL, the chunk is associated with the pool so its ref-count is decremented when the pool is cleared. dispose, if non-NULL, is called when the ref-count reaches zero.
requirements: pool may be NULL to create an orphan chunk
dispose may be NULL; if provided it must accept the user bytes pointer
Caller must manage ref-counting: use h2o_mem_addref_shared to add references and h2o_mem_release_shared to release
The returned pointer is to the user bytes (not to the internal header)

functions.name: h2o_mem_link_shared
functions.description: Links an existing ref-counted chunk to a memory pool; the pool will decrement the chunk’s ref-count when cleared. Can be linked more than once to the same pool.
requirements: p must be a pointer returned by h2o_mem_alloc_shared
pool must be initialized
Linking multiple times is permitted; each link likely accounts for one decrement on pool clear (per documentation)

functions.name: h2o_mem_addref_shared
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a ref-counted chunk.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer previously returned by h2o_mem_alloc_shared (i.e., to the user bytes)
The current ref-count must be non-zero (asserted)
Each increment should be balanced with a corresponding h2o_mem_release_shared

functions.name: h2o_mem_release_shared
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a ref-counted chunk and frees it (calling dispose if provided) when the count reaches zero. Returns 1 if the chunk was freed, 0 otherwise.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer previously returned by h2o_mem_alloc_shared
The current ref-count must be non-zero (asserted)
After it returns 1, the memory is freed and must not be used

functions.name: h2o_buffer_clear_recycle
functions.description: Frees unused memory pooled for buffer recycling. If full is non-zero, may clear more aggressively.
requirements: No buffer arguments; effect is global to the buffer recycler subsystem
Exact behavior of full is implementation-defined

functions.name: h2o_buffer_recycle_is_empty
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the global buffer recycling pool has no cached memory.
requirements: Global buffer recycler must have been initialized by the library (implicit)

functions.name: h2o_buffer_init
functions.description: Initializes a buffer handle to point to a prototype’s initial buffer, deferring allocation until needed.
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t* variable
prototype must be non-NULL and properly initialized

functions.name: h2o_buffer__do_free
functions.description: Frees resources associated with a buffer, using the appropriate deallocation method for its backing storage (implementation external).
requirements: buffer must be a buffer previously initialized or allocated by this subsystem
After this call the buffer must not be used

functions.name: h2o_buffer_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of a buffer handle: sets the caller’s pointer to NULL and frees the underlying buffer if it is dynamically allocated (i.e., if it has a prototype).
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
Safe to call with a buffer pointing to a prototype-initialized buffer; only frees when buffer->_prototype != NULL

functions.name: h2o_buffer_reserve
functions.description: Ensures that at least min_guarantee bytes are available for appending to the buffer, allocating or growing as needed, and aborts on allocation failure. Returns an iovec pointing to the reserved region where data should be written next.
requirements: inbuf must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*; pass *inbuf == NULL to allocate a new buffer
min_guarantee may be any non-negative size; 0 is allowed but reserved region may be empty
Caller must increase (*inbuf)->size appropriately after writing into the reserved region

functions.name: h2o_buffer_try_reserve
functions.description: Like h2o_buffer_reserve but does not abort on allocation failure; returns an iovec with base == NULL on failure.
requirements: inbuf must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
Caller must check the returned iovec.base is not NULL before writing/using it (warn_unused_result)
Caller must increase (*inbuf)->size accordingly on success

functions.name: h2o_buffer_append
functions.signature: static void h2o_buffer_append(h2o_buffer_t **dst, const void *src, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends len bytes from src to the buffer, allocating as necessary (aborts on allocation failure).
requirements: dst must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
src must point to at least len readable bytes (if len > 0)
On success, (*dst)->size is incremented by len

functions.name: h2o_buffer_try_append
functions.signature: static int h2o_buffer_try_append(h2o_buffer_t **dst, const void *src, size_t len) __attribute__((warn_unused_result));
functions.description: Attempts to append len bytes from src to the buffer; returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: dst must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
src must point to at least len readable bytes (if len > 0)
Caller must check the return value before assuming data was appended

functions.name: h2o_buffer_consume
functions.description: Consumes (drains) delta bytes from the start of the buffer, discarding them and adjusting internal pointers.
requirements: inbuf must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
delta must be less than or equal to the current (*inbuf)->size (behavior on overflow is implementation-defined)

functions.name: h2o_buffer_consume_all
functions.description: Discards all data stored in the buffer. If record_capacity is non-zero, the buffer will remember the current capacity to bias the next reservation.
requirements: inbuf must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
record_capacity should be 0 or 1; exact semantics beyond comments are implementation-defined

functions.name: h2o_buffer_set_prototype
functions.description: Resets a buffer’s prototype. If the current buffer is dynamic (has a prototype), it updates the prototype field; otherwise it points the handle to the new prototype’s initial buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer to a h2o_buffer_t*
prototype must be non-NULL and initialized
Caller must not use previous prototype buffer after switching if the handle changed

functions.name: h2o_buffer_link_to_pool
functions.description: Registers a buffer with a memory pool, so it will be freed automatically when the pool is cleared. After linking, the buffer cannot be resized.
requirements: buffer must be a valid buffer allocated/managed by this subsystem
pool must be initialized
After linking, do not attempt to resize the buffer

functions.name: h2o_buffer__dispose_linked
functions.description: Dispose callback used for freeing buffers linked to a memory pool (implementation external). Intended to be passed as a dispose function for shared allocations.
requirements: p must be a pointer created by h2o_buffer_link_to_pool’s internal shared allocation
Not intended for direct use except as a dispose callback

functions.name: h2o_doublebuffer_init
functions.description: Initializes a double buffer with a given buffer prototype; sets the inflight flag and counters to zero.
requirements: db must be a valid pointer to h2o_doublebuffer_t storage
prototype must be non-NULL and initialized

functions.name: h2o_doublebuffer_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of the internal buffer of the double buffer.
requirements: db must have been initialized by h2o_doublebuffer_init

functions.name: h2o_doublebuffer_prepare
functions.description: Produces a view of data to send up to max_bytes from the double buffer. If the double buffer is empty and receiving has data, it swaps the buffers. Marks the returned bytes as inflight until consumed.
requirements: db->inflight must be 0 on entry (asserted)
max_bytes must be non-zero (asserted)
receiving must be a valid pointer to a buffer handle; both db->buf and *receiving must be initialized
Caller must later call h2o_doublebuffer_consume to finalize consumption

functions.name: h2o_doublebuffer_prepare_empty
functions.description: Marks that an empty transmission is inflight (useful when only headers are sent).
requirements: db->inflight must be 0 on entry (asserted)
Must be followed by h2o_doublebuffer_consume when appropriate

functions.name: h2o_doublebuffer_consume
functions.description: Consumes the bytes previously marked as inflight by h2o_doublebuffer_prepare/prepare_empty and clears the inflight state. Uses h2o_buffer_consume or h2o_buffer_consume_all depending on the amount.
requirements: db->inflight must be 1 on entry (asserted)
Must only be called after a corresponding prepare or prepare_empty call
After consumption, db->_bytes_inflight becomes 0

functions.name: h2o_vector__reserve
functions.signature: static void h2o_vector__reserve(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_vector_t *vector, size_t alignment, size_t element_size, size_t new_capacity);
functions.description: Ensures the vector has capacity for at least new_capacity elements; grows the storage if needed by calling h2o_vector__expand.
requirements: pool must be initialized
vector must be a valid H2O_VECTOR instance
alignment should be suitable for the element type, and element_size must match the stored element size
new_capacity must be >= current size to avoid losing elements (common vector invariant)

functions.name: h2o_vector__expand
functions.signature: void h2o_vector__expand(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_vector_t *vector, size_t alignment, size_t element_size, size_t new_capacity);
functions.description: Expands the vector’s capacity to at least new_capacity elements, allocating aligned storage from the pool (implementation external).
requirements: pool must be initialized
vector must be a valid H2O_VECTOR instance
alignment should be suitable for the element type and typically a power of two
element_size must equal sizeof entries stored in vector
new_capacity must be >= vector->capacity

functions.name: h2o_vector__erase
functions.signature: static void h2o_vector__erase(h2o_vector_t *vector, size_t element_size, size_t index);
functions.description: Erases the entry at the specified index by moving the tail left by one element and decrementing size.
requirements: vector must be a valid H2O_VECTOR instance with size > 0
index must be less than vector->size
element_size must match the size of the stored elements
Erased element’s resources (if any) must be cleaned up by the caller before or after erasure, if needed

functions.name: h2o_memis
functions.signature: static int h2o_memis(const void *target, size_t target_len, const void *test, size_t test_len);
functions.description: Compares two memory regions for equality, returning non-zero if equal. Optimizes by checking the first byte and then memcmp of the remainder.
requirements: target and test must point to readable memory of lengths target_len and test_len respectively
Safe for zero-length comparisons (returns 1 when both lengths are 0)

functions.name: h2o_memrchr
functions.signature: static void *h2o_memrchr(const void *s, int c, size_t n);
functions.description: Searches for character c (interpreted as an unsigned char) in the first n bytes of the memory block s, scanning from the end towards the beginning. Returns a pointer to the last occurrence or NULL.
requirements: s must point to at least n bytes
Behavior is undefined if s is NULL and n > 0

functions.name: h2o_mem_set_secure
functions.signature: static void *h2o_mem_set_secure(void *b, int c, size_t len);
functions.description: Secure memset wrapper that calls the function referenced by h2o_mem__set_secure to fill len bytes of b with byte value c, preventing optimization away.
requirements: h2o_mem__set_secure must be set to a valid implementation before calling
b must point to at least len writable bytes
Returns the value returned by h2o_mem__set_secure

functions.name: h2o_mem_swap
functions.description: Swaps the contents of two memory regions of length len (implementation external). Useful for in-place data swapping without extra allocations.
requirements: x and y must point to at least len bytes each
Behavior with overlapping regions is unknown (implementation-dependent); callers should avoid overlap to be safe

functions.name: h2o_dump_memory
functions.signature: void h2o_dump_memory(FILE *fp, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Emits a hex dump of len bytes from buf to the given FILE stream fp (implementation external).
requirements: fp must be a valid, open FILE* for writing
buf must point to at least len readable bytes
len may be 0 to dump nothing

functions.name: h2o_append_to_null_terminated_list
functions.description: Appends element to a NULL-terminated list (array) of pointers allocated with malloc/realloc-like functions, updating the list pointer as needed (implementation external).
requirements: *list must be either NULL or a valid NULL-terminated array of pointers allocated with malloc/realloc
On success, the list remains NULL-terminated and may be reallocated; callers should not hold stale pointers into the old array
element can be NULL; semantics depend on consumer of the list

functions.name: h2o_multithread_create_queue
functions.description: Creates an inter-thread message queue associated with the given event loop. Typical usage: create once per loop/thread to enable other threads to post messages to that loop.
requirements: loop must point to a valid h2o_loop_t associated with a running event loop.
The returned queue must be destroyed with h2o_multithread_destroy_queue when no longer needed.
Exact failure/NULL-return behavior is not documented in this header; callers should be prepared for unknown behavior if allocation fails (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_multithread_destroy_queue
functions.description: Destroys a queue created for inter-thread communication and releases its resources.
requirements: queue must be a queue previously created by h2o_multithread_create_queue.
queue must remain unused after this call (no further register/send/get operations).
Behavior if queue is NULL or still in use by other threads is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_multithread_register_receiver
functions.description: Registers a receiver on the specified queue. The receiver will be invoked via its callback when messages arrive for it.
requirements: queue must be a valid queue created by h2o_multithread_create_queue.
receiver must be a valid pointer to storage that remains alive until unregistered.
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).
The same receiver must not be registered more than once on the same queue (inferred from typical register semantics; behavior otherwise unknown).

functions.name: h2o_multithread_unregister_receiver
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered receiver from the given queue.
requirements: queue must be a valid queue created by h2o_multithread_create_queue.
receiver must have been previously registered on this queue using h2o_multithread_register_receiver.
After unregistering, the receiver will no longer receive messages; do not assume pending messages are delivered unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_multithread_send_message
functions.description: Sends a message to the specified receiver, or if message is NULL, simply wakes the receiving thread/event loop.
requirements: receiver must refer to a receiver that is currently registered to a queue.
message may be NULL to perform a wake-up without payload.
If message is non-NULL, it must point to a valid h2o_multithread_message_t whose storage remains valid until processed (exact lifetime/ownership rules are not documented here; details unknown).

functions.name: h2o_multithread_create_thread
functions.signature: void h2o_multithread_create_thread(pthread_t *tid, const pthread_attr_t *attr, void *(*func)(void *), void *arg);
functions.description: Creates a new thread that starts at func(arg). This is a convenience wrapper around pthread creation semantics.
requirements: tid must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created thread ID.
func must be a non-NULL function pointer of type void *(*)(void *).
attr may be NULL for default attributes or a valid pthread_attr_t.
This function returns void; behavior on failure is not documented here (unknown whether it aborts or handles errors internally).

functions.name: h2o_multithread_get_loop
functions.description: Returns the event loop associated with the provided queue.
requirements: Argument must be a valid queue created by h2o_multithread_create_queue.
Return value is the associated h2o_loop_t; NULL-return conditions (if any) are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_sem_init
functions.description: Initializes a counting semaphore with the specified capacity (maximum count).
requirements: sem must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a semaphore.
capacity sets the maximum count; negative values behavior is not documented (unknown).
Must be called before any other h2o_sem_* operation on sem.

functions.name: h2o_sem_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a semaphore previously initialized with h2o_sem_init and releases its resources.
requirements: sem must have been initialized by h2o_sem_init.
No other thread should be using sem during or after destruction (not documented; safe-use requirement inferred; exact behavior otherwise unknown).

functions.name: h2o_sem_wait
functions.description: Waits (potentially blocks) until the semaphore can be acquired (decrements the count).
requirements: sem must have been initialized by h2o_sem_init.
May block the calling thread; interruption and timeout behavior are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_sem_post
functions.description: Posts (releases) to the semaphore (increments the count), potentially waking a waiting thread.
requirements: sem must have been initialized by h2o_sem_init.
Behavior when incrementing beyond capacity is managed internally; exact error handling is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_sem_set_capacity
functions.description: Changes the maximum capacity of the semaphore.
requirements: sem must have been initialized by h2o_sem_init.
new_capacity is the new maximum count; constraints and behavior when lowering below current count are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_barrier_init
functions.description: Initializes a barrier to synchronize a fixed number of threads.
requirements: barrier must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a barrier.
count is the number of threads to wait for; valid range and behavior for 0 are not documented (unknown).
Must be called before h2o_barrier_wait/done/add/dispose.

functions.name: h2o_barrier_wait
functions.description: Waits for all threads to enter the barrier. Blocks until the required number of threads have called wait/done as appropriate.
requirements: barrier must have been initialized with h2o_barrier_init.
May block the calling thread; spurious wake conditions and reuse semantics are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_barrier_done
functions.description: Signals that the calling thread is done with the barrier and returns an int (purpose not documented in this header).
requirements: barrier must have been initialized with h2o_barrier_init.
Return value semantics are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_barrier_add
functions.description: Adjusts the number of participants in the barrier by delta.
requirements: barrier must have been initialized with h2o_barrier_init.
delta may increase or decrease participation; exact constraints (e.g., not reducing below 0) are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_barrier_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of the barrier and releases its internal resources.
requirements: barrier must have been initialized with h2o_barrier_init.
No other threads should be using the barrier at the time of disposal (safe-use requirement inferred; exact behavior otherwise unknown).

functions.name: h2o_error_reporter__on_timeout
functions.description: Internal timeout callback for the error reporter. Invoked by the event loop when the reporter’s delayed timer expires to trigger error reporting via the reporter’s registered callback.
requirements: timer must be a pointer to the h2o_timer_t embedded in an h2o_error_reporter_t initialized with H2O_ERROR_REPORTER_INITIALIZER.
Intended to be called by the event loop; callers should not invoke this directly (inferred from naming and initializer).

functions.name: h2o_error_reporter_record_success
functions.description: Records a success event for the error reporter by atomically incrementing the internal success counter. Use this rather than modifying fields directly.
requirements: reporter must be a valid, initialized h2o_error_reporter_t (e.g., via H2O_ERROR_REPORTER_INITIALIZER).
Safe to call from multiple threads due to atomic increment; no memory ordering guarantees beyond what __sync_fetch_and_add provides are documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_error_reporter_record_error
functions.signature: uintptr_t h2o_error_reporter_record_error(h2o_loop_t *loop, h2o_error_reporter_t *reporter, uint64_t delay_ticks, uintptr_t new_data);
functions.description: Records an error event, arms a delayed timer if not already set, and swaps reporter->data to new_data, returning the previous value. When the timer expires, the reporter’s _report_errors callback is invoked to emit aggregated errors/successes.
requirements: loop must be a valid event loop on which the reporter’s timer can be scheduled.
reporter must be initialized using H2O_ERROR_REPORTER_INITIALIZER so that its mutex, timer, and _report_errors callback are set.
delay_ticks specifies how long to delay before invoking the reporting callback; the time base is the loop’s tick unit (exact unit not documented here).
Callers should expect the return value to be the previous reporter->data value and manage any ownership of that value appropriately (exact ownership semantics not documented).

functions.name: BIO_meth_new
functions.signature: static inline BIO_METHOD *BIO_meth_new(int type, const char *name)
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a BIO_METHOD structure (backport shim for OpenSSL < 1.1.0). Sets all fields to zero, then assigns the provided type and name. Intended to be followed by BIO_meth_set_* calls to install callbacks. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x10100000L or (defined(LIBRESSL_VERSION_NUMBER) && LIBRESSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x2070000fL).
type is an integer identifying the BIO method; must be a valid/recognized type for subsequent BIO usage.
name must be a non-NULL pointer to a persistent string (stored as a raw pointer in the BIO_METHOD).
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure) before using the result.
After creation, caller should set the method callbacks using BIO_meth_set_write/read/puts/ctrl before using the method in a BIO.
Caller is responsible for eventually freeing the allocated BIO_METHOD using the appropriate mechanism used by the surrounding library (this backport allocates with malloc).

functions.name: SSL_CTX_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an SSL_CTX object (backport macro mapping to CRYPTO_add on OpenSSL < 1.1.0). Returns the new reference count as an int.
requirements: Available only when not building with BoringSSL and when OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x10100000L (or corresponding LibreSSL condition).
ctx must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized SSL_CTX.
Caller should not rely on thread-unsafe usage; ensure ctx is used according to OpenSSL’s threading requirements in the surrounding build.
Caller may use the return value as the new reference count (as provided by CRYPTO_add).

functions.name: X509_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an X509 certificate object (backport macro mapping to CRYPTO_add on OpenSSL < 1.1.0). Returns the new reference count as an int.
requirements: Available only when not building with BoringSSL and when OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x10100000L (or corresponding LibreSSL condition).
x509 must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized X509.
Caller may use the return value as the new reference count (as provided by CRYPTO_add).

functions.name: X509_STORE_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an X509_STORE object (backport macro mapping to CRYPTO_add on OpenSSL < 1.1.0). Returns the new reference count as an int.
requirements: Available only when not building with BoringSSL and when OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x10100000L (or corresponding LibreSSL condition).
store must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized X509_STORE.
Caller may use the return value as the new reference count (as provided by CRYPTO_add).

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of an EVP_PKEY object (backport macro mapping to CRYPTO_add on OpenSSL < 1.1.0). Returns the new reference count as an int.
requirements: Available only when not building with BoringSSL and when OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x10100000L (or corresponding LibreSSL condition).
pkey must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized EVP_PKEY.
Caller may use the return value as the new reference count (as provided by CRYPTO_add).

functions.name: OpenSSL_version
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing OpenSSL build/runtime information (backport macro to SSLeay_version on older OpenSSL/LibreSSL). Typical usage: OpenSSL_version(OPENSSL_VERSION) or other selector constants.
requirements: Available when the header is compiled; the macro maps to SSLeay_version on older versions.
t must be a valid selector constant accepted by SSLeay_version (e.g., SSLeay version/component selectors as provided by the OpenSSL headers in use).
Return value is a NUL-terminated string managed by the library; the caller must not free or modify it.

functions.name: SSL_is_server
functions.description: Indicates whether the SSL object is operating in server mode (backport macro that inspects the ssl->server field). Returns non-zero if server, zero if client.
requirements: Available only when OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x10002000L or (defined(LIBRESSL_VERSION_NUMBER) && LIBRESSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x2070000fL).
ssl must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized SSL object whose server field reflects its mode.

functions.name: h2o_pipe_sender_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of a pipe sender, releasing any resources associated with it within the provided H2O context. Intended to be called when a previously initialized (and possibly started) pipe sender is no longer needed. Definition is not present in this header; behavior is provided by the linked H2O library.
requirements: sender must be a valid, non-null pointer to an h2o_pipe_sender_t.
ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to an h2o_context_t.
The sender should have been initialized (e.g., via h2o_pipe_sender_init) before disposal (inferred from naming and structure).
If the sender was started or is in use, dispose is expected to close/cleanup underlying resources (exact semantics unknown; implementation not shown).
Thread-safety and reentrancy guarantees are unknown; call from the appropriate H2O thread/context as required by h2o_context_t usage (inferred from library patterns).

functions.name: h2o_pipe_sender_start
functions.description: Starts a pipe sender using the provided H2O context and returns a boolean-like int indicating success (non-zero) or failure (0). Typically allocates/opens the pipe (sender->fds) and prepares it for sending data via the H2O sendvec path. Definition is not in this header; behavior is in the H2O library.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to an h2o_context_t.
sender must be a valid, non-null pointer to an h2o_pipe_sender_t.
Sender should be initialized with h2o_pipe_sender_init prior to calling start (inferred from presence of init and in_use helpers).
Sender should not already be in use (i.e., fds not already allocated); check with h2o_pipe_sender_in_use before calling (inferred from naming and helper).
Caller must check the return value and avoid using the pipe sender for sending if start returns 0 (failure).
Exact error reporting beyond the boolean return is unknown; no errno/out-params are specified.

functions.name: h2o_pipe_sender_send
functions.signature: void h2o_pipe_sender_send(h2o_req_t *req, h2o_pipe_sender_t *sender, size_t len, h2o_send_state_t send_state);
functions.description: Wrapper around h2o_sendvec that submits the contents of the pipe to the HTTP/2/HTTP/3 send path of an H2O request. Uses the pipe represented by sender to transmit up to len bytes with the given send_state. Actual implementation is elsewhere in the H2O library.
requirements: req must be a valid, non-null pointer to an h2o_req_t representing an active request.
sender must be a valid, non-null pointer to an h2o_pipe_sender_t.
The sender should have been successfully started (pipe allocated) before calling send; use h2o_pipe_sender_in_use to check (inferred).
len is the number of bytes to submit; acceptable range and whether zero is allowed are not documented here (unknown).
send_state must be a valid h2o_send_state_t value as defined by H2O (e.g., final/streaming states; exact set unknown in this header).
Call context/threading must comply with H2O’s requirements for sending on req (unknown; follow h2o_send/h2o_sendvec usage patterns).
Error handling behavior (e.g., async callbacks, immediate failures) is unknown; caller should rely on H2O request/send APIs’ standard conventions.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_create_decoder
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a QPACK decoder context with the given dynamic table size and maximum number of blocked streams. Use the returned decoder for parsing QPACK instructions and HEADERS payloads for requests/responses.
requirements: header_table_size is a uint32_t specifying desired dynamic table size; precise valid range is unspecified in this header (refer to QPACK/implementation limits).
max_blocked is a uint16_t specifying the maximum number of blocked streams; precise valid range is unspecified in this header.
Return value is a pointer to a newly created decoder or NULL on allocation failure (semantics are not stated here; caller must handle a possible NULL).
Caller owns the returned object and must destroy it using h2o_qpack_destroy_decoder.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_destroy_decoder
functions.description: Destroys and frees a QPACK decoder previously created by h2o_qpack_create_decoder.
requirements: qpack must be a valid pointer previously returned by h2o_qpack_create_decoder.
Behavior for qpack == NULL is unspecified by this header; pass a valid pointer.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_decoder_handle_input
functions.signature: int h2o_qpack_decoder_handle_input(h2o_qpack_decoder_t *qpack, int64_t **unblocked_stream_ids, size_t *num_unblocked, const uint8_t **src, const uint8_t *src_end, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Processes a contiguous range of bytes containing QPACK encoder instructions, advancing *src to the start of the first incomplete instruction. Reports any streams that became unblocked due to processed instructions.
requirements: qpack must be a valid QPACK decoder created by h2o_qpack_create_decoder.
unblocked_stream_ids and num_unblocked must be valid writable pointers; on return they are updated to report unblocked stream IDs (allocation/ownership semantics are not documented here).
*src must point to the start of available input; src_end must point one past the last available byte; *src <= src_end.
On return, *src is advanced to the first partial (incomplete) instruction if any remains.
err_desc must be a valid writable pointer for error description; content and lifetime of the string are not specified.
This decoder does not enforce instruction size limits; the caller must rely on transport-level flow control to avoid feeding excessively large instruction streams (as noted in the comment).
Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not specified in this header; caller must check for nonzero/zero as defined by the implementation.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_decoder_send_state_sync
functions.description: Generates decoder stream bytes to synchronize state with the encoder (e.g., Section Acknowledgements/Insert Count Increment), writing them into outbuf and returning the number of bytes written.
requirements: qpack must be a valid QPACK decoder.
outbuf must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the generated synchronization bytes; required capacity is not specified in this header.
Returns the number of bytes written to outbuf.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_decoder_send_stream_cancel
functions.description: Generates a decoder-stream instruction to cancel a request stream (e.g., to indicate that a stream was reset), writing to outbuf and returning the number of bytes written.
requirements: qpack must be a valid QPACK decoder.
outbuf must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the generated bytes; required capacity is not specified in this header.
stream_id is the HTTP/3 request stream ID to cancel; must be a valid stream identifier for the current connection (range/validity not specified here).
Returns the number of bytes written to outbuf.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_parse_request
functions.signature: int h2o_qpack_parse_request(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_qpack_decoder_t *qpack, int64_t stream_id, h2o_iovec_t *method, const h2o_url_scheme_t **scheme, h2o_iovec_t *authority, h2o_iovec_t *path, h2o_iovec_t *protocol, h2o_headers_t *headers, int *pseudo_header_exists_map, size_t *content_length, h2o_iovec_t *expect, h2o_cache_digests_t **digests, h2o_iovec_t *datagram_flow_id, uint8_t *outbuf, size_t *outbufsize, const uint8_t *src, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses a QPACK-encoded HTTP/3 request header block (the payload of a HEADERS frame) for the given stream, populating method, scheme, authority, path, protocol, general headers, and related metadata. Optionally emits decoder-stream bytes into outbuf (size via outbufsize).
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t for allocating parsed header storage.
qpack must be a valid QPACK decoder.
stream_id is the HTTP/3 request stream ID; must be appropriate for a request (validity not specified here).

method, scheme, authority, path, protocol, headers, pseudo_header_exists_map, content_length, expect, digests, datagram_flow_id must be valid writable pointers to receive parsed results (fields populated as available).

outbuf must point to a writable buffer; outbufsize must point to a size value indicating available capacity on input and is updated with bytes written on output; exact semantics are not detailed here.
src must point to the start of the HEADERS frame payload; len is the number of bytes in that payload; src..src+len must be readable.
err_desc must be a valid writable pointer for error descriptions; meaning and lifetime of the message are not specified.
The input must be the payload of an HTTP/3 HEADERS frame, not including the frame header (per comment).
Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not specified in this header; caller must check per implementation.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_parse_response
functions.signature: int h2o_qpack_parse_response(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_qpack_decoder_t *qpack, int64_t stream_id, int *status, h2o_headers_t *headers, h2o_iovec_t *datagram_flow_id, uint8_t *outbuf, size_t *outbufsize, const uint8_t *src, size_t len, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Parses a QPACK-encoded HTTP/3 response header block (the payload of a HEADERS frame) for the given stream, extracting the status code, headers, and optional datagram flow ID. Optionally emits decoder-stream bytes to outbuf.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t.
qpack must be a valid QPACK decoder.
stream_id is the HTTP/3 response stream ID; validity not specified here.
status, headers, datagram_flow_id must be valid writable pointers.
outbuf must point to a writable buffer that is at least H2O_HPACK_ENCODE_INT_MAX_LENGTH bytes long (per comment).
outbufsize must be a valid pointer and is used to communicate available capacity / bytes written (exact semantics not detailed here).
src must point to the start of the HEADERS frame payload; len is the length in bytes; region must be readable.
err_desc must be a valid writable pointer for error descriptions.
Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not specified in this header; caller must check per implementation.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_create_encoder
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a QPACK encoder context with the given dynamic table size and maximum number of blocked streams. Use the encoder to generate QPACK-encoded header blocks and to process decoder-stream input.
requirements: header_table_size is a uint32_t specifying desired dynamic table size; precise valid range is unspecified here.
max_blocked is a uint16_t specifying the maximum number of blocked streams; precise valid range is unspecified here.
Return value is a pointer to a newly created encoder or NULL on allocation failure (semantics not stated; caller should handle possible NULL).
Caller owns the returned object and must destroy it using h2o_qpack_destroy_encoder.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_destroy_encoder
functions.description: Destroys and frees a QPACK encoder previously created by h2o_qpack_create_encoder.
requirements: qpack must be a valid pointer previously returned by h2o_qpack_create_encoder.
Behavior for qpack == NULL is unspecified by this header; pass a valid pointer.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_encoder_handle_input
functions.signature: int h2o_qpack_encoder_handle_input(h2o_qpack_encoder_t *qpack, const uint8_t **src, const uint8_t *src_end, const char **err_desc);
functions.description: Handles bytes sent on the QPACK decoder stream and updates the encoder state accordingly. Advances *src as bytes are consumed.
requirements: qpack may be NULL (per comment); if NULL, the function must tolerate it (semantics otherwise unspecified).
*src must point to the start of available input; src_end must point one past the last available byte; *src <= src_end.
On return, *src is advanced by the number of bytes consumed.
err_desc must be a valid writable pointer for error descriptions; meaning and lifetime are not specified.
Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not specified in this header; caller must check per implementation.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_flatten_request
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_qpack_flatten_request(h2o_qpack_encoder_t *qpack, h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, int64_t stream_id, h2o_byte_vector_t *encoder_buf, h2o_iovec_t method, const h2o_url_scheme_t *scheme, h2o_iovec_t authority, h2o_iovec_t path, h2o_iovec_t protocol, const h2o_header_t *headers, size_t num_headers, h2o_iovec_t datagram_flow_id);
functions.description: Encodes an HTTP/3 request header set into a QPACK header block and prepends the HTTP/3 HEADERS frame header. Optionally emits encoder-stream data to encoder_buf to enable dynamic table use; pass NULL to avoid blocking (per comment). Returns the serialized bytes as an h2o_iovec_t.
requirements: qpack must be a valid QPACK encoder.
pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t used to allocate the returned buffer.
stream_id must be the request stream ID; validity not specified here.
encoder_buf may be NULL to avoid blocking; if non-NULL, it must be a valid, writable h2o_byte_vector_t to receive encoder stream data.
method, scheme, authority, path, protocol must be provided as h2o_iovec_t/ptrs; required/non-empty constraints are not specified here.
headers must point to an array of at least num_headers elements containing request headers.
datagram_flow_id is optional metadata; semantics not specified here.
The returned h2o_iovec_t refers to memory managed by pool; lifetime tied to pool.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_flatten_response
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_qpack_flatten_response(h2o_qpack_encoder_t *qpack, h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, int64_t stream_id, h2o_byte_vector_t *encoder_buf, int status, const h2o_header_t *headers, size_t num_headers, const h2o_iovec_t *server_name, size_t content_length, h2o_iovec_t datagram_flow_id, size_t *serialized_header_len);
functions.description: Encodes an HTTP/3 response header set into a QPACK header block and prepends the HTTP/3 HEADERS frame header. Optionally emits encoder-stream data to encoder_buf. Returns the serialized bytes as an h2o_iovec_t and, if provided, writes the length of the serialized header block to serialized_header_len.
requirements: qpack must be a valid QPACK encoder.
pool must be a valid, initialized h2o_mem_pool_t used to allocate the returned buffer.
stream_id must be the response stream ID; validity not specified here.
encoder_buf may be NULL to avoid blocking; if non-NULL, it must be a valid, writable h2o_byte_vector_t.
status is the HTTP status code; acceptable range is not specified here.
headers must point to an array of at least num_headers elements containing response headers.
server_name may be NULL or point to a server name; exact requirements not specified here.
content_length is the known content length; semantics for special values are not specified here.
datagram_flow_id is optional metadata; semantics not specified here.
serialized_header_len must be a valid writable pointer if non-NULL; receives the number of bytes in the serialized header block.
The returned h2o_iovec_t refers to memory managed by pool; lifetime tied to pool.

functions.name: h2o_rand
functions.description: Thread-safe random number generator wrapper. On non-Apple/BSD platforms, this is a real function returning a pseudo-random integer in the range [0, H2O_RAND_MAX] where H2O_RAND_MAX == RAND_MAX. Intended as a drop-in, thread-safe replacement for rand(3); h2o_srand() is a no-op and seeding is not required.
requirements: No arguments required.
May be called from multiple threads; implementation is documented as multi-thread safe.
Do not rely on srand() for seeding; h2o_srand() is defined as a no-op in this header.
Callers should be prepared for any integer value in the inclusive range [0, H2O_RAND_MAX] (where H2O_RAND_MAX == RAND_MAX on these platforms).
No error/exception semantics are defined; the function returns a value unconditionally.

functions.name: h2o_generate_uuidv4
functions.description: Generates a UUID version 4 (RFC 4122) in canonical string form and writes it to dst, including the terminating NUL. The format is 36 printable characters with hyphens (8-4-4-4-12), followed by a NUL byte, and the version/variant bits are set per RFC 4122.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least H2O_UUID_STR_RFC4122_LEN + 1 bytes (i.e., 36 + 1 = 37 bytes) to accommodate the string and terminating NUL.
dst must be a valid, non-null pointer.
The function does not return a status; callers should assume it always writes a properly formatted NUL-terminated UUIDv4 string to dst.
Thread-safety of concurrent calls is not explicitly documented; if used concurrently, ensure dst buffers do not overlap.

functions.name: h2o_redis_create_client
functions.description: Creates a Redis client object bound to the given h2o event loop. Intended to initialize client state and allocate a client structure (of size sz), returning a handle used for connect/command operations. Usage: call once to obtain a client, then configure callbacks (on_connect/on_close) on the returned object and call h2o_redis_connect to establish a connection. Details of the sz parameter are not documented in this header; by convention it likely represents the allocation size for the client structure (at least sizeof(h2o_redis_client_t)).
requirements: loop must be a valid, initialized h2o_loop_t pointer that remains alive as long as the client is in use.
sz must be large enough to hold the client object (inferred: at least sizeof(h2o_redis_client_t)); exact constraints are not documented.
The returned h2o_redis_client_t* must be freed with h2o_redis_free when no longer needed.
Do not use the returned client after it has been freed.

functions.name: h2o_redis_connect
functions.signature: void h2o_redis_connect(h2o_redis_client_t *client, const char *host, uint16_t port);
functions.description: Initiates an asynchronous connection from the client to a Redis server at host:port using the client's event loop. Expected usage: after creating a client, set any callbacks (on_connect/on_close) and timeouts on the client, then call this to start connecting. Connection progress and errors are reported via the client's callbacks; exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: client must point to a valid h2o_redis_client_t previously created by h2o_redis_create_client.
host must be a non-NULL pointer to a null-terminated hostname or IP address string; its storage must remain valid until the connection attempt consumes it (duration unspecified).
port is a 16-bit TCP port number (0–65535); typical Redis default is 6379 (usage detail; not required).
This function should be called on a client associated with a live h2o_loop_t.
Behavior when called on an already connecting/connected client is not specified by this header (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_redis_disconnect
functions.description: Closes the client's connection to the Redis server (if open) and transitions it to a disconnected state. Expected usage: call to proactively terminate the connection or during shutdown; on_close callback may be invoked with an error string indicating the reason. Exact callback behavior is not documented here.
requirements: client must point to a valid h2o_redis_client_t.
Safe to call regardless of connection state is not stated; behavior when not connected is unknown.
After disconnecting, commands that rely on a live connection may fail or trigger error callbacks (behavior not specified here).

functions.name: h2o_redis_free
functions.description: Frees resources associated with the client. Expected usage: call once when the client is no longer needed. If a connection is still open, behavior is not documented here; in typical patterns, disconnecting first is recommended, but this header does not mandate ordering.
requirements: client must be a pointer previously returned by h2o_redis_create_client (or compatible allocation by that function).
Do not use the client after this call (use-after-free is invalid).
If the client may still be connected or has pending commands, the outcome is unspecified by this header (unknown); callers should ensure no further use.

functions.name: h2o_redis_command
functions.signature: h2o_redis_command_t *h2o_redis_command(h2o_redis_client_t *client, h2o_redis_command_cb cb, void *cb_data, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Submits a Redis command using a format string and variadic arguments, and registers a callback to receive the reply or an error. The callback is of type h2o_redis_command_cb and receives redisReply*, cb_data, and an error string on failure. The formatting rules for the command string are not documented in this header (unknown).
requirements: client must point to a valid h2o_redis_client_t, typically with an active connection to send the command (connection-state requirement is not explicitly documented; unknown).
cb must be a valid function pointer if the caller expects to receive the result or errors; whether NULL is permitted is not specified (unknown).
cb_data may be NULL; it is passed through to the callback as provided.
format must be a non-NULL pointer to a null-terminated format string; specific formatting semantics are not documented here (unknown).
Variadic arguments must match the expected placeholders in format (semantics unknown due to lack of documentation).

The returned h2o_redis_command_t*, if non-NULL, represents the enqueued command and must remain valid until completion according to the library's lifecycle; explicit lifetime management by the caller is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_redis_command_argv
functions.signature: h2o_redis_command_t *h2o_redis_command_argv(h2o_redis_client_t *client, h2o_redis_command_cb cb, void *cb_data, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Submits a Redis command using an argument vector and explicit lengths, registering a callback to receive the reply or an error. This form allows passing binary-safe arguments. The exact ownership and lifetime expectations for argv/argvlen during submission are not documented here.
requirements: client must point to a valid h2o_redis_client_t, typically connected (explicit requirement not stated; unknown).
cb must be a valid function pointer if the caller expects to receive the result or errors; whether NULL is permitted is not specified (unknown).
argc must be >= 0; it specifies the number of elements in argv and argvlen.
argv must be a non-NULL pointer to an array of argc pointers, each pointing to a buffer containing the argument bytes; each argv[i] must be non-NULL when argc > 0.
argvlen must be a non-NULL pointer to an array of argc sizes; each argvlen[i] specifies the length in bytes of argv[i].
The memory referenced by argv[i] must remain valid at least until the library has consumed the command (exact timing not specified; unknown).
cb_data may be NULL and is passed through to the callback as provided.
The returned h2o_redis_command_t*, if non-NULL, identifies the enqueued command; explicit lifetime management is not described (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_set_signal_handler
functions.description: Registers a signal handler for the specified signal number, similar to signal(3). Use it to install a custom callback that will be invoked when the process receives the given signal. Notes: handler code should be async-signal-safe; semantics are intended to mirror standard signal handler installation.
requirements: signo must be a valid POSIX signal number for the current platform.
cb must be a valid function pointer to a handler with signature void(int).
The code executed inside cb must adhere to async-signal-safety restrictions (only async-signal-safe functions may be called).
May need to be called early in program initialization to ensure the handler is in place before signals arrive (general signal-handling practice).

functions.name: h2o_setuidgid
functions.description: Changes the process user and group IDs to those associated with the specified username; described as equivalent to djb’s setuidgid. Typically used to drop privileges after binding sockets or during daemon startup. Return convention is not explicitly documented here.
requirements: user must be a non-NULL C string naming an existing user on the system.
The process must have sufficient privileges (typically running as root) to change its real/effective UID and GID.
Should be called before starting work that depends on the final privilege set; after successful call, filesystem and permission checks occur under the new user/group.

functions.name: h2o_server_starter_get_fds
functions.description: Obtains the list of listening socket file descriptors provided by Server::Starter via the SERVER_STARTER_PORT environment variable. Returns the number of descriptors on success, 0 if Server::Starter was not used, or (per comment) -1 on error (i.e., SIZE_MAX due to size_t). The output array contains the fds.
