requirements: _fds must be a valid pointer to an int* variable (non-NULL) that can receive the address of the fd array.

On success, the returned pointer *_fds refers to an array of int fds with length equal to the function’s return value; lifetime/ownership and whether the caller must free the array are not specified in this header (unknown).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates no fds provided; SIZE_MAX indicates error per the comment’s "-1 on error" note.
SERVER_STARTER_PORT environment variable format (example: "127.0.0.1:80=3;/tmp/sock=4") is used by the provider; the function depends on it if present.

functions.name: h2o_spawnp
functions.signature: pid_t h2o_spawnp(const char *cmd, char *const *argv, const int *mapped_fds, int clocexec_mutex_is_locked);
functions.description: Spawns a child process to execute cmd (searched via PATH like execvp) with the provided argv, while remapping or closing designated file descriptors before exec. mapped_fds lists pairs of (from_fd, to_fd) terminated by -1; each pair is dup2(from_fd, to_fd) if to_fd != -1, or close(from_fd) if to_fd == -1. Returns the child pid on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: cmd must be a non-NULL path or executable name resolvable via PATH.
argv must be a NULL-terminated argument vector (as per execvp conventions); argv[0] should typically be the program name (inferred from execvp usage).

If mapped_fds is non-NULL, it must point to an array of int containing pairs (from_fd, to_fd), terminated by a single -1 sentinel value. For each pair: if to_fd != -1 then dup2(from_fd, to_fd) will be attempted; if to_fd == -1 then close(from_fd) will be attempted.
All file descriptors referenced in mapped_fds must be valid in the calling process at the time of the call.
The caller must handle the returned pid_t: on -1, spawning failed; on success, the caller is responsible for reaping the child (e.g., waitpid).

clocexec_mutex_is_locked indicates whether a cloexec-related mutex is already held; pass the appropriate value consistent with the caller’s locking protocol (exact semantics beyond the flag are not documented here).

functions.name: h2o_read_command
functions.signature: int h2o_read_command(const char *cmd, char **argv, h2o_iovec_t std_in, h2o_buffer_t **resp, int *child_status);
functions.description: Executes a command with arguments, writes std_in to the command’s standard input, and captures its output. On success (function returns 0), resp receives the command’s output buffer and child_status receives the waitpid status of the child. Nonzero return indicates failure and output parameters are not valid.
requirements: cmd must be a non-NULL path or executable name resolvable via PATH.
argv must be a NULL-terminated vector of C strings for the child’s arguments (as per execvp conventions).

std_in supplies the bytes to write to the child process’s standard input; the expected structure of h2o_iovec_t is not defined here (unknown), but it should contain the data pointer/length (inferred from common iovec patterns).
If resp is non-NULL and the function returns 0, *resp will point to the captured output; the ownership/lifetime and required deallocation routine for h2o_buffer_t are not specified here (unknown).
If child_status is non-NULL and the function returns 0, *child_status will contain the status as returned by waitpid(child_pid).
The caller must check the function’s return value: only when it is 0 are resp and child_status outputs valid.
The caller is responsible for handling the child process termination semantics indicated by child_status (e.g., WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS).

functions.name: h2o_numproc
functions.description: Returns the number of processor cores available on the system. Useful for sizing thread pools or process workers.
requirements: No arguments required; may be called at any time.
Return value is the count of logical processors; exact definition (logical vs. physical) is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_sliding_counter_stop
functions.description: Stops a sliding counter at the specified timestamp and updates its aggregates. Intended to be paired with start to measure elapsed time windows.
requirements: counter must point to a valid, initialized h2o_sliding_counter_t (typically started via h2o_sliding_counter_start).
now is a timestamp in the same timebase/units used with start (uint64_t).

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_loop
functions.description: Returns the event loop associated with the given socket.
requirements: sock must be a valid h2o_socket_t pointer currently associated with a loop.

functions.name: h2o_socket_export
functions.description: Detaches a socket from its loop and exports its state into h2o_socket_export_t, allowing reattachment on another loop or thread.
requirements: sock must be open/valid when called.
info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for the exported data.
After a successful export, the socket is detached from its loop; use h2o_socket_import to attach to a loop.

functions.name: h2o_socket_import
functions.description: Attaches a previously exported socket (h2o_socket_export_t) to the given event loop and returns a new h2o_socket_t handle.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_loop_t.
info must point to a h2o_socket_export_t previously filled by h2o_socket_export and not yet disposed via h2o_socket_dispose_export.

functions.name: h2o_socket_dispose_export
functions.description: Destroys/cleans up an exported socket info structure created by h2o_socket_export.
requirements: info must point to a h2o_socket_export_t previously initialized by h2o_socket_export.
Call after import or when the exported info is no longer needed.

functions.name: h2o_socket_close
functions.description: Closes the socket and releases associated resources. If an on_close callback is set, it will be invoked.
requirements: sock must be a valid h2o_socket_t pointer.
Do not use the socket after this call.

functions.name: h2o_socket_notify_write
functions.description: Schedules a callback to be invoked when the socket becomes immediately writable.
requirements: sock must be valid and open.
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_fd
functions.description: Obtains the underlying file descriptor of the socket.
requirements: sock must be a valid h2o_socket_t associated with a file descriptor.

functions.name: h2o_socket_dont_read
functions.description: Sets or unsets the H2O_SOCKET_FLAG_DONT_READ flag. When set, the socket will only notify readability instead of automatically reading data.
requirements: sock must be valid.
dont_read is treated as a boolean; non-zero to set, zero to unset.

functions.name: h2o_socket_connect
functions.signature: h2o_socket_t *h2o_socket_connect(h2o_loop_t *loop, struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addrlen, h2o_socket_cb cb, const char **err);
functions.description: Initiates a non-blocking connection to the given peer address and returns a socket handle. The callback is invoked on success or error.
requirements: loop must be a valid event loop.
addr must point to a valid socket address; addrlen must be the size of the structure at addr.
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL) to receive completion notification.
err must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a string on immediate failure; on success it may remain unchanged.

functions.name: h2o_socket_do_prepare_for_latency_optimized_write
functions.description: Prepares internal state for latency-optimized writes based on the provided conditions and returns the suggested number of bytes to write (or SIZE_MAX on failure/no restriction).
requirements: sock must be valid.
conditions must point to a valid h2o_socket_latency_optimization_conditions_t describing thresholds (min_rtt, max_additional_delay, max_cwnd).

functions.name: h2o_socket_write
functions.signature: void h2o_socket_write(h2o_socket_t *sock, h2o_iovec_t *bufs, size_t bufcnt, h2o_socket_cb cb);
functions.description: Queues a write of the given buffers to the socket. The callback is invoked when the write completes or on error.
requirements: sock must be valid and open (and connected if applicable).
bufs must point to an array of at least bufcnt h2o_iovec_t entries; bufcnt may be zero to write nothing.
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).

functions.name: h2o_socket_sendvec
functions.signature: void h2o_socket_sendvec(h2o_socket_t *sock, h2o_sendvec_t *bufs, size_t bufcnt, h2o_socket_cb cb);
functions.description: Sends data described by send vectors, allowing deferred flattening or zero-copy where possible. The callback is invoked upon completion or error.
requirements: sock must be valid and open.
bufs must point to an array of at least bufcnt h2o_sendvec_t entries; bufcnt may be zero.
If a pull (non-raw) vector is used, its total size should not exceed H2O_PULL_SENDVEC_MAX_SIZE, and bufcnt must be 1 (per header notes).
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).

functions.name: h2o_socket_read_start
functions.description: Starts polling the socket for readability and calls the callback whenever data arrives at the TCP level. Arrival does not guarantee new application data (e.g., partial TLS records).
requirements: sock must be valid and open.
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).
Caller should tolerate callbacks when no new decrypted data is available (per note in comment).

functions.name: h2o_socket_read_stop
functions.description: Stops polling the socket for read events.
requirements: sock must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_socket_getsockname
functions.description: Retrieves the local address of the socket into the provided buffer and returns the length written (0 on failure).
requirements: sock must be valid.
sa must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold a socket address (e.g., struct sockaddr_storage).

functions.name: h2o_socket_getpeername
functions.description: Retrieves the remote peer address of the socket into the provided buffer and returns the length written (0 on failure).
requirements: sock must be valid.
sa must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold a socket address (e.g., struct sockaddr_storage).

functions.name: h2o_socket_setpeername
functions.signature: void h2o_socket_setpeername(h2o_socket_t *sock, struct sockaddr *sa, socklen_t len);
functions.description: Overrides the stored remote peer address for the socket.
requirements: sock must be valid.
sa must point to a valid socket address, and len must specify its size.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ptls
functions.description: Returns the underlying picotls connection object for a TLS-enabled socket, if available.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Only meaningful when the socket is using picotls; may return NULL otherwise.

functions.name: h2o_socket_can_tls_offload
functions.description: Indicates whether TLS offload (e.g., kTLS) can be used for this socket.
requirements: sock must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_tcp_congestion_controller
functions.description: Returns a string iovec describing the TCP congestion control algorithm in use for the socket, allocated from the provided pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t pointer for allocation.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_tcp_delivery_rate
functions.description: Returns a string iovec describing the TCP delivery rate for the socket, allocated from the provided pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t pointer for allocation.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ssl_protocol_version
functions.description: Returns the negotiated SSL/TLS protocol version string for the socket, or NULL if not applicable.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Only meaningful after or during a TLS handshake.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ssl_session_reused
functions.description: Returns whether the SSL/TLS session was reused (1), not reused (0), or may return other values if unknown.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS sockets.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ssl_cipher
functions.description: Returns the name of the negotiated SSL/TLS cipher suite, or NULL if not applicable.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS sockets.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ssl_cipher_bits
functions.description: Returns the effective number of bits of the negotiated SSL/TLS cipher, or a non-positive value if unknown.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS sockets.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ssl_session_id
functions.description: Returns the TLS session ID as an iovec, or an empty iovec if not available.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS sockets.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_ssl_server_name
functions.description: Returns the SNI server name associated with the TLS connection, or NULL if not set.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS sockets with SNI.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_cipher_bits
functions.description: Returns a string iovec of the cipher bits negotiated for the TLS connection, allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t pointer.
Applicable only for TLS sockets.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_session_id
functions.description: Returns a string iovec representation of the TLS session ID, allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS sockets.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_ech_config_id
functions.description: Returns a string iovec describing the ECH (Encrypted ClientHello) config ID if available, allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be valid.
Applicable only when ECH is used; may be empty otherwise.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_ech_kem
functions.description: Returns a string iovec describing the ECH KEM (key exchange mechanism) if available, allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be valid.
Applicable only when ECH is used; may be empty otherwise.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_ech_cipher
functions.description: Returns a string iovec describing the ECH cipher if available, allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be valid.
Applicable only when ECH is used; may be empty otherwise.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_ech_cipher_bits
functions.description: Returns a string iovec of the bit-length for the ECH cipher if available, allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be valid.
Applicable only when ECH is used; may be empty otherwise.

functions.name: h2o_socket_log_ssl_backend
functions.description: Returns a string iovec identifying the SSL backend in use (e.g., OpenSSL, BoringSSL), allocated from the pool.
requirements: sock must be valid.
pool must be valid.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_new_session_cb
functions.description: Callback to be hooked into SSL to notify when a new TLS session is created. Used for session caching.
requirements: s must be a valid SSL pointer.
sess must be a valid SSL_SESSION pointer.
Intended to be registered with the SSL library as a new session callback.

functions.name: h2o_socket_compare_address
functions.signature: int h2o_socket_compare_address(struct sockaddr *x, struct sockaddr *y, int check_port);
functions.description: Compares two socket addresses for equality. If check_port is non-zero, ports must also match.
requirements: x and y must point to valid socket address structures of the same family.
check_port determines whether ports are considered in the comparison.

functions.name: h2o_socket_getnumerichost
functions.signature: size_t h2o_socket_getnumerichost(const struct sockaddr *sa, socklen_t salen, char *buf);
functions.description: Numeric getnameinfo helper: writes the numeric host string for the given socket address into buf. Returns SIZE_MAX on failure.
requirements: sa must point to a valid socket address of length salen.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least NI_MAXHOST bytes (per comment).

functions.name: h2o_socket_getport
functions.description: Returns the port number from the socket address, or -1 on failure.
requirements: sa must point to a valid socket address.

functions.name: h2o_socket_get_error_string
functions.description: Converts known socket-related error numbers to human-readable strings; returns default_err if the error is unknown.
requirements: default_err should be a valid string pointer to use as fallback.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_handshake
functions.signature: void h2o_socket_ssl_handshake(h2o_socket_t *sock, SSL_CTX *ssl_ctx, const char *server_name, h2o_iovec_t alpn_protos, h2o_socket_cb handshake_cb);
functions.description: Performs a TLS handshake on the socket using the provided SSL_CTX. Optionally supplies a server_name (SNI) and ALPN protocol list. Invokes handshake_cb when the handshake completes or fails.
requirements: sock must be a valid connected socket.
ssl_ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX configured for client or server use as appropriate.
server_name may be NULL or a valid SNI name string.
alpn_protos is a byte buffer of protocols in wire format expected by the implementation.
handshake_cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_resume_server_handshake
functions.description: Resumes a server-side TLS handshake using provided session data (or {NULL,0} if unavailable).
requirements: sock must be a valid socket in server handshake context.
session_data.base may be NULL with length 0 to indicate no session data.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_async_resumption_init
functions.description: Registers callbacks for handling TLS session data for asynchronous resumption (get and new).
requirements: get_cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL) to obtain session data asynchronously.
new_cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL) to store new session data.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_async_resumption_setup_ctx
functions.description: Configures the SSL context to use asynchronous session resumption handling as registered.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
h2o_socket_ssl_async_resumption_init should be called before setting up the context.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_get_selected_protocol
functions.description: Returns the protocol selected by ALPN or NPN (ALPN takes precedence) as an iovec.
requirements: sock must be valid.
Meaningful only for TLS sockets with negotiated ALPN/NPN.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_is_early_data
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the TLS socket is in early-data (0-RTT) state (ClientFinished not yet seen).
requirements: sock must be valid.
Applicable only for TLS 1.3 early data contexts.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_get_picotls_context
functions.description: Obtains the picotls context associated with the given OpenSSL SSL_CTX.
requirements: ossl must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_set_picotls_context
functions.description: Associates a picotls context with the given OpenSSL SSL_CTX for use by the socket layer.
requirements: ossl must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
ptls must be a valid picotls context pointer.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_get_session_cache
functions.description: Gets the session cache object associated with the SSL context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_set_session_cache
functions.description: Sets the session cache object to be used by the SSL context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
cache may be NULL to clear, or a valid h2o_cache_t pointer.

functions.name: h2o_socket_ssl_destroy_session_cache_entry
functions.description: Destroys or frees resources associated with a session cache entry stored in an iovec.
requirements: value must contain the session data to be destroyed; interpretation is implementation-defined.

functions.name: h2o_ssl_register_alpn_protocols
functions.description: Registers the list of protocols to advertise via ALPN on the given SSL context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
protocols must point to a list/array of h2o_iovec_t protocol identifiers in the expected format; the array lifetime must outlive context setup.

functions.name: h2o_ssl_register_npn_protocols
functions.description: Registers the NPN protocol list string on the SSL context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
protocols must be a valid NUL-terminated string in the expected NPN wire/list format.

functions.name: h2o_socket_set_df_bit
functions.description: Attempts to set the DF (Don't Fragment) bit on the socket for the given address family. Returns true on success or when the OS lacks necessary features (operation can continue either way).
requirements: fd must be a valid socket file descriptor.
domain should be the socket domain (e.g., AF_INET or AF_INET6).

functions.name: h2o_sendvec_init_raw
functions.signature: void h2o_sendvec_init_raw(h2o_sendvec_t *vec, const void *base, size_t len);
functions.description: Initializes a send vector to reference a mutable memory region directly. Enables reusing or releasing the memory when sending proceeds.
requirements: vec must point to writable h2o_sendvec_t storage.
base must point to a memory region of at least len bytes; the region must remain valid until send completes.

functions.name: h2o_sendvec_read_raw
functions.description: Callback implementation to load raw bytes from a send vector into dst. Makes the data available via h2o_sendvec_t::raw when used as the read_ callback.
requirements: vec must have been properly initialized (e.g., via h2o_sendvec_init_raw or an equivalent).
dst must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len should not exceed the remaining length of vec->len.

functions.name: h2o_socket_clear_recycle
functions.description: Garbage-collects internal resources related to socket buffer recycling. If full is set, performs a full cleanup.
requirements: full is treated as a boolean flag.

functions.name: h2o_socket_recycle_is_empty
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the socket recycle pool is empty.

functions.name: h2o_sendfile
functions.signature: size_t h2o_sendfile(int sockfd, int filefd, off_t off, size_t len);
functions.description: Thin wrapper around sendfile(2) to normalize behavior across OSes. Returns bytes written (0 is valid, indicating send buffer full) or SIZE_MAX on error.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid, writable socket descriptor.
filefd must be a valid file descriptor opened for reading.
off is the starting offset within the file; implementation may update the file offset or use off directly depending on OS semantics.
len is the maximum number of bytes to send.

functions.name: h2o_socket_boringssl_get_async_job_index
functions.description: Returns the SSL_[gs]et_ext_data index used to store ptls_async_job_t for async TLS handshake signature generation (BoringSSL-specific).
requirements: Available only when compiled with OPENSSL_IS_BORINGSSL.

functions.name: h2o_socket_boringssl_async_resumption_in_flight
functions.description: Returns non-zero if async resumption is in flight for the given SSL object. When true, the handshake will be discarded and async signature callback should fail rather than start.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.
Available only when compiled with OPENSSL_IS_BORINGSSL.

functions.name: h2o_socket_start_async_handshake
functions.signature: void h2o_socket_start_async_handshake(h2o_loop_t *loop, int async_fd, void *data, h2o_socket_cb cb);
functions.description: Sets up waiting for a notification on async_fd to resume an asynchronous TLS handshake. The callback must call h2o_socket_async_handshake_on_notify to finalize and to obtain the data pointer.
requirements: Available only when H2O_CAN_OSSL_ASYNC is enabled.
loop must be a valid event loop.
async_fd must be a valid file descriptor that becomes readable/writable to signal completion.
data is an opaque pointer passed through; the callback is expected to retrieve it via h2o_socket_async_handshake_on_notify.
cb must be a valid function pointer (non-NULL).

functions.name: h2o_socket_async_handshake_on_notify
functions.description: To be called by the notification callback set by h2o_socket_start_async_handshake. Performs necessary cleanup and returns the original data pointer supplied at start.
requirements: Available only when H2O_CAN_OSSL_ASYNC is enabled.
async_sock must be the async notification socket provided to the callback.
err may be NULL or a string describing an error.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_socket_create
functions.description: Creates an event-loop-managed socket object for an existing file descriptor, associated with the given event loop. Typical usage is to wrap a connected or listening socket after creating/opening it elsewhere, so it can be polled by the loop.
requirements: loop must be a valid pointer to an h2o_evloop_t instance (typically created by h2o_evloop_create).
fd must be a valid open socket file descriptor.
flags is a bitmask; valid values are not documented here, but may include H2O_SOCKET_FLAG_* defined in this header.
The returned h2o_socket_t* must be managed and eventually disposed by the caller via the appropriate h2o socket APIs (not shown here).

functions.name: h2o_evloop_socket_accept
functions.description: Accepts a new incoming connection from a listener socket and returns a new event-loop-managed socket for the accepted connection.
requirements: listener must be a valid listener socket compatible with this event loop (created/registered through this library).
listener must represent a listening socket; behavior for non-listener sockets is undefined.
Error handling and return-on-failure behavior are not documented in this header; callers should check for a NULL return and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_socket_set_max_read_size
functions.description: Sets the per-read upper bound on the number of bytes read from the socket in one operation. Default is 1 MB.
requirements: sock must be a valid h2o_socket_t* created for this event loop.
max_size defines the maximum read size per read call; must be set to an appropriate value for the application. No explicit bounds are documented here.
Callers should ensure this function is called before initiating reads if they need a non-default limit.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_create
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new event loop instance.
requirements: Must be paired with h2o_evloop_destroy to release resources.
Returns a pointer to a new loop or possibly NULL on failure (not documented here); callers should handle allocation failures appropriately.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an event loop instance and frees associated resources.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t* previously returned by h2o_evloop_create.
The loop should not be used after destruction.
Callers should ensure no outstanding operations depend on the loop at the time of destruction.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_run
functions.description: Runs one iteration of the event loop, waiting up to max_wait (units not specified here) for events. Returns 0 on success; returns -1 if a system call error aborts the operation (commonly due to EINTR). On error, consult errno and rerun the loop if appropriate.
requirements: loop must be a valid event loop created by h2o_evloop_create.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates an error and errno should be inspected.
If -1 is returned due to EINTR, the caller may rerun the loop as needed.
max_wait is a signed 32-bit value; the exact units and valid range are not specified in this header.

functions.name: h2o_timer_init
functions.description: Initializes a timer entry. This is a macro alias to h2o_timerwheel_init_entry. The exact signature is not provided in this header; based on typedefs, it operates on h2o_timer_t (alias of h2o_timerwheel_entry_t).
requirements: Because this is a macro mapping to h2o_timerwheel_init_entry, include and link against the timerwheel API providing that symbol.
The exact parameter list and constraints are not specified here; consult the timerwheel header for definitive requirements.

functions.name: h2o_timer_is_linked
functions.description: Checks whether a timer is currently linked/scheduled. This is a macro alias to h2o_timerwheel_is_linked. The precise signature is not provided in this header.
requirements: Relies on the timerwheel API; consult that API for exact parameter and return type.
Expected to accept a pointer to h2o_timer_t (timer entry) and return a truthy value if linked, but the exact details are not specified here.

functions.name: h2o_timer_link
functions.signature: inline void h2o_timer_link(h2o_evloop_t *loop, uint64_t delay_ticks, h2o_timer_t *timer);
functions.description: Schedules (links) a timer to fire at the current loop time plus delay_ticks. Internally links the timer into the loop’s timer wheel at absolute time now + delay_ticks.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t* with an initialized timer wheel (_timeouts).
timer must be a valid h2o_timer_t* (timerwheel entry).
delay_ticks is an absolute delay in the loop’s tick units (milliseconds as implied by _now_millisec naming), but exact units are not explicitly documented here.
The timer should be initialized (via h2o_timer_init) before linking.
Do not link a timer that is already linked; use h2o_timer_is_linked to check or unlink first.

functions.name: h2o_timer_unlink
functions.description: Unlinks (cancels) a previously linked timer. This is a macro alias to h2o_timerwheel_unlink. The exact signature is not provided in this header.
requirements: Requires the timerwheel API; consult that API for the exact parameter type and behavior.
Only call on timers that may be linked; behavior of unlinking an unlinked timer depends on the timerwheel implementation.

functions.name: h2o_gettimeofday
functions.description: Returns the event loop’s cached gettimeofday result (the time at which the loop was last updated).
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t*.
Returned time is cached within the loop; it may not represent the current wall-clock time outside an iteration.

functions.name: h2o_now
functions.description: Returns the loop’s current time in milliseconds, as maintained by the loop.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t*.
Value is loop-maintained time and may lag real time until the loop updates its clock.

functions.name: h2o_now_nanosec
functions.description: Returns the loop’s current time in nanoseconds, as maintained by the loop.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t*.
Value is loop-maintained time and may lag real time until the loop updates its clock.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_get_execution_time_millisec
functions.description: Returns the loop’s average execution time per iteration in milliseconds, derived from exec_time_nanosec_counter.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t*.
Interpretation depends on how exec_time_nanosec_counter is maintained elsewhere.

functions.name: h2o_evloop_get_execution_time_nanosec
functions.description: Returns the loop’s average execution time per iteration in nanoseconds, from exec_time_nanosec_counter.
requirements: loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t*.
Interpretation depends on how exec_time_nanosec_counter is maintained elsewhere.

functions.name: h2o_evloop__io_uring
functions.description: Returns the loop’s internal io_uring context. This symbol is only available when compiled with H2O_USE_IO_URING enabled.
requirements: Only available if H2O_USE_IO_URING is defined at build time; callers should guard usage with the same macro.
loop must be a valid h2o_evloop_t*.
Returned pointer is to an internal structure; usage is intended for internal or advanced integrations.

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_init_specific
functions.signature: void h2o_socketpool_init_specific(h2o_socketpool_t *pool, size_t capacity, h2o_socketpool_target_t **targets, size_t num_targets, h2o_balancer_t *balancer);
functions.description: Initializes a socket pool with a specific set of backend targets and an optional balancer. Use this when you know all targets (endpoints) up front and want per-target pooling and load-balancing behavior.
requirements: pool must be a valid, writable pointer to an h2o_socketpool_t structure
targets must point to an array of h2o_socketpool_target_t* of length num_targets, or be NULL only if num_targets is 0
num_targets must correctly specify the number of entries in targets
capacity must be a non-zero size designating the maximum number of connections governed by the pool (exact semantics beyond this are not documented)
balancer may be NULL or a valid h2o_balancer_t pointer
Call before using the pool with other APIs like connect/register_loop

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_init_global
functions.description: Initializes a global socket pool. A global pool is shared and not tied to specific targets at initialization time.
requirements: pool must be a valid, writable pointer to an h2o_socketpool_t structure
capacity must be a non-zero size indicating the maximum number of connections governed by the pool
Call before using other pool operations (e.g., register_loop, connect)

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_dispose
functions.description: Disposes of a socket pool, releasing resources and closing/forgetting pooled connections.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized socket pool
After disposal, the pool pointer must not be used with other socket pool functions
Ensure there are no outstanding connect requests or leased sockets prior to disposal (not explicitly stated; recommended based on typical pooling semantics)

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_is_global
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given pool is a global pool, zero otherwise.
requirements: pool must be a valid pointer to an h2o_socketpool_t

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_create_target
functions.description: Creates a pool target from an origin URL and optional per-target load-balancer configuration. If lb_target_conf is NULL, a default configuration is used. Use with h2o_socketpool_init_specific.
requirements: origin must be a valid pointer to a populated h2o_url_t describing the target endpoint
lb_target_conf may be NULL to use defaults, or a valid pointer whose fields (e.g., weight_m1) are in documented ranges (weight is within [1, 256] via weight_m1 storage)
The returned target must be destroyed with h2o_socketpool_destroy_target when no longer needed

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_destroy_target
functions.description: Destroys a target previously created with h2o_socketpool_create_target, releasing its resources.
requirements: target must be a pointer previously returned by h2o_socketpool_create_target
Do not use the target after destruction
Ensure the target is not in use by any live pool before destroying (not explicitly stated; inferred from typical usage)

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_get_timeout
functions.description: Returns the current pool timeout in milliseconds.
requirements: pool must be a valid pointer to an initialized h2o_socketpool_t

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_set_timeout
functions.description: Sets the pool timeout in milliseconds. This likely controls connection idle timeout or operation timeout for the pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid pointer to an initialized h2o_socketpool_t
msec is an unsigned 64-bit millisecond value; no explicit range constraints are documented

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_set_ssl_ctx
functions.description: Associates an OpenSSL SSL_CTX with the socket pool, enabling TLS for connections originating from this pool (e.g., HTTPS or TLS-over-TCP).
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized socket pool
ssl_ctx may be NULL to disable TLS, or a valid SSL_CTX pointer prepared for client connections (exact expectations not documented)
Call before initiating TLS connections where SNI/verification may rely on pool/target settings

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_register_loop
functions.description: Associates an event loop with the socket pool, likely to run periodic timers and asynchronous operations for the pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized socket pool
loop must be a valid pointer to an h2o_loop_t
Must be called before pool operations that require a loop-managed timer/interval (inferred from presence of _interval_cb)

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_unregister_loop
functions.description: Unregisters a previously associated event loop from the socket pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized socket pool
loop must be the same h2o_loop_t previously registered with this pool
Ensure there are no pending operations depending on the loop before unregistering (not explicitly stated; inferred)

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_connect
functions.signature: void h2o_socketpool_connect(h2o_socketpool_connect_request_t **_req, h2o_socketpool_t *pool, h2o_url_t *url, h2o_loop_t *loop, h2o_multithread_receiver_t *getaddr_receiver, h2o_iovec_t alpn_protos, h2o_socketpool_connect_cb cb, void *data);
functions.description: Initiates a connection to the given URL using the socket pool, or returns a pooled connection if available. Asynchronous; completion is reported via the callback with either a connected socket or an error string. The request handle can be used to cancel the operation.
requirements: _req must be a valid pointer to a h2o_socketpool_connect_request_t* storage location if the caller wishes to cancel later; may be NULL if the handle is not needed (not explicitly stated; inferred from double-pointer pattern)
pool must be a valid, initialized socket pool (global or specific)
url must be a valid pointer to a h2o_url_t describing the desired endpoint
loop must be a valid h2o_loop_t on which the connection will run
getaddr_receiver must be a valid h2o_multithread_receiver_t to receive DNS resolution results (used for asynchronous getaddrinfo)
alpn_protos is an h2o_iovec_t specifying ALPN protocols; may be empty if not using ALPN (not explicitly stated)

cb must be a non-NULL function pointer; it will be invoked with (sock, errstr, data, url) where either sock is non-NULL and errstr is NULL on success, or sock is NULL and errstr is non-NULL on error (callback contract inferred from signature)
data is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback
Caller must not use or free the socket after handing it back to the pool via h2o_socketpool_return or detach

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_cancel_connect
functions.description: Cancels a pending connect request previously initiated with h2o_socketpool_connect.
requirements: req must be a valid request handle previously obtained from h2o_socketpool_connect (via the _req out-parameter)
Must be called before the connect operation completes to be effective

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_return
functions.description: Returns an idle socket back to the pool for reuse. Returns an integer status (non-zero typically indicates success).
requirements: pool must be the socket pool that owns the socket
sock must be an idling socket obtained from this pool (i.e., not currently in use)
After returning, the caller must not use the socket unless re-leased via the pool
Function determines ownership using pool bookkeeping; using sockets not owned by the pool is invalid

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_detach
functions.description: Detaches a socket from the pool so it is no longer managed/returned to the pool. Use when the application intends to take exclusive ownership and not return it.
requirements: pool must be a valid socket pool
sock must be a socket currently associated with the pool
After detaching, the socket will not be pooled; the application becomes responsible for closing it

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_is_owned_socket
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given socket belongs to the pool, zero otherwise. Internally checks if sock->on_close.data == pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid socket pool pointer
sock must be a valid pointer to an h2o_socket_t
Only reliable for sockets created/managed by this library, where on_close.data is assigned

functions.name: h2o_socketpool_can_keepalive
functions.description: Determines if connections managed by the pool can be kept alive (details not documented). Likely checks pool state/capacity/policy to indicate whether idle connections should be preserved.
requirements: pool must be a valid pointer to an initialized h2o_socketpool_t

functions.name: h2o_strdup
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_strdup(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Duplicates a string into a newly allocated buffer and returns it as an h2o_iovec_t. If len == SIZE_MAX, strlen(s) is used. The returned buffer is NUL-terminated, but the iovec length excludes the NUL. Use when needing a pooled or heap-allocated copy of a string.
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
s must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes (or a NUL-terminated string if len == SIZE_MAX)
Returned iovec.base points to NUL-terminated memory; iovec.len does not include the NUL
Caller is responsible for lifetime management according to allocation source (pool vs malloc)

functions.name: h2o_strdup_shared
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_strdup_shared(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Variant of h2o_strdup that allocates the duplicated string using shared allocation (h2o_mem_alloc_shared). Returns an h2o_iovec_t pointing to a NUL-terminated copy (length excludes NUL).
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
s must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes (or a NUL-terminated string if len == SIZE_MAX)
Returned iovec.base is NUL-terminated; iovec.len excludes the NUL
Follow shared-allocation lifetime rules as defined by h2o_mem_alloc_shared

functions.name: h2o_strdup_slashed
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_strdup_slashed(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Duplicates a string, appending a trailing '/' if one is not present. Returns an h2o_iovec_t with NUL-terminated memory (length excludes NUL). Useful for normalizing directory-like paths.
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
s must be a valid pointer to at least len bytes (or a NUL-terminated string if len == SIZE_MAX)
Returned iovec.base is NUL-terminated; iovec.len excludes the NUL

functions.name: h2o_tolower
functions.description: Lowercases an ASCII uppercase letter; otherwise returns the character unchanged. Equivalent to a fast tolower for 'A'-'Z'.
requirements: Input ch should be an int representing an unsigned char or EOF-like integer; behavior is defined for ASCII range

functions.name: h2o_strtolower
functions.description: In-place lowercase conversion of the first len bytes of s (ASCII: 'A'-'Z' to 'a'-'z').
requirements: s must be a writable buffer of at least len bytes
Only ASCII letters are affected; other bytes are left unchanged

functions.name: h2o_strcopytolower
functions.signature: inline void h2o_strcopytolower(char *d, const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Copies len bytes from s to d while converting ASCII uppercase letters to lowercase. Destination receives exactly len bytes.
requirements: d must be a writable buffer of at least len bytes
s must point to at least len readable bytes
Conversion only affects ASCII letters

functions.name: h2o_toupper
functions.description: Uppercases an ASCII lowercase letter; otherwise returns the character unchanged. Equivalent to a fast toupper for 'a'-'z'.
requirements: Input ch should be an int representing an unsigned char or EOF-like integer; behavior is defined for ASCII range

functions.name: h2o_strtoupper
functions.description: In-place uppercase conversion of the first len bytes of s (ASCII: 'a'-'z' to 'A'-'Z').
requirements: s must be a writable buffer of at least len bytes
Only ASCII letters are affected; other bytes are left unchanged

functions.name: h2o_lcstris
functions.signature: inline int h2o_lcstris(const char *target, size_t target_len, const char *test, size_t test_len);
functions.description: Case-insensitive equality test implemented by comparing the lowercase views of the two strings. Returns non-zero if equal, zero otherwise. Only proceeds when lengths match.
requirements: target must point to at least target_len bytes; test must point to at least test_len bytes
Comparison is ASCII case-folding via lowercase; bytes outside ASCII letters compare byte-for-byte
If target_len != test_len, function returns 0

functions.name: h2o_base64_encode_capacity
functions.description: Computes the buffer capacity needed to base64-encode len bytes, including space for a trailing '\0'.
requirements: Use the returned value to size the destination buffer for h2o_base64_encode

functions.name: h2o_strtosize
functions.description: Parses a positive number from the given string segment. Returns the parsed value or SIZE_MAX on failure.
requirements: s must point to at least len bytes
Accepts only positive numbers; failure returns SIZE_MAX
Caller must check for SIZE_MAX to detect errors

functions.name: h2o_strtosizefwd
functions.description: Parses the first positive number starting at *s within a string of length len. Advances *s to just after the parsed number or to end of string. Returns the number or SIZE_MAX on failure.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* pointing to the current scan position
The memory referenced by *s must contain at least len bytes from the original start; function will advance *s
Caller must check for SIZE_MAX to detect errors

functions.name: h2o_decode_base64url
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_decode_base64url(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *src, size_t len);
functions.description: Decodes a base64url-encoded string into binary. Returns an h2o_iovec_t containing the decoded bytes (length in .len). Allocation uses pool or malloc if pool == NULL.
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
src must point to at least len bytes of base64url text
Caller should validate result length; error signaling specifics are not documented in this header (unknown)

functions.name: h2o_base64_encode
functions.signature: size_t h2o_base64_encode(char *dst, const void *src, size_t len, int url_encoded);
functions.description: Encodes binary data to base64 (standard or URL-safe) into dst and appends a trailing '\0'. Returns the number of bytes written excluding the NUL (typical for such encoders; exact return semantics not explicitly documented).
requirements: dst must have capacity at least h2o_base64_encode_capacity(len) bytes
src must point to at least len readable bytes
Set url_encoded non-zero to produce URL-safe base64 ('-' and '_' instead of '+' and '/')

functions.name: h2o_hex_decode
functions.signature: int h2o_hex_decode(void *dst, const char *src, size_t src_len);
functions.description: Decodes a hexadecimal ASCII string into binary written to dst. Return value is an int status (exact convention not specified in header; unknown).
requirements: dst must have capacity of at least src_len/2 bytes
src must point to src_len bytes of hex characters; src_len should be even for valid hex decoding
Caller must interpret the return int according to library conventions (unspecified here)

functions.name: h2o_hex_encode
functions.signature: void h2o_hex_encode(char *dst, const void *src, size_t src_len);
functions.description: Encodes binary data into a hexadecimal string, writing 2*src_len hex chars and appending a '\0'.
requirements: dst must have capacity of at least 2*src_len + 1 bytes
src must point to at least src_len readable bytes
Output is NUL-terminated; no return value

functions.name: h2o_uri_escape
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_uri_escape(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *s, size_t l, const char *preserve_chars);
functions.description: Percent-encodes a string per RFC 3986. Characters listed in preserve_chars are left unescaped. Returns an h2o_iovec_t whose base is NUL-terminated (NUL not counted in .len).
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
s must point to at least l bytes
preserve_chars may be NULL or a C-string of characters to preserve

functions.name: h2o_uri_unescape
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_uri_unescape(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *s, size_t l);
functions.description: Decodes a percent-encoded string per RFC 3986 Section 2.1. Returns a NUL-terminated decoded string in an h2o_iovec_t (NUL not counted in .len), or {NULL, 0} if decoding fails.
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
s must point to at least l bytes
Caller must check for failure by testing returned iovec.base == NULL and .len == 0

functions.name: h2o_get_filext
functions.description: Returns the extension portion of a path as an h2o_iovec_t slice (likely without allocation).
requirements: path must point to at least len bytes
Behavior for paths without an extension is not documented here (unknown)

functions.name: h2o_str_stripws
functions.description: Returns a view (h2o_iovec_t) of the string with surrounding whitespace removed.
requirements: s must point to at least len bytes
Definition of whitespace is not detailed here (unknown)

functions.name: h2o_strstr
functions.signature: size_t h2o_strstr(const char *haysack, size_t haysack_len, const char *needle, size_t needle_len);
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of needle within the given haystack slice. Returns the offset within haysack or SIZE_MAX if not found.
requirements: haysack must point to at least haysack_len bytes
needle must point to at least needle_len bytes
Caller must check for SIZE_MAX to detect not-found

functions.name: h2o_next_token
functions.signature: const char *h2o_next_token(h2o_iovec_t *iter, int inner, int outer, size_t *element_len, h2o_iovec_t *value);
functions.description: Parses a string into tokens or name-value pairs using inner and outer separators (RFC-style lists). On each call, returns a pointer to the next token and sets *element_len. If value is non-NULL and the element contains '=', returns the value range via *value and the name as the token. Returns NULL when input is fully consumed. Suitable for parsing header field values like Cache-Control.
requirements: On first call, iter->base must point to the full string and iter->len set to its length; the function will advance iter internally
inner specifies token separator; outer specifies outer-list separator for nested lists (use same as inner for flat lists)
element_len must be a non-NULL pointer to receive token length
value may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the value range when '=' is present
Caller should loop until return value is NULL to consume all tokens

functions.name: h2o_contains_token
functions.signature: int h2o_contains_token(const char *haysack, size_t haysack_len, const char *needle, size_t needle_len, int separator);
functions.description: Tests if needle exists as a token within a separator-separated string (used for handling RFC 2616-style token lists). Returns non-zero if found.
requirements: haysack must point to at least haysack_len bytes
needle must point to at least needle_len bytes
separator must be the character used to separate tokens in haysack

functions.name: h2o_htmlescape
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_htmlescape(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *src, size_t len);
functions.description: HTML-escapes a string (e.g., replaces special characters with entities). Returns the escaped string, or returns the original source if no escaping was necessary.
requirements: pool must be a valid memory pool; behavior for pool == NULL is not specified here (unknown)
src must point to at least len bytes
Returned iovec may alias src when no escaping is necessary; do not free or modify prematurely

functions.name: h2o_concat_list
functions.description: Concatenates a list of h2o_iovec_t buffers into a single NUL-terminated buffer and returns it as an h2o_iovec_t (length excludes NUL).
requirements: pool must be a valid memory pool (may accept NULL to malloc based on library conventions; not explicitly stated here, unknown)
list must point to an array of at least count h2o_iovec_t elements
Resulting buffer is NUL-terminated; iovec.len excludes the NUL

functions.name: h2o_join_list
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_join_list(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_iovec_t *list, size_t count, h2o_iovec_t delimiter);
functions.description: Joins a list of iovecs inserting delimiter between elements, returning a single NUL-terminated buffer as h2o_iovec_t (length excludes NUL).
requirements: pool must be a valid memory pool (may accept NULL to malloc depending on implementation; not specified here)
list must point to an array of at least count h2o_iovec_t elements
delimiter is an h2o_iovec_t inserted between elements; its .len may be zero
Resulting buffer is NUL-terminated; iovec.len excludes the NUL

functions.name: h2o_split
functions.signature: void h2o_split(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, h2o_iovec_vector_t *list, h2o_iovec_t str, const char needle);
functions.description: Splits str by the given needle character and writes the segments into list (an h2o_iovec_vector_t).
requirements: pool must be a valid memory pool (allocation behavior not further documented here)
list must be a valid pointer to an h2o_iovec_vector_t to receive results
str contains the source buffer and length; str.base must be non-NULL if str.len > 0

functions.name: h2o_str_at_position
functions.signature: int h2o_str_at_position(char *buf, const char *src, size_t src_len, int lineno, int column);
functions.description: Emits a two-line indicator string into buf that graphically points to the specified (lineno, column) within src. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: buf must be a writable buffer large enough to hold the two-line output (required size not specified; unknown)
src must point to at least src_len bytes
lineno and column specify the 1-based (assumed) position; exact indexing convention not specified here (unknown)
Caller should check for return value 0 indicating success

functions.name: h2o__lcstris_core
functions.signature: int h2o__lcstris_core(const char *target, const char *test, size_t test_len);
functions.description: Core routine used by h2o_lcstris to compare target and test for case-insensitive equality using lowercase comparison over test_len bytes. Intended for internal use.
requirements: target must point to at least test_len bytes; test must point to at least test_len bytes
For correct equality semantics, the caller should ensure the true target length equals test_len (as done by h2o_lcstris)

functions.name: h2o_encode_sf_string
functions.signature: h2o_iovec_t h2o_encode_sf_string(h2o_mem_pool_t *pool, const char *s, size_t slen);
functions.description: Encodes a Structured Field Value (RFC 8941) of type String (sf-string). If slen == SIZE_MAX, strlen(s) is used. Returns a NUL-terminated encoded string as h2o_iovec_t (length excludes NUL).
requirements: pool may be NULL to use malloc; otherwise must be a valid h2o_mem_pool_t*
s must point to at least slen bytes (or be NUL-terminated if slen == SIZE_MAX)
Returned iovec.base is NUL-terminated; iovec.len excludes the NUL

functions.name: h2o_time2str_rfc1123
functions.description: Formats the given UTC time (in struct tm) as an RFC-1123 HTTP-date string (e.g., "Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT") and writes it into buf. Intended for generating HTTP Date headers or similar uses. The string is fixed-length and should be NUL-terminated.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least H2O_TIMESTR_RFC1123_LEN + 1 bytes to accommodate the terminating NUL.
gmt must be a valid pointer to a populated struct tm representing time in GMT/UTC (caller is responsible for providing a UTC-normalized tm).
Function does not take the buffer length; caller must ensure sufficient space to avoid overflow.
buf must remain valid for the duration of the call; contents are overwritten.

functions.name: h2o_time_parse_rfc1123
functions.signature: int h2o_time_parse_rfc1123(const char *s, size_t len, struct tm *tm);
functions.description: Parses an HTTP-date string in RFC-1123 format from the input buffer s of length len and stores the broken-down time into tm. Intended for consuming HTTP Date/Expires headers. Return value semantics are not documented in this header; likely indicates success/failure, but exact conventions are unknown.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a buffer containing the RFC-1123 date text; it need not be NUL-terminated as len specifies the length.
len must be the number of bytes available at s that comprise the date string.
tm must be a non-null pointer to a writable struct tm to receive the parsed result.
Input must be formatted as an RFC-1123 HTTP-date (e.g., "Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT"); other formats may fail to parse.
Return value meaning is unspecified in this header; callers should consult implementation or higher-level documentation to interpret the int result.

functions.name: h2o_time2str_log
functions.description: Formats the given time_t as an Apache log-style timestamp (e.g., "29/Aug/2014:15:34:38 +0900") and writes it into buf. Useful for access/error log entries. The result should be NUL-terminated and fixed-length.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least H2O_TIMESTR_LOG_LEN + 1 bytes to accommodate the terminating NUL.
time is the time value to format; no special state is required.
Function does not take the buffer length; caller must ensure sufficient space to avoid overflow.
buf must remain valid for the duration of the call; contents are overwritten.

functions.name: h2o_timeval_subtract
functions.signature: static inline int64_t h2o_timeval_subtract(struct timeval *from, struct timeval *until);
functions.description: Computes the difference between two struct timeval values as (until - from) in microseconds and returns the signed 64-bit delta. Negative values are possible if until precedes from. Intended for interval/duration calculations.
requirements: from must be a non-null pointer to a valid struct timeval.
until must be a non-null pointer to a valid struct timeval.
The calculation internally casts tv_sec to int32_t; accuracy/defined behavior is only guaranteed when both tv_sec values fit within int32_t range.
No overflow checking is performed; extremely large absolute differences may overflow the 64-bit accumulation if inputs are outside typical timeval ranges.

functions.name: h2o_timeval_is_null
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given timeval is considered "null" by this library, defined as tv->tv_sec == 0; otherwise returns 0. Useful as a simple sentinel check.
requirements: tv must be a non-null pointer to a valid struct timeval.
Only tv_sec is checked; tv_usec is ignored. Callers should not assume any other notion of nullness.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_link_abs
functions.description: Activates/schedules a timerwheel entry to expire at an absolute timestamp. Intended usage: initialize an entry with a callback via h2o_timerwheel_init_entry, then call this function with a timerwheel context and the absolute expiration time to arm the timer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context previously created by h2o_timerwheel_create.
entry must be a valid pointer to a h2o_timerwheel_entry_t; typically initialized by h2o_timerwheel_init_entry before linking.
The at parameter is an absolute expiration time in the same time base used by the timerwheel (type uint64_t).

If the entry is already linked/active, behavior is unspecified by this header; callers should ensure the entry is not currently linked (use h2o_timerwheel_is_linked) or unlink it first (h2o_timerwheel_unlink).

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_create
functions.description: Creates and initializes a timerwheel context. Returns an opaque pointer to be used with other timerwheel APIs. Expected usage: call once per timerwheel you need, then pass the returned context to link, run, and destroy functions.
requirements: num_wheels specifies the number of wheels (hierarchical levels); must be a valid size_t; exact constraints are not documented here.
now is the current absolute time (uint64_t) establishing the initial time base for the wheel; must match the same time base used for future at/now values.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a timerwheel context and releases its resources. Expected usage: call once when you are finished with the timerwheel created by h2o_timerwheel_create.
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context obtained from h2o_timerwheel_create.
After this call, ctx must not be used again.

Behavior regarding any still-linked entries is not specified in this header; callers should ensure no required callbacks remain pending or handle that according to the implementation’s behavior (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_dump
functions.description: Displays (prints/logs) the contents/state of the timerwheel for debugging or inspection.
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_validate
functions.description: Validates internal consistency of the timerwheel and returns the result as a boolean-like value (nonzero for valid, zero for invalid). Intended for diagnostics or debug checks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_get_wake_at
functions.description: Returns information used to determine when to wake to service the next timer. Note: The comment says it returns the remaining time until the next timer triggers, while the name suggests an absolute wake time; the exact semantics (absolute vs. relative) are ambiguous in this header.
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context.
Callers must interpret the return according to the implementation they are building against; this header does not clarify whether the value is absolute time or a time delta (unknown).

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_get_expired
functions.description: Collects entries that have expired at or before the specified time and appends/returns them via the provided list. This function does not invoke callbacks; the application must subsequently run them (e.g., via h2o_timerwheel_run or by iterating the list and invoking callbacks according to implementation).
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context.
now is the current absolute time in the same time base used at creation/linking.

expired must be a valid pointer to a h2o_linklist_t to receive expired entries; it should be properly initialized for list operations before the call (exact initialization details depend on h2o_linklist_t usage).
Per the comment: After collecting, the application must call the routine that fires the timers; this header references h2o_timer_run (likely h2o_timerwheel_run) to execute callbacks.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_run
functions.description: Runs (fires) timers that have expired at or before the specified time, invoking their callbacks. Returns the number of timers run.
requirements: ctx must be a valid timerwheel context.
now is the current absolute time in the same time base used at creation/linking.
Callbacks (cb in h2o_timerwheel_entry_t) must be valid function pointers set during entry initialization.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_init_entry
functions.description: Initializes a timerwheel entry with a callback and clears linkage/expiration state. Expected usage: call once on a stack- or heap-allocated h2o_timerwheel_entry_t before linking it into a timerwheel.
requirements: entry must be a valid pointer to writable h2o_timerwheel_entry_t storage.
cb must be a valid function pointer of type h2o_timerwheel_cb (or NULL if the implementation allows; not specified here).
Must be called before h2o_timerwheel_link_abs is used with the entry.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_unlink
functions.description: Deactivates a timer by unlinking/removing a timerwheel entry from whichever list it is on, if currently linked. No-op if the entry is not linked.
requirements: entry must be a valid pointer to a h2o_timerwheel_entry_t.
Safe to call regardless of whether the entry is currently linked; the function checks linkage state.

functions.name: h2o_timerwheel_is_linked
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the timerwheel entry is currently active/linked into a list, zero otherwise.
requirements: entry must be a valid pointer to a h2o_timerwheel_entry_t.

functions.name: h2o_lookup_token
functions.description: Looks up a predefined HTTP header token by name and length and returns a pointer to a read-only h2o_token_t if found, or NULL if no matching token exists. Typically used to obtain canonical, interned representations of common header names for faster comparisons and HPACK/QPACK integration. The returned token, if non-NULL, refers to static storage and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: name must point to readable memory of at least len bytes.
len must specify the exact length of the token string to look up; the string does not need to be NUL-terminated because len is provided.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, refers to static, read-only storage and must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Callers must handle a NULL return value (meaning the token is not available).

functions.name: h2o_iovec_is_token
functions.description: Returns a non-zero value if the provided h2o_iovec_t refers to a predefined h2o_token_t (i.e., a fast, read-only tokenized iovec), otherwise returns 0. Useful for determining whether an iovec is a canonical token versus an arbitrary buffer.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized h2o_iovec_t.
The function does not take ownership of buf and does not modify it.
Callers should treat any non-zero return value as true and zero as false.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_authority
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the :authority header with the given value. Returns a table index and sets is_exact to indicate whether the match is an exact name+value match vs. a name-only or non-exact match. Typical usage: selecting the best static-table index when encoding :authority.
requirements: value must be a valid h2o_iovec_t that points to the header value bytes and length for :authority.
is_exact must point to writable storage for an int; behavior if NULL is unknown.
Return value semantics (range and not-found sentinel) are not documented in this header; consult implementation.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_method
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the :method header with the given value (e.g., GET, POST). Returns a table index and sets is_exact to indicate exact name+value match status. Used during QPACK encoding to reference static entries for :method.
requirements: value must contain the method token bytes (e.g., "GET") as an h2o_iovec_t for :method.
is_exact must be a valid non-null pointer to int; behavior if NULL is unknown.
Exact return semantics and not-found indicator are not specified here.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_path
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the :path header with the supplied value. Returns index and indicates if the match is exact via is_exact. Used to leverage common :path values from the static table.
requirements: value must be the :path value as bytes and length in h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must point to writable int storage; behavior if NULL is unknown.
Return value and not-found behavior are unspecified in this header.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_protocol
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the :protocol header field value. Returns a QPACK static table index and sets is_exact to indicate exactness.
requirements: value must hold the :protocol value in h2o_iovec_t form.
Provide a valid, writable is_exact pointer; NULL handling is unspecified.
Return value semantics and not-found behavior are not described here.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_scheme
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the :scheme header value (e.g., http, https). Sets is_exact based on whether the static table contains an exact name+value entry.
requirements: value must be the :scheme value in an h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must be a valid pointer to int; NULL permissibility unknown.
Not-found indicator and exact return range are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_status
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the :status pseudo-header with the given value (e.g., "200"). Returns index and indicates exactness via is_exact.
requirements: value must contain the numeric :status value as bytes (e.g., "200").
is_exact must reference writable int storage; NULL handling is unknown.
Not-found and error returns are not defined in this header.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_accept
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for the Accept header given a value. Sets is_exact when the value exactly matches a static table entry.
requirements: value must hold the Accept header value as h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must be a valid pointer to int; NULL handling unspecified.
Exact return semantics and not-found indicator are not described.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_accept_charset
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for the Accept-Charset header value. is_exact indicates exact name+value match.
requirements: value must be the Accept-Charset value in h2o_iovec_t.
Provide a writable is_exact pointer; NULL behavior unknown.
Return and not-found semantics are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_accept_encoding
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the Accept-Encoding header value (e.g., gzip, br). Indicates exactness via is_exact.
requirements: value must contain the Accept-Encoding value as h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must be a valid writable pointer; NULL handling unknown.
Not-found/return conventions are not documented here.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_accept_language
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table entry for the Accept-Language header value. is_exact reports exact name+value match.
requirements: value must be the Accept-Language value as h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must point to an int for output; behavior if NULL is unknown.
Return semantics and not-found indicator are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_accept_ranges
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for the Accept-Ranges header value (e.g., bytes). Sets is_exact for exact match.
requirements: value must hold Accept-Ranges value as bytes in h2o_iovec_t.
Valid, writable is_exact pointer required; NULL handling unknown.
Not-found/return value details are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_allow_credentials
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. is_exact indicates exact match.
requirements: value must be the header value for Access-Control-Allow-Credentials.
is_exact must be a valid pointer to int; NULL behavior unknown.
Return value semantics/not-found sentinel are not specified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_allow_headers
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for Access-Control-Allow-Headers with the supplied value. is_exact indicates exactness.
requirements: value must be the Access-Control-Allow-Headers value as h2o_iovec_t.
Provide writable is_exact pointer; NULL handling unknown.
Return semantics and not-found behavior are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_allow_methods
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for Access-Control-Allow-Methods given a value. Reports exactness via is_exact.
requirements: value must contain the Access-Control-Allow-Methods value.
is_exact must be a valid pointer; NULL handling unknown.
Not-found and return conventions are not documented.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_allow_origin
functions.description: Looks up the static table index for Access-Control-Allow-Origin. is_exact indicates whether an exact name+value pair was found.
requirements: value must be the Access-Control-Allow-Origin value as h2o_iovec_t.
Writable is_exact pointer is required; NULL permissibility unknown.
Return value semantics and not-found behavior are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_expose_headers
functions.description: Looks up the static table index for Access-Control-Expose-Headers with the given value. Indicates exactness.
requirements: value must hold the Access-Control-Expose-Headers value in h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must be a valid pointer to int; NULL handling unknown.
Not-found and return semantics are not specified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_request_headers
functions.description: Looks up the static table index for Access-Control-Request-Headers based on the provided value. is_exact indicates exact match status.
requirements: value must be the Access-Control-Request-Headers value in h2o_iovec_t form.
Provide a writable is_exact pointer; NULL behavior unknown.
Return semantics/not-found indicator are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_access_control_request_method
functions.description: Looks up the static table index for Access-Control-Request-Method for the given value. Sets is_exact for exactness.
requirements: value must contain the Access-Control-Request-Method value.
is_exact must be a valid pointer; behavior if NULL is unknown.
Return behavior for not-found is unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_age
functions.description: Looks up the QPACK static table index for the Age header with the given value. is_exact reports if the name+value pair is found exactly.
requirements: value must be the Age header value, as an h2o_iovec_t.
Writable is_exact pointer required; NULL handling unknown.
Not-found and return conventions are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_allow
functions.description: Looks up the static table index for the Allow header given a value. Indicates exactness via is_exact.
requirements: value must be the Allow header value bytes in h2o_iovec_t.
Provide valid is_exact pointer; NULL handling unknown.
Return semantics and not-found indicator are unspecified.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_alt_svc
functions.description: Looks up the static table entry index for the Alt-Svc header value. Sets is_exact accordingly.
requirements: value must be the Alt-Svc header value in h2o_iovec_t.
is_exact must point to an int for output; NULL permissibility unknown.
Return value semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: h2o_qpack_lookup_authorization
functions.description: Looks up the static table index for Authorization given a value. is_exact indicates whether the match is exact.
requirements: value must hold the Authorization header value in h2o_iovec_t.
Writable is_exact pointer required; behavior for NULL unknown.
